FILE source/bfcl/bfcl_eval/constants/default_prompts.py
    1 MAXIMUM_STEP_LIMIT = 20
    2 
    3 DEFAULT_SYSTEM_PROMPT_WITHOUT_FUNC_DOC = """You are an expert in composing functions. You are given a question and a set of possible functions. Based on the question, you will need to make one or more function/tool calls to achieve the purpose.
    4 If none of the functions can be used, point it out. If the given question lacks the parameters required by the function, also point it out.
    5 You should only return the function calls in your response.
    6 
    7 If you decide to invoke any of the function(s), you MUST put it in the format of [func_name1(params_name1=params_value1, params_name2=params_value2...), func_name2(params)]
    8 You SHOULD NOT include any other text in the response.
    9 
   10 At each turn, you should try your best to complete the tasks requested by the user within the current turn. Continue to output functions to call until you have fulfilled the user's request to the best of your ability. Once you have no more functions to call, the system will consider the current turn complete and proceed to the next turn or task.
   11 """
   12 
   13 DEFAULT_SYSTEM_PROMPT = (
   14     DEFAULT_SYSTEM_PROMPT_WITHOUT_FUNC_DOC
   15     + """
   16 Here is a list of functions in JSON format that you can invoke.\n{functions}\n
   17 """
   18 )
   19 
   20 DEFAULT_USER_PROMPT_FOR_ADDITIONAL_FUNCTION_FC = "I have updated some more functions you can choose from. What about now?"
   21 
   22 DEFAULT_USER_PROMPT_FOR_ADDITIONAL_FUNCTION_PROMPTING = "{functions}\n" + DEFAULT_USER_PROMPT_FOR_ADDITIONAL_FUNCTION_FC

    4 VLLM_PORT = 1053

    6 # Price got from Lambda Cloud, 23.92 per hour for 8x H100, on-demand pay as you go total price
    7 # Reference: https://lambda.ai/pricing
    8 H100_X8_PRICE_PER_HOUR = 23.92
    9 
   10 # Directory of the installed package
   11 PACKAGE_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
   12 
   13 # By default, results and other generated files are stored alongside the
   14 # package itself so that editable installs behave the same as a regular
   15 # installation. You can override this by setting the ``BFCL_PROJECT_ROOT``
   16 # environment variable.
   17 PROJECT_ROOT = Path(os.getenv("BFCL_PROJECT_ROOT", Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]))
   18 
   19 
   20 RESULT_PATH = PROJECT_ROOT / "result"
   21 SCORE_PATH = PROJECT_ROOT / "score"
   22 DOTENV_PATH = PROJECT_ROOT / ".env"
   23 TEST_IDS_TO_GENERATE_PATH = PROJECT_ROOT / "test_case_ids_to_generate.json"
   24 
   25 PROMPT_PATH = PACKAGE_ROOT / "data"
   26 MULTI_TURN_FUNC_DOC_PATH = PROMPT_PATH / "multi_turn_func_doc"
   27 POSSIBLE_ANSWER_PATH = PROMPT_PATH / "possible_answer"
   28 UTILS_PATH = PACKAGE_ROOT / "scripts"
   29 
   30 
   31 RED_FONT = "\033[91m"
   32 RESET = "\033[0m"
   33 
   34 RESULT_PATH.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   35 SCORE_PATH.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

   72 # -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
   73 # A mapping of model identifiers to their respective model configurations.
   74 # Each key corresponds to the model id passed to the `--model` argument
   75 # in both generation and evaluation commands.
   76 # Make sure to update the `supported_models.py` file as well when updating this map.
   77 # -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
   78 
   79 
   80 @dataclass
   81 class ModelConfig:
   82     """
   83     Model configuration class for storing model metadata and settings.
   84 
   85     Attributes:
   86         model_name (str): [Not Used] Name of the model as used in the API or on Hugging Face.
   87         display_name (str): Model name as it should appear on the leaderboard.
   88         url (str): Reference URL for the model or hosting service.
   89         org (str): Organization providing the model.
   90         license (str): License under which the model is released.
   91         model_handler (str): Handler name for invoking the model.
   92         input_price (Optional[float]): USD per million input tokens (None for open source models).
   93         output_price (Optional[float]): USD per million output tokens (None for open source models).
   94         is_fc_model (bool): True if this model is used in Function-Calling mode, otherwise False for Prompt-based mode.
   95         underscore_to_dot (bool): True if model does not support '.' in function names, in which case we will replace '.' with '_'. Currently this only matters for checker.  TODO: We should let the tool compilation step also take this into account.
   96 
   97     """
   98 
   99     model_name: str
  100     display_name: str
  101     url: str
  102     org: str
  103     license: str
  104 
  105     model_handler: str
  106 
  107     # Prices are in USD per million tokens; open source models have None
  108     input_price: Optional[float] = None
  109     output_price: Optional[float] = None
  110 
  111     # True if the model is in function-calling mode, False if in prompt mode
  112     is_fc_model: bool = True
  113 
  114     # True if this model does not allow '.' in function names
  115     underscore_to_dot: bool = False
  116 
  117

FILE source/bfcl/bfcl_eval/eval_checker/__init__.py

FILE source/bfcl/bfcl_eval/eval_checker/ast_eval/ast_checker.py
    1 from bfcl_eval.constants.model_config import MODEL_CONFIG_MAPPING
    2 from bfcl_eval.constants.type_mappings import (
    3     JAVA_TYPE_CONVERSION,
    4     JS_TYPE_CONVERSION,
    5 )
    6 from bfcl_eval.eval_checker.ast_eval.type_convertor.java_type_converter import java_type_converter
    7 from bfcl_eval.eval_checker.ast_eval.type_convertor.js_type_converter import js_type_converter
    8 import re
    9 
   10 #### Constants ####
   11 PYTHON_TYPE_MAPPING = {
   12     "string": str,
   13     "integer": int,
   14     "float": float,
   15     "boolean": bool,
   16     "array": list,
   17     "tuple": list,
   18     "dict": dict,
   19     "any": str,
   20 }
   21 
   22 # This is the list of types that we need to recursively check its values
   23 PYTHON_NESTED_TYPE_CHECK_LIST = ["array", "tuple"]
   24 
   25 
   26 NESTED_CONVERSION_TYPE_LIST = ["Array", "ArrayList", "array"]
   27 
   28 
   29 #### Main function ####
   30 def ast_checker(
   31     func_description, model_output, possible_answer, language, test_category, model_name
   32 ):
   33     if "parallel" in test_category:
   34         return parallel_function_checker_no_order(
   35             func_description, model_output, possible_answer, language, model_name
   36         )
   37         
   38     elif "multiple" in test_category:
   39         return multiple_function_checker(
   40             func_description, model_output, possible_answer, language, model_name
   41         )
   42         
   43     else:
   44         if len(model_output) != 1:
   45             return {
   46                 "valid": False,
   47                 "error": ["Wrong number of functions."],
   48                 "error_type": "simple_function_checker:wrong_count",
   49             }
   50 
   51         return simple_function_checker(
   52             func_description[0], model_output[0], possible_answer[0], language, model_name
   53         )
   54 
   55 
   56 #### Helper functions for AST ####
   57 def find_description(func_descriptions, name):
   58     if type(func_descriptions) == list:
   59         for func_description in func_descriptions:
   60             if func_description["name"] == name:
   61                 return func_description
   62         return None
   63     else:
   64         # it is a dict, there is only one function
   65         return func_descriptions
   66 
   67 
   68 def get_possible_answer_type(possible_answer: list):
   69     for answer in possible_answer:
   70         if answer != "":  # Optional parameter
   71             return type(answer)
   72     return None
   73 
   74 
   75 def convert_func_name(function_name, model_name: str):
   76     model_name_escaped = model_name.replace("_", "/")
   77     if "." in function_name:
   78         if MODEL_CONFIG_MAPPING[model_name_escaped].underscore_to_dot:
   79             # OAI does not support "." in the function name so we replace it with "_". ^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,64}$ is the regex for the name.
   80             # This happens for OpenAI, Mistral, and Google models
   81             return re.sub(r"\.", "_", function_name)
   82     return function_name
   83 
   84 
   85 def type_checker(
   86     param: str,
   87     value,
   88     possible_answer: list,
   89     expected_type_description: str,
   90     expected_type_converted,
   91     nested_type_converted,
   92 ):
   93     # NOTE: This type checker only supports nested type checking for one level deep.
   94     # We didn't implement recursive type checking for nested types, as it's not needed for the current use case and it's very complex.
   95 
   96     result = {
   97         "valid": True,
   98         "error": [],
   99         "is_variable": False,
  100         "error_type": "type_error:simple",
  101     }
  102 
  103     is_variable = False
  104     # check for the case where a variable is used instead of a actual value.
  105     # use the type in possible_answer as the expected type
  106     possible_answer_type = get_possible_answer_type(possible_answer)
  107     # if possible_answer only contains optional parameters, we can't determine the type
  108     if possible_answer_type != None:
  109         # we are being precise here.
  110         # in fact, possible_answer_type should always be string, as that's how we treat varibale in possible_answer
  111         if possible_answer_type != expected_type_converted:
  112             is_variable = True
  113 
  114     # value is the same type as in function description
  115     if type(value) == expected_type_converted:
  116         # We don't need to do recursive check for simple types
  117         if nested_type_converted == None:
  118             result["is_variable"] = is_variable
  119             return result
  120         else:
  121             for possible_answer_item in possible_answer:
  122                 flag = True  # Each parameter should match to at least one possible answer type.
  123                 # Here, we assume that each item should be the same type. We could also relax it.
  124                 if type(possible_answer_item) == list:
  125                     for value_item in value:
  126                         checker_result = type_checker(
  127                             param,
  128                             value_item,
  129                             possible_answer_item,
  130                             str(nested_type_converted),
  131                             nested_type_converted,
  132                             None,
  133                         )
  134                         if not checker_result["valid"]:
  135                             flag = False
  136                             break
  137 
  138                 if flag:
  139                     return {"valid": True, "error": [], "is_variable": is_variable}
  140 
  141             result["valid"] = False
  142             result["error"] = [
  143                 f"Nested type checking failed for parameter {repr(param)}. Expected outer type {expected_type_description} with inner type {str(nested_type_converted)}. Parameter value: {repr(value)}."
  144             ]
  145             result["error_type"] = "type_error:nested"
  146 
  147     # value is not as expected, check for the case where a variable is used instead of a actual value
  148     # use the type in possible_answer as the expected type
  149     possible_answer_type = get_possible_answer_type(possible_answer)
  150     # if possible_answer only contains optional parameters, we can't determine the type
  151     if possible_answer_type != None:
  152         # we are being precise here.
  153         # in fact, possible_answer_type should always be string, as that's how we treat varibale in possible_answer
  154         if type(value) == possible_answer_type:
  155             result["is_variable"] = True
  156             return result
  157 
  158     result["valid"] = False
  159     result["error"].append(
  160         f"Incorrect type for parameter {repr(param)}. Expected type {expected_type_description}, got {type(value).__name__}. Parameter value: {repr(value)}."
  161     )
  162     result["error_type"] = "type_error:simple"
  163     return result
  164 
  165 
  166 def standardize_string(input_string: str):
  167     # This function standardizes the string by removing all the spaces, ",./-_*^" punctuation, and converting it to lowercase
  168     # It will also convert all the single quotes to double quotes
  169     # This is used to compare the model output with the possible answers
  170     # We don't want to punish model for answer like April 1, 2024 vs April 1,2024, vs April 1 2024
  171     regex_string = r"[ \,\.\/\-\_\*\^]"
  172     return re.sub(regex_string, "", input_string).lower().replace("'", '"')
  173 
  174 
  175 def string_checker(param: str, model_output: str, possible_answer: list):
  176     standardize_possible_answer = []
  177     standardize_model_output = standardize_string(model_output)
  178     for i in range(len(possible_answer)):
  179         if type(possible_answer[i]) == str:
  180             standardize_possible_answer.append(standardize_string(possible_answer[i]))
  181 
  182     if standardize_model_output not in standardize_possible_answer:
  183         return {
  184             "valid": False,
  185             "error": [
  186                 f"Invalid value for parameter {repr(param)}: {repr(model_output)}. Expected one of {possible_answer}. Case insensitive."
  187             ],
  188             "error_type": "value_error:string",
  189         }
  190 
  191     return {"valid": True, "error": []}
  192 
  193 
  194 def list_checker(param: str, model_output: list, possible_answer: list):
  195     # Convert the tuple to a list
  196 
  197     standardize_model_output = list(model_output)
  198 
  199     # If the element in the list is a string, we need to standardize it
  200     for i in range(len(standardize_model_output)):
  201         if type(standardize_model_output[i]) == str:
  202             standardize_model_output[i] = standardize_string(model_output[i])
  203 
  204     standardize_possible_answer = []
  205     # We also need to standardize the possible answers
  206     for i in range(len(possible_answer)):
  207         standardize_possible_answer.append([])
  208         for j in range(len(possible_answer[i])):
  209             if type(possible_answer[i][j]) == str:
  210                 standardize_possible_answer[i].append(
  211                     standardize_string(possible_answer[i][j])
  212                 )
  213             else:
  214                 standardize_possible_answer[i].append(possible_answer[i][j])
  215 
  216     if standardize_model_output not in standardize_possible_answer:
  217         return {
  218             "valid": False,
  219             "error": [
  220                 f"Invalid value for parameter {repr(param)}: {repr(model_output)}. Expected one of {possible_answer}."
  221             ],
  222             "error_type": "value_error:list/tuple",
  223         }
  224 
  225     return {"valid": True, "error": []}
  226 
  227 
  228 def dict_checker(param: str, model_output: dict, possible_answers: list):
  229     # This function works for simple dictionaries, but not dictionaries with nested dictionaries.
  230     # The current dataset only contains simple dictionaries, so this is sufficient.
  231 
  232     result = {"valid": False, "error": [], "error_type": "dict_checker:unclear"}
  233     for i in range(len(possible_answers)):
  234 
  235         if possible_answers[i] == "":
  236             continue
  237 
  238         result = {"valid": False, "error": [], "error_type": "dict_checker:unclear"}
  239 
  240         flag = True
  241 
  242         possible_answer = possible_answers[i]
  243         # possible_anwer is a single dictionary
  244         
  245         for key, value in model_output.items():
  246             if key not in possible_answer:
  247                 result["valid"] = False
  248                 result["error"].append(f"Unexpected dict key parameter: '{key}'.")
  249                 result["error_type"] = "value_error:dict_key"
  250                 flag = False
  251                 break
  252 
  253             standardize_value = value
  254             # If the value is a string, we need to standardize it
  255             if type(value) == str:
  256                 standardize_value = standardize_string(value)
  257                 
  258             # We also need to standardize the possible answers if they are string
  259             standardize_possible_answer = []
  260             for i in range(len(possible_answer[key])):
  261                 if type(possible_answer[key][i]) == str:
  262                     standardize_possible_answer.append(
  263                         standardize_string(possible_answer[key][i])
  264                     )
  265                 else:
  266                     standardize_possible_answer.append(possible_answer[key][i])
  267 
  268             if standardize_value not in standardize_possible_answer:
  269                 result["valid"] = False
  270                 result["error"].append(
  271                     f"Invalid value for parameter {repr(key)}: {repr(value)}. Expected one of {standardize_possible_answer}."
  272                 )
  273                 result["error_type"] = "value_error:dict_value"
  274                 flag = False
  275                 break
  276         
  277         for key, value in possible_answer.items():
  278             if key not in model_output and "" not in value:
  279                 result["valid"] = False
  280                 result["error"].append(f"Missing dict key parameter: '{key}'.")
  281                 result["error_type"] = "value_error:dict_key"
  282                 flag = False
  283                 break
  284             
  285         if flag:
  286             return {"valid": True, "error": []}
  287 
  288     return result
  289 
  290 
  291 def list_dict_checker(param: str, model_output: list, possible_answers: list):
  292     # This function takes in a list of dictionaries and checks if each dictionary is valid
  293     # The order of the dictionaries in the list must match the order of the possible answers
  294 
  295     result = {"valid": False, "error": [], "error_type": "list_dict_checker:unclear"}
  296 
  297     for answer_index in range(len(possible_answers)):
  298         flag = True  # True means so far, all dictionaries are valid
  299 
  300         # Only proceed if the number of dictionaries in the list matches the number of dictionaries in the possible answers
  301         if len(model_output) != len(possible_answers[answer_index]):
  302             result["valid"] = False
  303             result["error"] = ["Wrong number of dictionaries in the list."]
  304             result["error_type"] = "value_error:list_dict_count"
  305             flag = False
  306             continue
  307 
  308         for dict_index in range(len(model_output)):
  309             result = dict_checker(
  310                 param,
  311                 model_output[dict_index],
  312                 [possible_answers[answer_index][dict_index]],
  313             )
  314             if not result["valid"]:
  315                 flag = False
  316                 break
  317         if flag:
  318             return {"valid": True, "error": []}
  319 
  320     return result
  321 
  322 
  323 def simple_function_checker(
  324     func_description: dict,
  325     model_output: dict,
  326     possible_answer: dict,
  327     language: str,
  328     model_name: str,
  329 ):
  330     possible_answer = list(possible_answer.values())[0]
  331     # Extract function name and parameters details
  332     func_name = func_description["name"]
  333     param_details = func_description["parameters"]["properties"]
  334     required_params = func_description["parameters"]["required"]
  335 
  336     # Initialize a result dictionary
  337     result = {
  338         "valid": True,
  339         "error": [],
  340         "error_type": "simple_function_checker:unclear",
  341     }
  342 
  343     func_name = convert_func_name(func_name, model_name)
  344 
  345     # Check if function name matches
  346     if func_name not in model_output:
  347         result["valid"] = False
  348         result["error"].append(
  349             f"Function name {repr(func_name)} not found in model output."
  350         )
  351         result["error_type"] = "simple_function_checker:wrong_func_name"
  352         return result
  353 
  354     model_params = model_output[func_name]
  355 
  356     # Check for required parameters in model output
  357     for param in required_params:
  358         if param not in model_params:
  359             result["valid"] = False
  360             result["error"].append(f"Missing required parameter: {repr(param)}.")
  361             result["error_type"] = "simple_function_checker:missing_required"
  362             return result
  363 
  364     # Validate types and values for each parameter in model output
  365     for param, value in model_params.items():
  366         if param not in param_details or param not in possible_answer:
  367             result["valid"] = False
  368             result["error"].append(f"Unexpected parameter: {repr(param)}.")
  369             result["error_type"] = "simple_function_checker:unexpected_param"
  370             return result
  371 
  372         full_param_details = param_details[param]
  373         expected_type_description = full_param_details["type"]  # This is a string
  374         is_variable = False
  375         nested_type_converted = None
  376 
  377         if language == "Java":
  378             expected_type_converted = JAVA_TYPE_CONVERSION[expected_type_description]
  379 
  380             if expected_type_description in JAVA_TYPE_CONVERSION:
  381                 if type(value) != str:
  382                     result["valid"] = False
  383                     result["error"].append(
  384                         f"Incorrect type for parameter {repr(param)}. Expected type String, got {type(value).__name__}. Parameter value: {repr(value)}."
  385                     )
  386                     result["error_type"] = "type_error:java"
  387                     return result
  388 
  389                 if expected_type_description in NESTED_CONVERSION_TYPE_LIST:
  390                     nested_type = param_details[param]["items"]["type"]
  391                     nested_type_converted = JAVA_TYPE_CONVERSION[nested_type]
  392                     value = java_type_converter(
  393                         value, expected_type_description, nested_type
  394                     )
  395                 else:
  396                     value = java_type_converter(value, expected_type_description)
  397 
  398         elif language == "JavaScript":
  399             expected_type_converted = JS_TYPE_CONVERSION[expected_type_description]
  400 
  401             if expected_type_description in JS_TYPE_CONVERSION:
  402                 if type(value) != str:
  403                     result["valid"] = False
  404                     result["error"].append(
  405                         f"Incorrect type for parameter {repr(param)}. Expected type String, got {type(value).__name__}. Parameter value: {repr(value)}."
  406                     )
  407                     result["error_type"] = "type_error:js"
  408                     return result
  409 
  410                 if expected_type_description in NESTED_CONVERSION_TYPE_LIST:
  411                     nested_type = param_details[param]["items"]["type"]
  412                     nested_type_converted = JS_TYPE_CONVERSION[nested_type]
  413                     value = js_type_converter(
  414                         value, expected_type_description, nested_type
  415                     )
  416                 else:
  417                     value = js_type_converter(value, expected_type_description)
  418 
  419         elif language == "Python":
  420             expected_type_converted = PYTHON_TYPE_MAPPING[expected_type_description]
  421             if expected_type_description in PYTHON_NESTED_TYPE_CHECK_LIST:
  422                 nested_type = param_details[param]["items"]["type"]
  423                 nested_type_converted = PYTHON_TYPE_MAPPING[nested_type]
  424 
  425         # We convert all tuple value to list when the expected type is tuple.
  426         # The conversion is necessary because any tuple in the possible answer would become a list after being processed through json.dump() and json.load().
  427         # This does introduce some false positive (eg, when the model provides a list value instead of tuple). We hope to find a better solution in the future.
  428         if expected_type_description == "tuple" and type(value) == tuple:
  429             value = list(value)
  430 
  431         # Allow python auto conversion from int to float
  432         if (
  433             language == "Python"
  434             and expected_type_description == "float"
  435             and type(value) == int
  436         ):
  437             value = float(value)
  438 
  439         # Type checking
  440         # In fact, we only check for Python here.
  441         # Type check for other languages are handled by the type converter, and so their value (after conversion) is always correct.
  442         type_check_result = type_checker(
  443             param,
  444             value,
  445             possible_answer[param],
  446             expected_type_description,
  447             expected_type_converted,
  448             nested_type_converted,
  449         )
  450         is_variable = type_check_result["is_variable"]
  451         if not type_check_result["valid"]:
  452             return type_check_result
  453 
  454         # It doesn't make sense to special handle dictionaries and list of dictionaries if the value is a variable.
  455         # We can just treat the variable as a string and use the normal flow.
  456         if not is_variable:
  457             # Special handle for dictionaries
  458             if expected_type_converted == dict:
  459                 result = dict_checker(param, value, possible_answer[param])
  460                 if not result["valid"]:
  461                     return result
  462                 continue
  463 
  464             # Special handle for list of dictionaries
  465             elif expected_type_converted == list and nested_type_converted == dict:
  466                 result = list_dict_checker(param, value, possible_answer[param])
  467                 if not result["valid"]:
  468                     return result
  469                 continue
  470 
  471             # Special handle for strings
  472             elif expected_type_converted == str:
  473                 # We don't check for case sensitivity for string, as long as it's not a variable
  474                 result = string_checker(param, value, possible_answer[param])
  475                 if not result["valid"]:
  476                     return result
  477                 continue
  478 
  479             elif expected_type_converted == list:
  480                 result = list_checker(param, value, possible_answer[param])
  481                 if not result["valid"]:
  482                     return result
  483                 continue
  484 
  485         # Check if the value is within the possible answers
  486         if value not in possible_answer[param]:
  487             result["valid"] = False
  488             result["error"].append(
  489                 f"Invalid value for parameter {repr(param)}: {repr(value)}. Expected one of {possible_answer[param]}."
  490             )
  491             result["error_type"] = "value_error:others"
  492             return result
  493 
  494     # Check for optional parameters not provided but allowed
  495     for param in possible_answer:
  496         if param not in model_params and "" not in possible_answer[param]:
  497             result["valid"] = False
  498             result["error"].append(
  499                 f"Optional parameter {repr(param)} not provided and not marked as optional."
  500             )
  501             result["error_type"] = "simple_function_checker:missing_optional"
  502             return result
  503 
  504     return result
  505 
  506 
  507 def parallel_function_checker_enforce_order(
  508     func_descriptions: list,
  509     model_output: list,
  510     possible_answers: dict,
  511     language: str,
  512     model_name: str,
  513 ):
  514     if len(model_output) != len(possible_answers):
  515         return {
  516             "valid": False,
  517             "error": ["Wrong number of functions."],
  518             "error_type": "parallel_function_checker_enforce_order:wrong_count",
  519         }
  520 
  521     func_name_list = list(possible_answers.keys())
  522     possible_answers_list = []
  523 
  524     for key, value in possible_answers.items():
  525         possible_answers_list.append({key: value})
  526 
  527     for i in range(len(possible_answers_list)):
  528         func_description = find_description(func_descriptions, func_name_list[i])
  529         
  530         result = simple_function_checker(
  531             func_description,
  532             model_output[i],
  533             possible_answers_list[i],
  534             language,
  535             model_name,
  536         )
  537         if not result["valid"]:
  538             return result
  539 
  540     return {"valid": True, "error": []}
  541 
  542 
  543 def parallel_function_checker_no_order(
  544     func_descriptions: list,
  545     model_output: list,
  546     possible_answers: list,
  547     language: str,
  548     model_name: str,
  549 ):
  550     if len(model_output) != len(possible_answers):
  551         return {
  552             "valid": False,
  553             "error": ["Wrong number of functions."],
  554             "error_type": "parallel_function_checker_no_order:wrong_count",
  555         }
  556 
  557     matched_indices = []
  558 
  559     # We go throught the possible answers one by one, and eliminate the model output that matches the possible answer
  560     # It must be this way because we need ground truth to fetch the correct function description
  561     for i in range(len(possible_answers)):
  562         # possible_answers[i] is a dictionary with only one key
  563         func_name_expected = list(possible_answers[i].keys())[0]
  564         func_description = find_description(func_descriptions, func_name_expected)
  565 
  566 
  567         all_errors = []
  568 
  569         for index in range(len(model_output)):
  570             if index in matched_indices:
  571                 continue
  572 
  573             result = simple_function_checker(
  574                 func_description,
  575                 model_output[index],
  576                 possible_answers[i],
  577                 language,
  578                 model_name,
  579             )
  580 
  581             if result["valid"]:
  582                 matched_indices.append(index)
  583                 break
  584             else:
  585                 all_errors.append(
  586                     {
  587                         f"Model Result Index {index}": {
  588                             "sub_error": result["error"],
  589                             "sub_error_type": result["error_type"],
  590                             "model_output_item": model_output[index],
  591                             "possible_answer_item": possible_answers[i],
  592                         }
  593                     }
  594                 )
  595 
  596         if not result["valid"]:
  597             considered_indices = [
  598                 i for i in range(len(model_output)) if i not in matched_indices
  599             ]
  600             all_errors.insert(
  601                 0,
  602                 f"Could not find a matching function among index {considered_indices} of model output for index {i} of possible answers.",
  603             )
  604             return {
  605                 "valid": False,
  606                 "error": all_errors,
  607                 "error_type": "parallel_function_checker_no_order:cannot_find_match",
  608             }
  609 
  610     return {"valid": True, "error": []}
  611 
  612 
  613 def multiple_function_checker(
  614     func_descriptions: list,
  615     model_output: list,
  616     possible_answers: list,
  617     language: str,
  618     model_name: str,
  619 ):
  620     if len(model_output) != len(possible_answers):
  621         return {
  622             "valid": False,
  623             "error": ["Wrong number of functions."],
  624             "error_type": "multiple_function_checker:wrong_count",
  625         }
  626 
  627     # possible_answers is a list of only one dictionary with only one key
  628     func_name_expected = list(possible_answers[0].keys())[0]
  629     func_description = find_description(func_descriptions, func_name_expected)
  630     return simple_function_checker(
  631         func_description,
  632         model_output[0],
  633         possible_answers[0],
  634         language,
  635         model_name,
  636     )

FILE source/bfcl/bfcl_eval/eval_checker/ast_eval/type_convertor/java_type_converter.py
    1 import re
    2 from typing import List, Dict, Union
    3 from bfcl_eval.constants.type_mappings import JAVA_TYPE_CONVERSION

    6 def java_type_converter(value, expected_type, nested_type=None):
    7     if expected_type not in JAVA_TYPE_CONVERSION:
    8         raise ValueError(f"Unsupported type: {expected_type}")
    9     if (
   10         expected_type == "byte"
   11         or expected_type == "short"
   12         or expected_type == "integer"
   13     ):
   14         if not re.match(r"^-?\d+$", value):
   15             return str(value)  # default to string
   16         return int(value)
   17     elif expected_type == "float":
   18         if not re.match(r"^-?\d+(\.\d+)?([eE][+-]?\d+)?[fF]$", value):
   19             return str(value)  # default to string
   20         return float(re.sub(r"[fF]$", "", value))
   21     elif expected_type == "double":
   22         if not re.match(r"^-?\d+(\.\d+)?([eE][+-]?\d+)?$", value):
   23             return str(value)  # default to string
   24         return float(value)
   25     elif expected_type == "long":
   26         if not re.match(r"^-?\d+[lL]$", value):
   27             return str(value)  # default to string
   28         return int(re.sub(r"[lL]$", "", value))
   29     elif expected_type == "boolean":
   30         if value not in ["true", "false"]:
   31             return str(value)  # default to string
   32         return parse_java_boolean(value)
   33     elif expected_type == "char":
   34         if not re.match(r"^\'.$\'", value):
   35             return str(value)  # default to string
   36         return value  # Remove the single quotes
   37     elif expected_type == "Array" or expected_type == "ArrayList":
   38         return parse_java_collection(value, expected_type, nested_type)
   39     elif expected_type == "Set":
   40         raise NotImplementedError("Set conversion is not implemented")
   41     elif expected_type == "HashMap":
   42         return parse_java_collection(value, expected_type, nested_type)
   43     elif expected_type == "Hashtable":
   44         raise NotImplementedError("Set conversion is not implemented")
   45     elif expected_type == "Queue" or expected_type == "Stack":
   46         raise NotImplementedError(f"{expected_type} conversion is not implemented")
   47     elif expected_type == "String" or expected_type == "any":
   48         return str(value)  # we output as string for `any` type
   49     else:
   50         raise ValueError(f"Unsupported type: {expected_type}")
   51 
   52 
   53 def parse_java_boolean(value):
   54     return value == "true"
   55 
   56 
   57 def parse_java_collection(
   58     input_str: str, type_str: str, nested_type=None
   59 ) -> Union[List, Dict]:
   60     if type_str == "ArrayList":
   61         return parse_arraylist(input_str, nested_type)
   62     elif type_str == "Array":
   63         return parse_array(input_str, nested_type)
   64     elif type_str == "HashMap":
   65         return parse_hashmap(input_str)
   66     else:
   67         raise ValueError(f"Unsupported type: {type_str}")
   68 
   69 
   70 def parse_arraylist(input_str: str, nested_type=None) -> List:
   71     match_asList = re.search(
   72         r"new\s+ArrayList<\w*>\(Arrays\.asList\((.+?)\)\)", input_str
   73     )
   74     if match_asList:
   75         elements_str = match_asList.group(1)
   76         elements = []
   77         for element_str in elements_str.split(","):
   78             element_str = element_str.strip()
   79             if nested_type == "char":
   80                 element = element_str[1:-1]  # Remove the single quotes
   81             elif nested_type == "String":
   82                 element = element_str[1:-1]  # Remove the double quotes
   83             else:
   84                 element = (
   85                     java_type_converter(element_str, nested_type)
   86                     if nested_type
   87                     else parse_java_value(element_str)
   88                 )
   89             elements.append(element)
   90         return elements
   91 
   92     match_add = re.search(
   93         r"new\s+ArrayList<\w*>\(\)\s*\{\{\s*(.+?)\s*\}\}", input_str, re.DOTALL
   94     )
   95     if match_add:
   96         adds_str = match_add.group(1)
   97         elements = []
   98         matches = re.findall(r"add\((.+?)\)", adds_str)
   99         for match in matches:
  100             value_str = match.strip()
  101             if nested_type == "char":
  102                 value = value_str[1:-1]  # Remove the single quotes
  103             elif nested_type == "String":
  104                 value = value_str[1:-1]  # Remove the double quotes
  105             else:
  106                 value = (
  107                     java_type_converter(value_str, nested_type)
  108                     if nested_type
  109                     else parse_java_value(value_str)
  110                 )
  111             elements.append(value)
  112         return elements
  113 
  114     match_empty = re.search(r"new\s+ArrayList<\w*>\(\)", input_str)
  115     if match_empty:
  116         return []  # Return an empty list for an empty ArrayList
  117 
  118     return input_str  # default to string
  119 
  120 
  121 def parse_array(input_str: str, nested_type=None) -> List:
  122     match = re.search(r"new\s+\w+\[\]\s*\{(.*?)\}", input_str)
  123     if match:
  124         elements_str = match.group(1)
  125         if nested_type:
  126             elements = [
  127                 java_type_converter(x.strip(), nested_type)
  128                 for x in elements_str.split(",")
  129                 if x.strip()
  130             ]
  131         else:
  132             elements = [
  133                 parse_java_value(x.strip())
  134                 for x in elements_str.split(",")
  135                 if x.strip()
  136             ]
  137 
  138         return elements
  139     else:
  140         return input_str  # default to string
  141 
  142 
  143 def parse_hashmap(input_str: str) -> Dict:
  144     elements = {}
  145     match = re.search(
  146         r"new\s+HashMap<.*?>\s*\(\)\s*\{\s*\{?\s*(.*?)\s*\}?\s*\}", input_str, re.DOTALL
  147     )
  148     if match:
  149         puts_str = match.group(1)
  150         if puts_str.strip():
  151             matches = re.findall(r"put\(\"(.*?)\",\s*(.*?)\)", puts_str)
  152             for match in matches:
  153                 key = match[0]
  154                 value = parse_java_value(match[1].strip())
  155                 elements[key] = value
  156         return elements
  157 
  158     match_empty = re.search(r"new\s+HashMap<.*?>\s*\(\)", input_str)
  159     if match_empty:
  160         return {}  # Return an empty dictionary for an empty HashMap
  161 
  162     return input_str  # default to string
  163 
  164 
  165 # This method parses without the information of what each element type is, contrary of the previous
  166 def parse_java_value(value_str: str):
  167     # check if it's boolean
  168     if value_str == "true":
  169         return True
  170     elif value_str == "false":
  171         return False
  172     # check if it's a string
  173     elif value_str.startswith('"') and value_str.endswith('"'):
  174         return value_str[1:-1]
  175     # check if it's a long
  176     elif re.match(r"^-?\d+[lL]$", value_str):
  177         return int(value_str[:-1])
  178     # check if it's a float
  179     elif re.match(r"^-?\d+(\.\d+)?([eE][+-]?\d+)?[fF]$", value_str):
  180         return float(re.sub(r"[fF]$", "", value_str))
  181     # check if it's a integer-like and float-like types (including byte, short, integer, double, etc)
  182     else:
  183         try:
  184             return int(value_str)
  185         except ValueError:
  186             try:
  187                 return float(value_str)
  188             except ValueError:
  189                 # this assuming all other types are converted to string
  190                 return value_str
  191 
  192 
  193 # Write tests for the `java_type_converter` function
  194 def test_java_type_converter():
  195     # Test valid conversions
  196     assert java_type_converter("true", "boolean") == True
  197     assert java_type_converter("false", "boolean") == False
  198     assert java_type_converter("123", "integer") == 123
  199     assert java_type_converter("-123", "integer") == -123
  200     assert java_type_converter("3.14f", "float") == 3.14
  201     assert java_type_converter("-3.14f", "float") == -3.14
  202     assert java_type_converter("3.14", "double") == 3.14
  203     assert java_type_converter("-3.14", "double") == -3.14
  204     assert java_type_converter("123L", "long") == 123
  205     assert java_type_converter("-123L", "long") == -123
  206     assert java_type_converter("a", "char") == "a"
  207     assert java_type_converter("abc", "String") == "abc"
  208     assert java_type_converter("new int[]{1, 2, 3}", "Array") == [1, 2, 3]
  209     assert java_type_converter(
  210         'new ArrayList<>(Arrays.asList("a", "b"))', "ArrayList"
  211     ) == ["a", "b"]
  212     assert java_type_converter(
  213         'new HashMap<String, String>() {{ put("key", "value"); }}', "HashMap"
  214     ) == {"key": "value"}
  215     assert java_type_converter("3f", "float") == 3.0
  216     assert java_type_converter("3e3F", "float") == 3e3
  217     assert java_type_converter("3e-3F", "float") == 3e-3
  218     assert java_type_converter("3.14e2", "double") == 3.14e2
  219     assert java_type_converter("3.14e-2", "double") == 3.14e-2
  220     assert java_type_converter("127", "byte") == 127
  221     assert java_type_converter("-128", "byte") == -128
  222     assert java_type_converter("32767", "short") == 32767
  223     assert java_type_converter("-32768", "short") == -32768
  224     assert java_type_converter("9223372036854775807L", "long") == 9223372036854775807
  225     assert java_type_converter("-9223372036854775808L", "long") == -9223372036854775808
  226     assert java_type_converter("123", "any") == "123"
  227     assert java_type_converter("abc", "any") == "abc"
  228 
  229     # Test empty collections
  230     assert java_type_converter("new int[]{}", "Array") == []
  231     assert java_type_converter("new ArrayList<>()", "ArrayList") == []
  232     assert java_type_converter("new HashMap<>()", "HashMap") == {}
  233 
  234     # Test collections with mixed types
  235     assert java_type_converter('new Object[]{1, "abc", true}', "Array") == [
  236         1,
  237         "abc",
  238         True,
  239     ]
  240     assert java_type_converter(
  241         'new ArrayList<>(Arrays.asList(1, "abc", true))', "ArrayList"
  242     ) == [1, "abc", True]
  243     assert java_type_converter(
  244         'new HashMap<String, Object>() {{ put("key1", 1); put("key2", "value"); put("key3", true); }}',
  245         "HashMap",
  246     ) == {"key1": 1, "key2": "value", "key3": True}
  247 
  248     # Test invalid values
  249     try:
  250         java_type_converter("true", "integer")
  251     except ValueError as e:

  321     assert java_type_converter("new int[] {1, 2, 3}", "Array") == [1, 2, 3]

  340         "HashMap",

  344         "HashMap",

FILE source/bfcl/bfcl_eval/eval_checker/ast_eval/type_convertor/js_type_converter.py
    1 import re
    2 from bfcl_eval.constants.type_mappings import JS_TYPE_CONVERSION
    3 
    4 
    5 def js_type_converter(value, expected_type, nested_type=None):
    6     if expected_type not in JS_TYPE_CONVERSION:
    7         raise ValueError(f"Unsupported type: {expected_type}")
    8 
    9     if expected_type == "String":
   10         if not (value.startswith('"') and value.endswith('"')) and not (
   11             value.startswith("'") and value.endswith("'")
   12         ):
   13             return str(value)
   14         return value[1:-1]
   15 
   16     elif expected_type == "integer":
   17         if not re.match(r"^-?\d+$", value):
   18             return str(value)  # default to string
   19         return int(value)
   20     elif expected_type == "float":
   21         if not re.match(r"^-?\d+(\.\d+)?$", value):
   22             return str(value)  # default to string
   23         return float(value)
   24     elif expected_type == "Bigint":
   25         if not re.match(r"^-?\d+n$", value):
   26             return str(value)  # default to string
   27         return int(value[:-1])
   28     elif expected_type == "Boolean":
   29         if value not in ["true", "false"]:
   30             return str(value)  # default to string
   31         return value == "true"
   32     elif expected_type == "dict":
   33         return parse_js_collection(value, "dict", nested_type)
   34     elif expected_type == "array":
   35         return parse_js_collection(value, "array", nested_type)
   36     elif expected_type == "any":
   37         return str(value)
   38     else:
   39         raise ValueError(f"Unsupported type: {expected_type}")
   40 
   41 
   42 def parse_js_collection(code, type_str, nested_type=None):
   43     code = code.strip()
   44     if type_str == "array":
   45         # Regular expression patterns
   46         array_2d_pattern = r"\[\s*\[.*?\]\s*(,\s*\[.*?\]\s*)*\]|\bnew\s+Array\(\s*\[.*?\]\s*(,\s*\[.*?\]\s*)*\)"
   47         array_pattern = r"\[(.*?)\]|\bnew\s+Array\((.*?)\)"
   48 
   49         # Check if the code is a 2D array
   50         array_2d_match = re.match(array_2d_pattern, code)
   51         try:
   52             if array_2d_match:
   53                 elements_str = array_2d_match.group(0)
   54                 inner_arrays = re.findall(r"\[(.*?)\]", elements_str)
   55                 elements = []
   56                 for idx, inner_array_str in enumerate(inner_arrays):
   57                     inner_array_str = inner_array_str.strip()
   58                     if idx == 0 and inner_array_str.startswith("["):
   59                         inner_array_str = inner_array_str[1:]
   60                     inner_array_elements = [
   61                         e.strip() for e in inner_array_str.split(",")
   62                     ]
   63                     if nested_type:
   64                         inner_array = [parse_js_value(e) for e in inner_array_elements]
   65                     else:
   66                         inner_array = [parse_js_value(e) for e in inner_array_elements]
   67                     elements.append(inner_array)
   68                 return elements
   69 
   70             # Check if the code is a 1D array
   71             array_match = re.match(array_pattern, code)
   72             if array_match:
   73                 if array_match.group(1) is not None:
   74                     elements_str = array_match.group(1).strip()
   75                     if elements_str:
   76                         elements = elements_str.split(",")
   77                     else:
   78                         elements = []
   79                 elif array_match.group(2) is not None:
   80                     elements_str = array_match.group(2).strip()
   81                     if elements_str:
   82                         elements = elements_str.split(",")
   83                     else:
   84                         elements = []
   85                 else:
   86                     elements = []
   87                 if nested_type:
   88                     elements = [
   89                         (
   90                             js_type_converter(e.strip(), nested_type, "String")
   91                             if (e.strip().startswith("'") or e.strip().startswith('"'))
   92                             else js_type_converter(e.strip(), nested_type)
   93                         )
   94                         for e in elements
   95                     ]
   96                 else:
   97                     elements = [parse_js_value(e.strip()) for e in elements]
   98                 return elements
   99             else:
  100                 return code
  101         except:
  102             return code
  103 
  104     elif type_str == "dict":
  105         if code == "{}":
  106             return {}  # Return an empty dictionary for an empty object
  107         dict_pattern = r"\{(.*?)\}"
  108         # Check if the code is a dictionary
  109         dict_match = re.match(dict_pattern, code)
  110         if dict_match:
  111             try:
  112                 content = dict_match.group(1)
  113                 pairs = re.findall(r"([^:]+):\s*(.*?)(?:,\s*(?=[^,]+:)|$)", content)
  114                 dictionary = {}
  115                 for key, value in pairs:
  116                     key = key.strip().strip("'\"")
  117                     value = value.strip()
  118                     if value.startswith("[") and value.endswith("]"):
  119                         # Handle array values
  120                         dictionary[key] = parse_js_collection(value, "array")
  121                     elif value.startswith("{") and value.endswith("}"):
  122                         # Handle nested dictionary values
  123                         dictionary[key] = parse_js_collection(value, "dict")
  124                     else:
  125                         dictionary[key] = parse_js_value(value.strip("'\""))
  126                 return dictionary
  127             except Exception as e:
  128                 print(f"Error parsing dictionary: {e}")
  129                 return code
  130         else:
  131             return code  # default to string
  132     else:
  133         raise ValueError(f"Unsupported type: {type_str}")
  134 
  135 
  136 def parse_js_value(value_str: str):
  137     value_str = value_str.strip()
  138     if value_str == "true":
  139         return True
  140     elif value_str == "false":
  141         return False
  142     elif (value_str.startswith('"') and value_str.endswith('"')) or (
  143         value_str.startswith("'") and value_str.endswith("'")
  144     ):
  145         return value_str[1:-1]
  146     else:
  147         try:
  148             return int(value_str)
  149         except ValueError:
  150             try:
  151                 return float(value_str)
  152             except ValueError:
  153                 return value_str
  154 
  155 
  156 # Write tests for the `js_type_converter` function
  157 def test_js_type_converter():
  158     assert js_type_converter("true", "Boolean") == True
  159     assert js_type_converter("false", "Boolean") == False
  160     assert js_type_converter("123", "integer") == 123
  161     assert js_type_converter("3.14", "float") == 3.14
  162     assert js_type_converter("123n", "Bigint") == 123
  163     assert js_type_converter("abc", "String") == "abc"
  164     assert js_type_converter("[1, 2, 3]", "array") == [1, 2, 3]
  165     assert js_type_converter("new Array(1, 2, 3)", "array") == [1, 2, 3]
  166     assert js_type_converter("{'key': 'value'}", "dict") == {"key": "value"}
  167     assert js_type_converter("{'key': 123}", "dict") == {"key": 123}
  168     assert js_type_converter("{'key': true}", "dict") == {"key": True}
  169 
  170     # Additional test cases
  171     # Test empty array and dictionary
  172     assert js_type_converter("[]", "array") == []
  173     assert js_type_converter("{}", "dict") == {}
  174 
  175     # Test array with mixed types
  176     assert js_type_converter("[1, 'two', true]", "array") == [1, "two", True]
  177 
  178     # Test dictionary with mixed types
  179     assert js_type_converter(
  180         "{'key1': 123, 'key2': 'value', 'key3': false}", "dict"
  181     ) == {"key1": 123, "key2": "value", "key3": False}
  182 
  183     # Test string with special characters
  184 
  185     # Test negative integer and float values
  186     assert js_type_converter("-123", "integer") == -123
  187     assert js_type_converter("-3.14", "float") == -3.14
  188 
  189     # Test invalid type
  190     try:
  191         js_type_converter("123", "InvalidType")
  192     except ValueError as e:
  193         assert str(e) == "Unsupported type: InvalidType"
  194 
  195     # Test invalid integer value
  196     try:
  197         js_type_converter("123.45", "integer")
  198     except ValueError as e:
  199         assert str(e) == "Invalid integer value: 123.45"
  200 
  201     # Test invalid float value
  202     try:
  203         js_type_converter("3.14abc", "float")
  204     except ValueError as e:
  205         assert str(e) == "Invalid float value: 3.14abc"
  206 
  207     # Test invalid Bigint value
  208     try:
  209         js_type_converter("123", "Bigint")
  210     except ValueError as e:
  211         assert str(e) == "Invalid Bigint value: 123"
  212 
  213     # Test invalid boolean value
  214     try:
  215         js_type_converter("not_a_boolean", "Boolean")
  216     except ValueError as e:
  217         assert str(e) == "Invalid boolean value: not_a_boolean"

  219     print("All tests passed successfully!")

  222 def test_js_type_converter_nested_array():
  223     # Test array with nested integers
  224     assert js_type_converter("[1, 2, 3]", "array", "integer") == [1, 2, 3]
  225     assert js_type_converter("new Array(4, 5, 6)", "array", "integer") == [4, 5, 6]
  226 
  227     # Test array with nested floats
  228     assert js_type_converter("[1.1, 2.2, 3.3]", "array", "float") == [1.1, 2.2, 3.3]
  229     assert js_type_converter("new Array(4.4, 5.5, 6.6)", "array", "float") == [
  230         4.4,
  231         5.5,
  232         6.6,
  233     ]
  234 
  235     # Test array with nested Bigints
  236     assert js_type_converter("[1n, 2n, 3n]", "array", "Bigint") == [1, 2, 3]
  237     assert js_type_converter("new Array(4n, 5n, 6n)", "array", "Bigint") == [4, 5, 6]
  238 
  239     # Test array with nested booleans
  240     assert js_type_converter("[true, false, true]", "array", "Boolean") == [
  241         True,
  242         False,
  243         True,
  244     ]
  245     assert js_type_converter("new Array(false, true, false)", "array", "Boolean") == [
  246         False,
  247         True,
  248         False,
  249     ]
  250 
  251     # Test array with nested strings
  252     print(js_type_converter('["hello", "world", "!"]', "array", "String"))
  253     assert js_type_converter('["hello", "world", "!"]', "array", "String") == [
  254         "hello",
  255         "world",
  256         "!",
  257     ]
  258     assert js_type_converter('new Array("foo", "bar", "baz")', "array", "String") == [
  259         "foo",
  260         "bar",
  261         "baz",
  262     ]
  263 
  264     # Test array with mixed nested types
  265     assert js_type_converter('[1, "two", true]', "array") == [1, "two", True]
  266     assert js_type_converter('new Array(3.14, "pi", false)', "array") == [
  267         3.14,
  268         "pi",
  269         False,
  270     ]
  271 
  272     # Test array with nested arrays
  273     print(js_type_converter(" [ [1, 2], [3, 4], [5, 6]]", "array", "array"))
  274     assert js_type_converter(" [ [ 1, 2 ], [ 3,   4], [5, 6]]", "array", "array") == [
  275         [1, 2],
  276         [3, 4],
  277         [5, 6],
  278     ]  # this example has many weird spacings
  279     assert js_type_converter("new Array([1, 2], [3, 4], [5, 6])", "array", "array") == [
  280         [1, 2],
  281         [3, 4],
  282         [5, 6],
  283     ]
  284 
  285     # Test array with nested dictionaries
  286     assert js_type_converter(
  287         '[{"key1": 1}, {"key2": 2}, {"key3": 3}]', "array", "dict"
  288     ) == [{"key1": 1}, {"key2": 2}, {"key3": 3}]
  289     assert js_type_converter(
  290         'new Array({"key1": 1}, {"key2": 2}, {"key3": 3})', "array", "dict"
  291     ) == [{"key1": 1}, {"key2": 2}, {"key3": 3}]
  292 
  293     print("All nested array tests passed successfully!")
