   28 
   29 def get_handler(model_name):
   30     config = MODEL_CONFIG_MAPPING[model_name]
   31     handler = config.model_handler(
   32         model_name, temperature=0
   33     )  # Temperature doesn't matter for evaluation
   34     handler.is_fc_model = config.is_fc_model
   35     return handler
   36 
   37 
   38 def multi_turn_runner(
   39     handler, model_result, prompt, possible_answer, model_name, test_category, score_dir
   40 ):
   41     assert (
   42         len(model_result) == len(prompt) == len(possible_answer)
   43     ), f"The length of the model result ({len(model_result)}) does not match the length of the prompt ({len(prompt)}) or possible answer ({len(possible_answer)}). Please check the input files for completeness."
   44 
   45     result = []
   46     correct_count = 0
   47     for i in range(len(model_result)):
   48         index: str = model_result[i]["id"]
   49         # Model result is stored as a list of list of model responses. Each inner list represents a turn.
   50         multi_turn_model_result_list: list[list] = model_result[i]["result"]
   51         multi_turn_ground_truth_list: list[list[str]] = possible_answer[i]["ground_truth"]
   52         test_entry: dict = prompt[i]
   53 
   54         # Remove the function doc from the score file for better readability; they are repeated and way too long
   55         if "function" in test_entry:
   56             del test_entry["function"]
   57 
   58         if type(multi_turn_model_result_list) != list:
   59             result.append(
   60                 {
   61                     "id": index,
   62                     "model_name": model_name,
   63                     "test_category": test_category,
   64                     "valid": False,
   65                     "error": {
   66                         "error_message": [
   67                             "Error during inference phase. Model did not output a list of model responses."
   68                         ],
   69                         "error_type": "multi_turn:inference_error",
   70                     },
   71                     "prompt": test_entry,
   72                     "model_result": multi_turn_model_result_list,
   73                     "possible_answer": multi_turn_ground_truth_list,
   74                 }
   75             )
   76         # Check if force-terminated during inference phase.
   77         # This happens when the model has retried too many times and still haven't figured out the answer.
   78         # When force-terminated, no further evaluation is needed. This whole entry will be failed.
   79         if len(multi_turn_model_result_list) != len(multi_turn_ground_truth_list):
   80             result.append(
   81                 {
   82                     "id": index,
   83                     "model_name": model_name,
   84                     "test_category": test_category,
   85                     "valid": False,
   86                     "error": {
   87                         "error_message": [
   88                             f"Model was force-terminated during inference phase. The length of the model result turns ({len(multi_turn_model_result_list)}) does not match the length of the ground truth turns ({len(multi_turn_ground_truth_list)})."
   89                         ],
   90                         "error_type": "multi_turn:force_terminated",
   91                     },
   92                     "prompt": test_entry,
   93                     "model_result": multi_turn_model_result_list,
   94                     "possible_answer": multi_turn_ground_truth_list,
   95                 }
   96             )
   97             continue
   98 
   99         multi_turn_model_result_list_decoded: list[list[list[str]]] = (
  100             []
  101         )  # decode_execute returns a list of strings
  102         # Try decoding the model results into executable function calls
  103         for single_turn_model_result_list in multi_turn_model_result_list:
  104             single_turn_model_result_list_decoded = []
  105             for model_result_item in single_turn_model_result_list:
  106                 # model_result_item is per step
  107                 try:
  108                     decoded_result: list[str] = handler.decode_execute(model_result_item)
  109                     if is_empty_execute_response(decoded_result):
  110                         # Empty output is not considered as a valid function call
  111                         continue
  112 
  113                     single_turn_model_result_list_decoded.append(decoded_result)
  114 
  115                 except Exception as e:
  116                     # Ignore any failed decoding and continue to the next message
  117                     # We only care about the decoded function call, not the error message or if the model is chatting
  118                     continue
  119             multi_turn_model_result_list_decoded.append(
  120                 single_turn_model_result_list_decoded
  121             )
  122 
  123         # Check if the model output the correct function calls
  124         accuracy_checker_result = multi_turn_checker(
  125             multi_turn_model_result_list_decoded,
  126             multi_turn_ground_truth_list,
  127             test_entry,
  128             test_category,
  129             model_name,
  130         )
  131 
  132         # Perform additional check for multi-turn irrelevance
  133         # This happens when the model is expected to not output any function calls in a certain turn due to miss parameters or miss functions
  134         # irrelevance_checker_result = multi_turn_irrelevance_checker(
  135         #     multi_turn_model_result_list_decoded,
  136         #     multi_turn_ground_truth_list,
  137         # )
  138 
  139         if not accuracy_checker_result["valid"]:
  140             temp = {}
  141             temp["id"] = index
  142             temp["model_name"] = model_name
  143             temp["test_category"] = test_category
  144             temp["valid"] = accuracy_checker_result.pop("valid")
  145             temp["error"] = accuracy_checker_result
  146             temp["prompt"] = test_entry
  147             temp["model_result_raw"] = multi_turn_model_result_list
  148             temp["model_result_decoded"] = multi_turn_model_result_list_decoded
  149             temp["possible_answer"] = multi_turn_ground_truth_list
  150             temp["inference_log"] = model_result[i].get("inference_log", "")
  151             result.append(temp)
  152         else:
  153             correct_count += 1
  154 
  155     accuracy = correct_count / len(model_result)
  156     result.insert(
  157         0,
  158         {
  159             "accuracy": accuracy,
  160             "correct_count": correct_count,
  161             "total_count": len(model_result),
  162         },
  163     )
  164     output_file_name = f"{VERSION_PREFIX}_{test_category}_score.json"
  165     output_file_dir = score_dir / model_name
  166     write_list_of_dicts_to_file(output_file_name, result, output_file_dir)
  167 
  168     return accuracy, len(model_result)
  169 
  170 
  171 def relevance_file_runner(
  172     handler, model_result, prompt, model_name, test_category, score_dir
  173 ):
  174     # This function serves for both relevance and irrelevance tests, which share the exact opposite logic.
  175     # If `test_category` is "irrelevance", the model is expected to output no function call.
  176     # No function call means either the AST decoding fails (a error message is generated) or the decoded AST does not contain any function call (such as a empty list, `[]`).
  177     # If `test_category` is "relevance", the model is expected to output to a function call, and empty list doesn't count as a function call.
  178     result = []
  179     correct_count = 0
  180     for i in range(len(model_result)):
  181         index: str = model_result[i]["id"]
  182         model_result_item = model_result[i]["result"]
  183         contain_func_call = False
  184         decoded_result = None
  185         decode_error = None
  186 
  187         try:
  188             decoded_result = handler.decode_ast(model_result_item, language="Python")
  189             # Decode successfully, which means the model output is in valid function call format
  190             contain_func_call = True
  191             if is_empty_output(decoded_result):
  192                 # Empty output is not considered as a valid function call
  193                 contain_func_call = False
  194 
  195         except Exception as e:
  196             # Decode failed, which means the model output is not in valid function call format
  197             contain_func_call = False
  198             decode_error = str(e)
  199 
  200         # irrelevance test means no function call outputted
  201         if "irrelevance" in test_category:
  202             success = not contain_func_call
  203         else:
  204             success = contain_func_call
  205 
  206         if success:
  207             correct_count += 1
  208         else:
  209             temp = {}
  210             temp["id"] = index
  211             temp["model_name"] = model_name
  212             temp["test_category"] = test_category
  213             temp["valid"] = success
  214             if "irrelevance" in test_category:
  215                 temp["error"] = [
  216                     f"Valid syntax. Successfully decode AST when it should not."
  217                 ]
  218                 temp["error_type"] = "irrelevance_error:decoder_success"
  219             else:
  220                 temp["error"] = [
  221                     f"Invalid syntax. Failed to decode AST when it should have. {decode_error}"
  222                 ]
  223                 temp["error_type"] = "relevance_error:decoder_failed"
  224             temp["prompt"] = prompt[i]
  225             temp["model_result"] = model_result_item
  226             temp["decoded_result"] = decoded_result
  227 
  228             result.append(temp)
  229 
  230     accuracy = correct_count / len(model_result)
  231     result.insert(
  232         0,
  233         {
  234             "accuracy": accuracy,
  235             "correct_count": correct_count,
  236             "total_count": len(model_result),
  237         },
  238     )
  239     output_file_name = f"{VERSION_PREFIX}_{test_category}_score.json"
  240     output_file_dir = score_dir / model_name
  241     write_list_of_dicts_to_file(output_file_name, result, output_file_dir)
  242 
  243     return accuracy, len(model_result)
  244 
  245 
  246 def ast_file_runner(
  247     handler,
  248     model_result,
  249     prompt,
  250     possible_answer,
  251     language,
  252     test_category,
  253     model_name,
  254     score_dir,
  255 ):
  256     assert (
  257         len(model_result) == len(prompt) == len(possible_answer)
  258     ), f"The length of the model result ({len(model_result)}) does not match the length of the prompt ({len(prompt)}) or possible answer ({len(possible_answer)}). Please check the input files for completeness."
  259 
  260     result = []
  261     correct_count = 0
  262     for i in range(len(model_result)):
  263         index: str = model_result[i]["id"]
  264         model_result_item = model_result[i]["result"]
  265         prompt_item = prompt[i]["function"]
  266         possible_answer_item = possible_answer[i]["ground_truth"]
  267 
  268         try:
  269             model_result_item_raw = model_result_item
  270             model_result_item = handler.decode_ast(model_result_item, language)
  271         except Exception as e:
  272             result.append(
  273                 {
  274                     "id": index,
  275                     "model_name": model_name,
  276                     "test_category": test_category,
  277                     "valid": False,
  278                     "error": [f"Invalid syntax. Failed to decode AST. {str(e)}"],
  279                     "error_type": "ast_decoder:decoder_failed",
  280                     "prompt": prompt[i],
  281                     "model_result_raw": model_result_item_raw,
  282                     "possible_answer": possible_answer_item,
  283                 }
  284             )
  285             continue
  286 
  287         decoder_output_valid = is_function_calling_format_output(model_result_item)
  288         if not decoder_output_valid:
  289             result.append(
  290                 {
  291                     "id": index,
  292                     "model_name": model_name,
  293                     "test_category": test_category,
  294                     "valid": False,
  295                     "error": [
  296                         "Did not output in the specified format. Note: the model_result is wrapped in a string to ensure json serializability."
  297                     ],
  298                     "error_type": "ast_decoder:decoder_wrong_output_format",
  299                     "prompt": prompt[i],
  300                     "model_result_raw": str(model_result_item_raw),
  301                     "model_result_decoded": str(model_result_item),
  302                     "possible_answer": possible_answer_item,
  303                 }
  304             )
  305             continue
  306 
  307         checker_result = ast_checker(
  308             prompt_item,
  309             model_result_item,
  310             possible_answer_item,
  311             language,
  312             test_category,
  313             model_name,
  314         )
  315 
  316         if checker_result["valid"]:
  317             correct_count += 1
  318         else:
  319             temp = {}
  320             temp["id"] = index
  321             temp["model_name"] = model_name
  322             temp["test_category"] = test_category
  323             temp["valid"] = checker_result["valid"]
  324             temp["error"] = checker_result["error"]
  325             temp["error_type"] = checker_result["error_type"]
  326             temp["prompt"] = prompt[i]
  327             temp["model_result_raw"] = model_result_item_raw
  328             temp["model_result_decoded"] = model_result_item
  329             temp["possible_answer"] = possible_answer_item
  330             result.append(temp)
  331 
  332     accuracy = correct_count / len(model_result)
  333     result.insert(
  334         0,
  335         {
  336             "accuracy": accuracy,
  337             "correct_count": correct_count,
  338             "total_count": len(model_result),
  339         },
  340     )
  341     output_file_name = f"{VERSION_PREFIX}_{test_category}_score.json"
  342     output_file_dir = score_dir / model_name
  343     write_list_of_dicts_to_file(output_file_name, result, output_file_dir)
  344 
  345     return accuracy, len(model_result)
  346 
  347 
  348 #### Main runner function ####
  349 def runner(model_names, test_categories, result_dir, score_dir):
  350 
  351     # State udpated by each eval subtask.
  352     state = dict(
  353         # A dictionary to store the evaluation scores.
  354         # Key is model name, value is a dictionary with keys as test category
  355         # and values as a dictionary with accuracy and total count.
  356         leaderboard_table={},
  357     )
  358 
  359     # Get a list of all entries in the folder
  360     entries = result_dir.iterdir()
  361 
  362     # Filter out the subdirectories
  363     subdirs = [entry for entry in entries if entry.is_dir()]
  364 
  365     # Traverse each subdirectory
  366     for subdir in tqdm(subdirs, desc="Number of models evaluated"):
  367 
  368         model_name = subdir.relative_to(result_dir).name
  369         if model_names is not None and model_name not in model_names:
  370             continue
  371 
  372         model_name_escaped = model_name.replace("_", "/")
  373 
  374         print(f"🦍 Model: {model_name}")
  375 
  376         # Find and process all JSON files in the subdirectory
  377         for model_result_json in subdir.glob("*.json"):
  378             test_category = extract_test_category(model_result_json)
  379             if test_category not in test_categories:
  380                 continue
  381 
  382             handler = get_handler(model_name_escaped)
  383 
  384             # We don't evaluate the following categories in the current iteration of the benchmark
  385             if is_chatable(test_category) or is_sql(test_category) or is_executable(test_category):
  386                 continue
  387 
  388             model_result = load_file(model_result_json, sort_by_id=True)
  389 
  390             state = evaluate_task(
  391                 test_category,
  392                 result_dir,
  393                 score_dir,
  394                 model_result,
  395                 model_name,
  396                 handler,
  397                 state,
  398             )
  399 
  400     # This function reads all the score files from local folder and updates the
  401     # leaderboard table. This is helpful when you only want to run the
  402     # evaluation for a subset of models and test categories.
  403     update_leaderboard_table_with_local_score_file(state["leaderboard_table"], score_dir)
  404     # Write the leaderboard table to a file
  405     generate_leaderboard_csv(
  406         state["leaderboard_table"], score_dir, model_names, test_categories
  407     )
  408 
  409 
  410 def evaluate_task(
  411     test_category,
  412     result_dir,
  413     score_dir,
  414     model_result,
  415     model_name,
  416     handler,
  417     state,
  418 ):
  419 
  420     language = "Python"
  421     if is_java(test_category):
  422         language = "Java"
  423     if is_js(test_category):
  424         language = "JavaScript"
  425 
  426     print(f"🔍 Running test: {test_category}")
  427 
  428     record_cost_latency(state["leaderboard_table"], model_name, model_result)
  429 
  430     # Find the corresponding test file.
  431     prompt_file = find_file_with_suffix(PROMPT_PATH, test_category)
  432     prompt = load_file(prompt_file, sort_by_id=True)
  433 
  434     if is_relevance_or_irrelevance(test_category):
  435         accuracy, total_count = relevance_file_runner(
  436             handler, model_result, prompt, model_name, test_category, score_dir
  437         )
  438 
  439     else:
  440         # Find the corresponding possible answer file
  441         possible_answer_file = find_file_with_suffix(POSSIBLE_ANSWER_PATH, test_category)
  442         possible_answer = load_file(possible_answer_file, sort_by_id=True)
  443 
  444         if is_multi_turn(test_category):
  445             accuracy, total_count = multi_turn_runner(
  446                 handler,
  447                 model_result,
  448                 prompt,
  449                 possible_answer,
  450                 model_name,
  451                 test_category,
  452                 score_dir,
  453             )
  454 
  455         # Single turn test
  456         else:
  457             accuracy, total_count = ast_file_runner(
  458                 handler,
  459                 model_result,
  460                 prompt,
  461                 possible_answer,
  462                 language,
  463                 test_category,
  464                 model_name,
  465                 score_dir,
  466             )
  467 
  468     record_result(state["leaderboard_table"], model_name, test_category, accuracy, total_count)
  469     print(f"✅ Test completed: {test_category}. 🎯 Accuracy: {accuracy}")
  470 
  471     return state
  472 
  473 
  474 def main(model, test_categories, result_dir, score_dir):
  475     if result_dir is None:
  476         result_dir = RESULT_PATH
  477     else:
  478         result_dir = (PROJECT_ROOT / result_dir).resolve()
  479 
  480     if score_dir is None:
  481         score_dir = SCORE_PATH
  482     else:
  483         score_dir = (PROJECT_ROOT / score_dir).resolve()
  484 
  485     if type(test_categories) is not list:
  486         test_categories = [test_categories]
  487 
  488     _, all_test_categories = parse_test_category_argument(test_categories)
  489 
  490     model_names = None
  491     if model:
  492         model_names = []
  493         for model_name in model:
  494             if model_name not in MODEL_CONFIG_MAPPING:
  495                 raise ValueError(f"Invalid model name '{model_name}'.")
  496             # Runner takes in the model name that contains "_", instead of "/", for the sake of file path issues.
  497             # This is differnet than the model name format that the generation script "openfunctions_evaluation.py" takes in (where the name contains "/").
  498             # We patch it here to avoid confusing the user.
  499             model_names.append(model_name.replace("/", "_"))
  500 
  501     # Driver function to run the evaluation for all categories involved.
  502     runner(model_names, all_test_categories, result_dir, score_dir)
  503 
  504     print(
  505         f"🏁 Evaluation completed. See {score_dir / 'data_overall.csv'} for overall evaluation results on BFCL V3."
  506     )
  507     print(
  508         f"See {score_dir / 'data_live.csv'}, {score_dir / 'data_non_live.csv'} and {score_dir / 'data_multi_turn.csv'} for detailed evaluation results on each sub-section categories respectively."
  509     )
  510 
  511 
  512 if __name__ == "__main__":
  513     parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Process two lists of strings.")
  514 
  515     # Add arguments for two lists of strings
  516     parser.add_argument(
  517         "--model", nargs="+", type=str, help="A list of model names to evaluate"
  518     )
  519     parser.add_argument(
  520         "--test-category",
  521         nargs="+",
  522         type=str,
  523         default="all",
  524         help="A list of test categories to run the evaluation on",
  525     )
  526     parser.add_argument(
  527         "--result-dir",
  528         default=None,
  529         type=str,
  530         help="Path to the folder where the model response files are stored; relative to the `berkeley-function-call-leaderboard` root folder",
  531     )
  532     parser.add_argument(
  533         "--score-dir",
  534         default=None,
  535         type=str,
  536         help="Path to the folder where the evaluation score files will be stored; relative to the `berkeley-function-call-leaderboard` root folder",
  537     )
  538 
  539     args = parser.parse_args()
  540 
  541     load_dotenv(dotenv_path=DOTENV_PATH, verbose=True, override=True)  # Load the .env file
  542     main(
  543         args.model,
  544         args.test_category,
  545         args.result_dir,
  546         args.score_dir,
  547     )

   15 def calculate_weighted_accuracy(accuracy_dict_list, display_na_if_category_missing=True):
   16     has_na = False
   17     total_count = 0
   18     total_accuracy = 0
   19     for accuracy_dict in accuracy_dict_list:
   20         accuracy = accuracy_dict["accuracy"]
   21         count = accuracy_dict["total_count"]
   22         if accuracy_dict["display_accuracy"] == "N/A":
   23             has_na = True
   24 
   25         total_count += count
   26         total_accuracy += accuracy * count
   27 
   28     result = {"accuracy": total_accuracy / total_count, "total_count": total_count}
   29 
   30     if has_na and display_na_if_category_missing:
   31         result["display_accuracy"] = "N/A"
   32     else:
   33         result["display_accuracy"] = result["accuracy"]
   34 
   35     return result
   36 
   37 
   38 def calculate_unweighted_accuracy(accuracy_dict_list, display_na_if_category_missing=True):
   39     has_na = False
   40     total_count = 0
   41     total_accuracy = 0
   42     for accuracy_dict in accuracy_dict_list:
   43         accuracy = accuracy_dict["accuracy"]
   44         count = accuracy_dict["total_count"]
   45         if accuracy_dict["display_accuracy"] == "N/A":
   46             # If a category is not being evaluated, it will still be considered 0 in the overall score calculation.
   47             has_na = True
   48 
   49         total_count += count
   50         total_accuracy += accuracy
   51 
   52     result = {
   53         "accuracy": total_accuracy / len(accuracy_dict_list),
   54         "total_count": total_count,
   55     }
   56 
   57     if has_na and display_na_if_category_missing:
   58         result["display_accuracy"] = "N/A"
   59     else:
   60         result["display_accuracy"] = result["accuracy"]
   61 
   62     return result

   65 def record_result(leaderboard_table, model_name, test_category, accuracy, total_count):
   66     if model_name not in leaderboard_table:
   67         leaderboard_table[model_name] = {}
   68     leaderboard_table[model_name][test_category] = {
   69         "accuracy": accuracy,
   70         "total_count": total_count,
   71     }
   72 
   73 
   74 def record_cost_latency(leaderboard_table, model_name, model_output_data):
   75     def process_data(key, data, output_list):
   76         # All entries are either a list of list (in multi-turn), or a single value (in single-turn)
   77         if key in data:
   78             if isinstance(data[key], list) and all(
   79                 isinstance(inner_item, list) for inner_item in data[key]
   80             ):
   81                 flattened_list = sum(data[key], [])
   82                 output_list.extend(
   83                     [
   84                         item
   85                         for item in flattened_list
   86                         if isinstance(item, (int, float)) and item != 0
   87                     ]
   88                 )
   89             else:
   90                 if isinstance(data[key], (int, float)) and data[key] != 0:
   91                     output_list.append(data[key])
   92 
   93     if model_name not in leaderboard_table:
   94         leaderboard_table[model_name] = {}
   95         leaderboard_table[model_name]["cost"] = {"input_data": [], "output_data": []}
   96         leaderboard_table[model_name]["latency"] = {"data": []}
   97 
   98     input_token = []
   99     output_token = []
  100     latency = []
  101     for data in model_output_data:
  102         process_data("latency", data, latency)
  103         process_data("input_token_count", data, input_token)
  104         process_data("output_token_count", data, output_token)
  105 
  106     leaderboard_table[model_name]["cost"]["input_data"].extend(input_token)
  107     leaderboard_table[model_name]["cost"]["output_data"].extend(output_token)
  108     leaderboard_table[model_name]["latency"]["data"].extend(latency)
  109 
  110 
  111 def get_cost_latency_info(model_name, cost_data, latency_data):
  112     cost, mean_latency, std_latency, percentile_95_latency = "N/A", "N/A", "N/A", "N/A"
  113     model_config = MODEL_CONFIG_MAPPING[model_name]
  114 
  115     # For API models, we use the input and output token counts to calculate the cost
  116     if model_config.input_price is not None and model_config.output_price is not None:
  117         if len(cost_data["input_data"]) > 0 and len(cost_data["output_data"]) > 0:
  118             total_input_tokens = sum(cost_data["input_data"])
  119             total_output_tokens = sum(cost_data["output_data"])
  120             # price is in USD per million tokens
  121             cost = (
  122                 total_input_tokens * model_config.input_price / 1000000
  123                 + total_output_tokens * model_config.output_price / 1000000
  124             )
  125             cost = round(cost, 2)
  126 
  127     # For local-hosted models, we calculate the total GPU cost by summing all latencies and multiplying by the hourly GPU price.
  128     elif len(latency_data["data"]) > 0:
  129         total_latency_seconds = sum(latency_data["data"])
  130         total_latency_hours = total_latency_seconds / 3600
  131 
  132         # Divide by 100 since we are doing 100x parallel inference; this is an approximation to the GPU up-time.
  133         cost = total_latency_hours * H100_X8_PRICE_PER_HOUR / 100
  134         cost = round(cost, 2)
  135 
  136     # Calculate latency statistics for ALL models (both API and local)
  137     if len(latency_data["data"]) != 0:
  138         mean_latency = statistics.mean(latency_data["data"])
  139         std_latency = statistics.stdev(latency_data["data"])
  140         percentile_95_latency = np.percentile(latency_data["data"], 95)
  141         mean_latency = round(mean_latency, 2)
  142         std_latency = round(std_latency, 2)
  143         percentile_95_latency = round(percentile_95_latency, 2)
  144 
  145     return cost, mean_latency, std_latency, percentile_95_latency
  146 
  147 
  148 def get_category_score(score_dict: dict, test_category: str) -> dict:
  149     if test_category in score_dict:
  150         score = score_dict[test_category]
  151         score["display_accuracy"] = score["accuracy"]
  152         return score
  153     else:
  154         test_file_path = TEST_FILE_MAPPING[test_category]
  155         num_entry = len(load_file(PROMPT_PATH / test_file_path))
  156         # If a category is not being evaluated, it needs to be distinguished from the situation where the evaluation score is 0
  157         # It will still be considered 0 in the overall score calculation though
  158         # We use `display_accuracy` to special handle
  159         return {"accuracy": 0, "total_count": num_entry, "display_accuracy": "N/A"}
  160 
  161 
  162 def write_score_csv_file(
  163     data,
  164     file_path: str,
  165     header: list,
  166     sort_column_index: int,
  167     no_conversion_numeric_column_index: list[int] = [],
  168 ) -> None:
  169     data.sort(key=lambda x: x[sort_column_index], reverse=True)
  170     for i in range(len(data)):
  171         # Add the ranking column, start from 0
  172         data[i][0] = str(i + 1)
  173         for j in range(1, len(data[i])):
  174             if type(data[i][j]) == str:
  175                 continue
  176             # Some columns such as Latency and Cost, should not be presented in the percentage format
  177             elif j in no_conversion_numeric_column_index:
  178                 data[i][j] = str(data[i][j])
  179             else:
  180                 # Convert numeric value to percentage format
  181                 data[i][j] = "{:.2f}%".format(data[i][j] * 100)
  182 
  183     data.insert(0, header)
  184 
  185     with open(file_path, "w") as f:
  186         for i, row in enumerate(data):
  187             if i < len(data) - 1:
  188                 f.write(",".join(row) + "\n")
  189             else:
  190                 f.write(",".join(row))
  191

  487 def update_leaderboard_table_with_local_score_file(
  488     leaderboard_table, score_path: Path
  489 ) -> None:
  490 
  491     entries = score_path.iterdir()
  492 
  493     # Filter out the subdirectories
  494     subdirs = [entry for entry in entries if entry.is_dir()]
  495 
  496     # Traverse each subdirectory
  497     for subdir in subdirs:
  498         model_name = subdir.relative_to(score_path).name
  499         # Find and process all JSON files in the subdirectory
  500         for model_score_json in subdir.glob("*.json"):
  501             metadata = load_file(model_score_json)[0]
  502             accuracy, total_count = metadata["accuracy"], metadata["total_count"]
  503             test_category = extract_test_category(model_score_json)
  504             if model_name not in leaderboard_table:
  505                 leaderboard_table[model_name] = {}
  506             if test_category not in leaderboard_table[model_name]:
  507                 leaderboard_table[model_name][test_category] = {
  508                     "accuracy": accuracy,
  509                     "total_count": total_count,
  510                 }

FILE source/bfcl/bfcl_eval/eval_checker/multi_turn_eval/__init__.py

FILE source/bfcl/bfcl_eval/eval_checker/multi_turn_eval/multi_turn_checker.py
    1 from bfcl_eval.eval_checker.multi_turn_eval.multi_turn_utils import (
    2     execute_multi_turn_func_call,
    3     is_empty_execute_response,
    4 )

    8 
    9 def multi_turn_checker(
   10     multi_turn_model_result_list_decoded: list[list[list[str]]],
   11     multi_turn_ground_truth_list: list[list[str]],
   12     test_entry: dict,
   13     test_category: str,
   14     model_name: str,
   15 ) -> dict:
   16     """
   17     The main function that checks the correctness of the model's function call execution.
   18     """
   19 
   20     initial_config: dict = test_entry["initial_config"]
   21     involved_classes: list = test_entry["involved_classes"]
   22     test_entry_id: str = test_entry["id"]
   23     test_category: str = test_entry_id.rsplit("_", 1)[0]
   24     execution_results: list[dict] = []
   25     all_turn_model_execution_results: list[str] = []
   26 
   27     # First execute all the function calls
   28     for turn_index, single_turn_ground_truth_list in enumerate(
   29         multi_turn_ground_truth_list
   30     ):
   31         single_turn_model_response_list = multi_turn_model_result_list_decoded[turn_index]
   32 
   33         # Note that we combine all the sub-step results into a single list, for easier comparison
   34         single_turn_model_execution_results = []
   35         single_turn_model_execution_results_uncombined = []
   36         single_turn_ground_truth_execution_results = []
   37         model_instances = {}  # Will be overwritten in the for loop
   38         single_step_model_execution_results = []  # Will be overwritten in the for loop
   39     
   40         for single_step_model_response in single_turn_model_response_list:
   41             single_step_model_execution_results, model_instances = (
   42                 execute_multi_turn_func_call(
   43                     func_call_list=single_step_model_response,
   44                     initial_config=initial_config,
   45                     involved_classes=involved_classes,
   46                     model_name=model_name,
   47                     test_entry_id=test_entry_id,
   48                     long_context=(
   49                         "long_context" in test_category or "composite" in test_category
   50                     ),
   51                     is_evaL_run=True,
   52                 )
   53             )
   54             single_turn_model_execution_results.extend(single_step_model_execution_results)
   55             single_turn_model_execution_results_uncombined.append(single_step_model_execution_results)
   56 
   57         # Execute the ground truth function calls
   58         single_turn_ground_truth_execution_results, ground_truth_instances = (
   59             execute_multi_turn_func_call(
   60                 func_call_list=single_turn_ground_truth_list,
   61                 initial_config=initial_config,
   62                 involved_classes=involved_classes,
   63                 model_name=model_name + "_ground_truth",
   64                 test_entry_id=test_entry_id,
   65                 long_context=(
   66                     "long_context" in test_category or "composite" in test_category
   67                 ),
   68                 is_evaL_run=True,
   69             )
   70         )
   71 
   72         all_turn_model_execution_results.extend(single_turn_model_execution_results)
   73         execution_results.append(
   74             {
   75                 "model": single_turn_model_execution_results_uncombined,
   76                 "ground_truth": single_turn_ground_truth_execution_results,
   77             }
   78         )
   79 
   80         # If the ground truth list is not empty, then the model response list should not be empty
   81         if len(single_turn_ground_truth_list) > 0:
   82             if not single_turn_model_response_list or is_empty_execute_response(
   83                 single_turn_model_response_list
   84             ):
   85                 return {
   86                     "valid": False,
   87                     "error_message": f"Model response list is empty for turn {turn_index}",
   88                     "error_type": "multi_turn:empty_turn_model_response",
   89                     "details": {
   90                         "execution_result": execution_results,
   91                     },
   92                 }
   93 
   94         # If the ground truth list is empty, this is the turn where the model should eventually fail to achieve the user request.
   95         # The actual check for irrelevance is done in the multi_turn_irrelevance_checker function
   96         # Note: If the model outputs any function call in this turn, we will still execute it so that the state check at the next turn is accurate.
   97         if not single_turn_ground_truth_list:
   98             continue
   99 
  100         ## Check after each turn ##
  101         assert len(model_instances) == len(
  102             ground_truth_instances
  103         ), f"Model instances and ground truth instances do not match in length for turn {turn_index}. Model instances: {len(model_instances)}, Ground truth instances: {len(ground_truth_instances)}"
  104         assert set(model_instances.keys()) == set(ground_truth_instances.keys())
  105 
  106         # Check the state of the instances
  107         state_check_result = state_checker(model_instances, ground_truth_instances)
  108         if not state_check_result["valid"]:
  109             state_check_result["execution_result"] = execution_results
  110             return state_check_result
  111 
  112         # Check the response of the function calls
  113         # We use the all_turn_model_execution_results to accomodate the situation where the model invokes a function in a previous turn, and thus don't need to invoke it again in the current turn.
  114         response_check_result = response_checker(
  115             all_turn_model_execution_results,
  116             single_turn_ground_truth_execution_results,
  117             turn_index,
  118         )
  119         if not response_check_result["valid"]:
  120             return response_check_result
  121 
  122         # # Check the method invoke order
  123         # method_invoke_order_check_result = method_invoke_order_checker(
  124         #     model_instances, ground_truth_instances
  125         # )
  126         # if not method_invoke_order_check_result["valid"]:
  127         #     return method_invoke_order_check_result
  128 
  129     return {"valid": True}
  130 
  131 
  132 def multi_turn_irrelevance_checker(
  133     multi_turn_model_result_list_decoded: list[list[list[str]]],
  134     multi_turn_ground_truth_list: list[list[str]],
  135 ) -> dict:
  136     """
  137     Check if the model's output are irrelevant when it should be.
  138     It should be empty when the ground truth is a empty list for that turn.
  139     """
  140     for turn_index, single_turn_ground_truth_list in enumerate(
  141         multi_turn_ground_truth_list
  142     ):
  143         single_turn_model_response_list = multi_turn_model_result_list_decoded[turn_index]
  144         if len(single_turn_ground_truth_list) == 0:
  145             if is_empty_execute_response(single_turn_model_response_list):
  146                 continue
  147             else:
  148                 return {
  149                     "valid": False,
  150                     "error_message": f"Model outputs valid function calls when it should not for turn {turn_index}.",
  151                     "error_type": "multi_turn:irrelevance_error:decoder_success",
  152                     "details": {
  153                         "model response decoded": single_turn_model_response_list,
  154                     },
  155                 }
  156     return {"valid": True}
  157 
  158 
  159 #### Sub-Chekcers ####
  160 
  161 
  162 def state_checker(model_instances: dict, ground_truth_instances: dict):
  163     """
  164     Checks if, after executing the function calls, the model_instance has the same state (defined by the attributes) as the ground_truth_instance.
  165     It checks if every instance in the model_instances has the same attributes as their corresponding instance (of the same class) from ground_truth_instances.
  166     """
  167     for class_name, ground_truth_instance in ground_truth_instances.items():
  168         model_instance = model_instances[class_name]
  169         valid, differences = _compare_instances(model_instance, ground_truth_instance)
  170 
  171         if not valid:
  172             model_instance_attributes = {
  173                 key: value
  174                 for key, value in vars(model_instance).items()
  175                 if not key.startswith("_")
  176             }
  177             ground_truth_instance_attributes = {
  178                 key: value
  179                 for key, value in vars(ground_truth_instance).items()
  180                 if not key.startswith("_")
  181             }
  182             # Format the error message for better readability
  183             return {
  184                 "valid": False,
  185                 "error_message": f"Model instance for {class_name} does not match the state with ground truth instance.",
  186                 "error_type": "multi_turn:instance_state_mismatch",
  187                 "details": {
  188                     "differences": differences,
  189                     "model_instance_state": model_instance_attributes,
  190                     "ground_truth_instance_state": ground_truth_instance_attributes,
  191                 },
  192             }
  193 
  194     return {"valid": True}
  195 
  196 
  197 def response_checker(
  198     model_response_list: list, ground_truth_response_list: list, turn_index: int
  199 ):
  200     """
  201     Checks if the model_response is a subsequence of the ground_truth_response.
  202     Each list contains the response of the function calls executed in that single turn.
  203     """
  204     # We don't need to enforce the order of the responses, because many entries have parallel operations, and so the model can execute them in any order.
  205     is_subsequence, missing_items = _is_subsequence_unordered(
  206         ground_truth_response_list, model_response_list
  207     )
  208     if not is_subsequence:
  209         return {
  210             "valid": False,
  211             "error_message": f"Model response execution results so far does not contain all the ground truth response execution results for turn {turn_index}.",
  212             "error_type": "multi_turn:execution_response_mismatch",
  213             "details": {
  214                 "missing_items": missing_items,
  215                 "model_response (including all previous turns)": model_response_list,
  216                 "ground_truth_response (only the current turn)": ground_truth_response_list,
  217             },
  218         }
  219 
  220     return {"valid": True}
  221 
  222 
  223 def method_invoke_order_checker(model_instances: dict, ground_truth_instances: dict):
  224     """
  225     Checks if the model_instance called the same order of methods as the ground_truth_instance.
  226     model_instance can call additional methods, but not skip any method that the ground_truth_instance called.
  227 
  228     Note: Currently, this functions only checks for the method names and not the arguments.
  229     """
  230     for class_name, ground_truth_instance in ground_truth_instances.items():
  231         model_instance = model_instances[class_name]
  232 
  233         # The get_method_called method is added by the LoggingMeta metaclass automatically
  234         model_invoke_order = model_instance.get_method_called()
  235         ground_truth_invoke_order = ground_truth_instance.get_method_called()
  236 
  237         # Extract the method names
  238         model_invoke_order = [method_call["method"] for method_call in model_invoke_order]
  239         ground_truth_invoke_order = [
  240             method_call["method"] for method_call in ground_truth_invoke_order
  241         ]
  242 
  243         is_subsequence, missing_items = _is_subsequence(
  244             ground_truth_invoke_order, model_invoke_order
  245         )
  246         if not is_subsequence:
  247             return {
  248                 "valid": False,
  249                 "error_message": f"Model instance for {class_name} does not match the method invoke order with ground truth instance. Missing items: {missing_items}",
  250                 "error_type": "multi_turn:method_invoke_order_mismatch",
  251             }
  252 
  253     return {"valid": True}
  254 
  255 
  256 #### Helper functions ####
  257 
  258 
  259 def _compare_instances(model_obect, ground_truth_object):
  260     """
  261     Checks if the model_object has the same attributes as the ground_truth_object. They are instances of the same class.
  262     """
  263     assert type(model_obect) == type(
  264         ground_truth_object
  265     ), "Objects are not of the same type."
  266     differences = {}
  267     valid = True
  268     for attr_name in vars(ground_truth_object):
  269         # We don't check for private attributes
  270         if attr_name.startswith("_"):
  271             continue
  272         model_attr = getattr(model_obect, attr_name)
  273         ground_truth_attr = getattr(ground_truth_object, attr_name)
  274 
  275         if model_attr != ground_truth_attr:
  276             valid = False
  277             differences[attr_name] = {"model": model_attr, "ground_truth": ground_truth_attr}
  278 
  279     return valid, differences
  280 
  281 
  282 def _is_subsequence(list1, list2) -> tuple[bool, list]:
  283     """
  284     Checks if list1 is a subsequence of list2, i.e., all elements of list1 are present in list2 in the same order.
  285     Also returns the elements of list1 that are not present in list2.
  286     """
  287     # Convert list2 to an iterator to ensure that the elements are consumed only once.
  288     iter_list2 = iter(list2)
  289     return all(item in iter_list2 for item in list1), [
  290         item for item in list1 if item not in list2
  291     ]
  292 
  293 
  294 def _is_subsequence_unordered(list1, list2) -> tuple[bool, list]:
  295     """
  296     Checks if all elements of list1 are present in list2, regardless of order.
  297     Also returns the elements of list1 that are not present in list2.
  298     """
  299     # Copy list2 to avoid modifying the original list during checks
  300     list2_copy = list2[:]
  301     
  302     # Check each item in list1 to see if it exists in list2_copy
  303     missing_elements = []
  304     for item in list1:
  305         try:
  306             # Attempt to remove one occurrence of `item` from list2_copy to handle duplicates
  307             list2_copy.remove(item)
  308         except ValueError:
  309             # If item is not found, add it to missing_elements
  310             missing_elements.append(item)
  311     
  312     # If there are missing elements, list1 is not a subsequence of list2
  313     is_subsequence = len(missing_elements) == 0
  314     return is_subsequence, missing_elements

FILE source/bfcl/bfcl_eval/eval_checker/multi_turn_eval/multi_turn_utils.py
    1 import importlib
    2 import inspect
    3 import json
    4 import re
    5 import copy
    6 
    7 CLASS_FILE_PATH_MAPPING = {
    8     "GorillaFileSystem": "bfcl_eval.eval_checker.multi_turn_eval.func_source_code.gorilla_file_system",
    9     "MathAPI": "bfcl_eval.eval_checker.multi_turn_eval.func_source_code.math_api",
   10     "MessageAPI": "bfcl_eval.eval_checker.multi_turn_eval.func_source_code.message_api",
   11     "TwitterAPI": "bfcl_eval.eval_checker.multi_turn_eval.func_source_code.posting_api",
   12     "TicketAPI": "bfcl_eval.eval_checker.multi_turn_eval.func_source_code.ticket_api",
   13     "TradingBot": "bfcl_eval.eval_checker.multi_turn_eval.func_source_code.trading_bot",
   14     "TravelAPI": "bfcl_eval.eval_checker.multi_turn_eval.func_source_code.travel_booking",
   15     "VehicleControlAPI": "bfcl_eval.eval_checker.multi_turn_eval.func_source_code.vehicle_control",
   16 }
   17 
   18 # These classes are stateless and do not require any initial configuration
   19 STATELESS_CLASSES = [
   20     "MathAPI",
   21 ]
   22 
   23 
   24 def execute_multi_turn_func_call(
   25     func_call_list: list[str],  # a list of strings of func calls
   26     initial_config: dict,
   27     involved_classes: list,
   28     model_name: str,
   29     test_entry_id: str,
   30     long_context: bool = False,
   31     is_evaL_run: bool = False,
   32 ) -> tuple[list[str], dict]:
   33     """
   34     TODO: Add docstring
   35     """
   36     if is_evaL_run:
   37         model_name += "_eval"
   38 
   39     class_method_name_mapping = {}
   40     involved_instances = {}
   41     for class_name in involved_classes:
   42         module_name = CLASS_FILE_PATH_MAPPING[class_name]
   43         # TODO: Handler the model name issue from handler more elegantly
   44         instance_name = (
   45             f"{model_name.replace('-', '_').replace('.', '_').replace('/', '_')}_{test_entry_id}_{class_name.lower()}_instance"
   46         )
   47         if instance_name not in globals():
   48             module = importlib.import_module(module_name)
   49             class_ = getattr(module, class_name)
   50             class_instance = class_()
   51             if class_name not in STATELESS_CLASSES:
   52                 class_initial_config = initial_config.get(class_name, {})
   53                 # Deep copy the initial configuration to avoid mutation issues
   54                 class_instance._load_scenario(
   55                     copy.deepcopy(class_initial_config), long_context=long_context
   56                 )
   57             globals()[instance_name] = class_instance
   58         # This happens in subsequent turns
   59         else:
   60             class_instance = globals()[instance_name]
   61 
   62         involved_instances[class_name] = class_instance
   63 
   64         # Retrieve all method names and map them to the instance
   65         for method_name, method in inspect.getmembers(
   66             class_instance, predicate=inspect.ismethod
   67         ):
   68             # Skip private methods
   69             if method_name.startswith("_"):
   70                 continue
   71             class_method_name_mapping[method_name] = instance_name
   72 
   73     execution_results = []
   74     for func_call in func_call_list:
   75         # Add the instance name to the method calls
   76         func_call = _process_method_calls(func_call, class_method_name_mapping)
   77 
   78         # Evaluate the function call
   79         try:
   80             # We need to make a copy here because otherwise the `eval(func_call)` would error. 
   81             func_call_copy = func_call
   82             # Before calling `eval`, we need to make sure that the function call is safe
   83             # We do so by checking if the function is `kill` or `exit`, etc.
   84             # Extract the function name first
   85             if "(" in func_call_copy:
   86                 func_call_copy = func_call_copy.split("(")[0]
   87             # Situation where the function call is a method call
   88             if "." in func_call_copy:
   89                 func_call_copy = func_call_copy.split(".")[1]
   90             if func_call_copy in ["kill", "exit", "quit", "remove", "unlink", "popen", "Popen", "run"]:
   91                 raise Exception(f"Function call {func_call_copy} is not allowed.")
   92 
   93             func_call_result = eval(func_call)
   94 
   95             if type(func_call_result) == str:
   96                 pass
   97             elif type(func_call_result) == dict:
   98                 # Some function returns a object instance, which is not serializable
   99                 try:
  100                     func_call_result = json.dumps(func_call_result)
  101                 except:
  102                     func_call_result = str(func_call_result)
  103             else:
  104                 func_call_result = str(func_call_result)
  105 
  106             execution_results.append(func_call_result)
  107         except Exception as e:
  108             execution_results.append(f"Error during execution: {str(e)}")
  109 
  110     return execution_results, involved_instances
  111 
  112 
  113 def is_empty_execute_response(input_list: list):
  114     if len(input_list) == 0:
  115         return True
  116     if len(input_list) == 1 and len(input_list[0]) == 0:
  117         return True
  118     return False
  119 
  120 
  121 def _process_method_calls(function_call_string: str, instance_mapping: dict) -> str:
  122     """
  123     Prepends the instance name to the function name for each of the function name represented in the string, you will
  124     also be provided with the mapping of method name to instance name.
  125 
  126     Example input:
  127     ```
  128     f(x = g((1, 2), h(3)), y = (4), z = (5, 6))
  129     ```
  130 
  131     Example return:
  132     ```
  133     a.f(x=a.g((1, 2), a.h(3)), y=(4), z=(5, 6))
  134     ```
  135 
  136     Args:
  137         function_call_string (str): The function call string to parse.
  138         class_mapping (dict): A dictionary mapping method names to instance names.
  139 
  140     Returns:
  141         str: The parsed function call string with instance names prepended to method names.
  142     """
  143 
  144     def replace_function(match):
  145         func_name = match.group(1)
  146         if func_name in instance_mapping:
  147             return f"{instance_mapping[func_name]}.{func_name}"
  148         return func_name
  149 
  150     # Regular expression to match function names
  151     pattern = r"\b([a-zA-Z_]\w*)\s*(?=\()"
  152 
  153     # Replace function names with their class-prepended versions
  154     processed_string = re.sub(pattern, replace_function, function_call_string)
  155 
  156     return processed_string

   25 class ClaudeHandler(BaseHandler):
   26     def __init__(self, model_name, temperature) -> None:
   27         super().__init__(model_name, temperature)
   28         self.model_style = ModelStyle.Anthropic
   29         self.client = Anthropic(api_key=os.getenv("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"))
   30 
   31     def decode_ast(self, result, language="Python"):
   32         if "FC" not in self.model_name:
   33             func = result
   34             if " " == func[0]:
   35                 func = func[1:]
   36             if not func.startswith("["):
   37                 func = "[" + func
   38             if not func.endswith("]"):
   39                 func = func + "]"
   40             decode_output = ast_parse(func, language)
   41             return decode_output
   42 
   43         else:
   44             decoded_output = []
   45             for invoked_function in result:
   46                 name = list(invoked_function.keys())[0]
   47                 params = json.loads(invoked_function[name])
   48                 decoded_output.append({name: params})
   49             return decoded_output
   50 
   51     def decode_execute(self, result):
   52         if "FC" not in self.model_name:
   53             func = result
   54             if " " == func[0]:
   55                 func = func[1:]
   56             if not func.startswith("["):
   57                 func = "[" + func
   58             if not func.endswith("]"):
   59                 func = func + "]"
   60             decode_output = ast_parse(func)
   61             execution_list = []
   62             for function_call in decode_output:
   63                 for key, value in function_call.items():
   64                     execution_list.append(
   65                         f"{key}({','.join([f'{k}={repr(v)}' for k, v in value.items()])})"
   66                     )
   67             return execution_list
   68 
   69         else:
   70             function_call = convert_to_function_call(result)
   71             return function_call
   72 
   73     @retry_with_backoff(error_type=RateLimitError)
   74     def generate_with_backoff(self, **kwargs):
   75         start_time = time.time()
   76         api_response = self.client.messages.create(**kwargs)
   77         end_time = time.time()
   78 
   79         return api_response, end_time - start_time
   80 
   81     def _get_max_tokens(self):
   82         """
   83         max_tokens is required to be set when querying, so we default to the model's max tokens
   84         """
   85         if "claude-opus-4-20250514" in self.model_name:
   86             return 32000
   87         elif "claude-sonnet-4-20250514" in self.model_name:
   88             return 64000
   89         elif "claude-3-5-haiku-20241022" in self.model_name:
   90             return 8192
   91         else:
   92             raise ValueError(f"Unsupported model: {self.model_name}")

   94     #### FC methods ####

   96     def _query_FC(self, inference_data: dict):
   97         inference_data["inference_input_log"] = {
   98             "message": repr(inference_data["message"]),
   99             "tools": inference_data["tools"],
  100         }
  101         messages = inference_data["message"]
  102 
  103         if inference_data["caching_enabled"]:
  104             # Only add cache control to the last two user messages
  105             # Remove previously set cache control flags from all user messages except the last two
  106             count = 0
  107             for message in reversed(messages):
  108                 if message["role"] == "user":
  109                     if count < 2:
  110                         message["content"][0]["cache_control"] = {"type": "ephemeral"}
  111                     else:
  112                         if "cache_control" in message["content"][0]:
  113                             del message["content"][0]["cache_control"]
  114                     count += 1
  115 
  116         # Need to set timeout to avoid auto-error when requesting large context length
  117         # https://github.com/anthropics/anthropic-sdk-python#long-requests
  118         return self.generate_with_backoff(
  119             model=self.model_name.strip("-FC"),
  120             max_tokens=self._get_max_tokens(),
  121             tools=inference_data["tools"],
  122             temperature=self.temperature,
  123             messages=messages,
  124             timeout=1200,
  125         )
  126 
  127     def _pre_query_processing_FC(self, inference_data: dict, test_entry: dict) -> dict:
  128         for round_idx in range(len(test_entry["question"])):
  129             test_entry["question"][round_idx] = convert_system_prompt_into_user_prompt(
  130                 test_entry["question"][round_idx]
  131             )
  132             test_entry["question"][round_idx] = combine_consecutive_user_prompts(
  133                 test_entry["question"][round_idx]
  134             )
  135         inference_data["message"] = []
  136 
  137         test_entry_id: str = test_entry["id"]
  138         test_category: str = test_entry_id.rsplit("_", 1)[0]
  139         # caching enabled only for multi_turn category
  140         inference_data["caching_enabled"] = is_multi_turn(test_category)
  141 
  142         return inference_data
  143 
  144     def _compile_tools(self, inference_data: dict, test_entry: dict) -> dict:
  145         functions: list = test_entry["function"]
  146         test_category: str = test_entry["id"].rsplit("_", 1)[0]
  147 
  148         functions = func_doc_language_specific_pre_processing(functions, test_category)
  149         tools = convert_to_tool(functions, GORILLA_TO_OPENAPI, self.model_style)
  150 
  151         if inference_data["caching_enabled"]:
  152             # First time compiling tools, so adding cache control flag to the last tool
  153             if "tools" not in inference_data:
  154                 tools[-1]["cache_control"] = {"type": "ephemeral"}
  155             # This is the situation where the tools are already compiled and we are adding more tools to the existing tools (in miss_func category)
  156             # We add the cache control flag to the last tool in the previous existing tools and the last tool in the new tools to maximize cache hit
  157             else:
  158                 existing_tool_len = len(inference_data["tools"])
  159                 tools[existing_tool_len - 1]["cache_control"] = {"type": "ephemeral"}
  160                 tools[-1]["cache_control"] = {"type": "ephemeral"}
  161 
  162         inference_data["tools"] = tools
  163 
  164         return inference_data
  165 
  166     def _parse_query_response_FC(self, api_response: any) -> dict:
  167         text_outputs = []
  168         tool_call_outputs = []
  169         tool_call_ids = []
  170 
  171         for content in api_response.content:
  172             if isinstance(content, TextBlock):
  173                 text_outputs.append(content.text)
  174             elif isinstance(content, ToolUseBlock):
  175                 tool_call_outputs.append({content.name: json.dumps(content.input)})
  176                 tool_call_ids.append(content.id)
  177 
  178         model_responses = tool_call_outputs if tool_call_outputs else text_outputs
  179 
  180         model_responses_message_for_chat_history = api_response.content
  181 
  182         return {
  183             "model_responses": model_responses,
  184             "model_responses_message_for_chat_history": model_responses_message_for_chat_history,
  185             "tool_call_ids": tool_call_ids,
  186             "input_token": api_response.usage.input_tokens,
  187             "output_token": api_response.usage.output_tokens,
  188         }
  189 
  190     def add_first_turn_message_FC(
  191         self, inference_data: dict, first_turn_message: list[dict]
  192     ) -> dict:
  193         for message in first_turn_message:
  194             message["content"] = [{"type": "text", "text": message["content"]}]
  195         inference_data["message"].extend(first_turn_message)
  196         return inference_data

  202             message["content"] = [{"type": "text", "text": message["content"]}]
  203         inference_data["message"].extend(user_message)
  204         return inference_data

  206     def _add_assistant_message_FC(

  210             {
  211                 "role": "assistant",

  217     def _add_execution_results_FC(
  218         self,
  219         inference_data: dict,
  220         execution_results: list[str],
  221         model_response_data: dict,
  222     ) -> dict:
  223         # Claude don't use the tool role; it uses the user role to send the tool output
  224         tool_message = {
  225             "role": "user",
  226             "content": [],
  227         }
  228         for execution_result, tool_call_id in zip(
  229             execution_results, model_response_data["tool_call_ids"]
  230         ):
  231             tool_message["content"].append(
  232                 {
  233                     "type": "tool_result",
  234                     "content": execution_result,
  235                     "tool_use_id": tool_call_id,
  236                 }
  237             )
  238 
  239         inference_data["message"].append(tool_message)
  240 
  241         return inference_data

  243     #### Prompting methods ####
