   23 def _cast_to_openai_type(properties, mapping):
   24     for key, value in properties.items():
   25         if "type" not in value:
   26             properties[key]["type"] = "string"
   27         else:
   28             var_type = value["type"]
   29             if mapping == GORILLA_TO_OPENAPI and var_type == "float":
   30                 properties[key]["format"] = "float"
   31                 properties[key]["description"] += " This is a float type value."
   32             if var_type in mapping:
   33                 properties[key]["type"] = mapping[var_type]
   34             else:
   35                 properties[key]["type"] = "string"
   36 
   37         # Currently support:
   38         # - list of any
   39         # - list of list of any
   40         # - list of dict
   41         # - list of list of dict
   42         # - dict of any
   43 
   44         if properties[key]["type"] == "array" or properties[key]["type"] == "object":
   45             if "properties" in properties[key]:
   46                 properties[key]["properties"] = _cast_to_openai_type(
   47                     properties[key]["properties"], mapping
   48                 )
   49             elif "items" in properties[key]:
   50                 properties[key]["items"]["type"] = mapping[properties[key]["items"]["type"]]
   51                 if (
   52                     properties[key]["items"]["type"] == "array"
   53                     and "items" in properties[key]["items"]
   54                 ):
   55                     properties[key]["items"]["items"]["type"] = mapping[
   56                         properties[key]["items"]["items"]["type"]
   57                     ]
   58                 elif (
   59                     properties[key]["items"]["type"] == "object"
   60                     and "properties" in properties[key]["items"]
   61                 ):
   62                     properties[key]["items"]["properties"] = _cast_to_openai_type(
   63                         properties[key]["items"]["properties"], mapping
   64                     )
   65     return properties
   66 
   67 
   68 def convert_to_tool(functions, mapping, model_style):
   69     functions = copy.deepcopy(functions)
   70     oai_tool = []
   71     for item in functions:
   72         if "." in item["name"] and model_style in [
   73             ModelStyle.OpenAI_Completions,
   74             ModelStyle.OpenAI_Responses,
   75             ModelStyle.Mistral,
   76             ModelStyle.GOOGLE,
   77             ModelStyle.OSSMODEL,
   78             ModelStyle.Anthropic,
   79             ModelStyle.COHERE,
   80             ModelStyle.AMAZON,
   81             ModelStyle.NOVITA_AI,
   82         ]:
   83             # OAI does not support "." in the function name so we replace it with "_". ^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,64}$ is the regex for the name.
   84             item["name"] = re.sub(r"\.", "_", item["name"])
   85 
   86         item["parameters"]["type"] = "object"
   87         item["parameters"]["properties"] = _cast_to_openai_type(
   88             item["parameters"]["properties"], mapping
   89         )
   90 
   91         if model_style == ModelStyle.Anthropic:
   92             item["input_schema"] = item["parameters"]
   93             del item["parameters"]
   94 
   95         if model_style == ModelStyle.AMAZON:
   96             item["inputSchema"] = {"json": item["parameters"]}
   97             del item["parameters"]
   98 
   99         if model_style in [
  100             ModelStyle.GOOGLE,
  101             ModelStyle.WRITER,
  102         ]:
  103             # Remove fields that are not supported by Gemini or Palmyra.
  104             # No `optional` field in function schema.
  105             if "optional" in item["parameters"]:
  106                 del item["parameters"]["optional"]
  107             for params in item["parameters"]["properties"].values():
  108                 if "description" not in params:
  109                     params["description"] = ""
  110                 # No `default` field in GOOGLE or Palmyra's schema.
  111                 if "default" in params:
  112                     params["description"] += f" Default is: {str(params['default'])}."
  113                     del params["default"]
  114                 # No `optional` field in parameter schema as well.
  115                 if "optional" in params:
  116                     params["description"] += f" Optional: {str(params['optional'])}."
  117                     del params["optional"]
  118                 # No `required` field in parameter schema as well.
  119                 if "required" in params:
  120                     params["description"] += f" Required: {str(params['required'])}."
  121                     del params["required"]
  122                 # No `maximum` field.
  123                 if "maximum" in params:
  124                     params["description"] += f" Maximum value: {str(params['maximum'])}."
  125                     del params["maximum"]
  126                 # No `minItems` field.
  127                 if "minItems" in params:
  128                     params[
  129                         "description"
  130                     ] += f" Minimum number of items: {str(params['minItems'])}."
  131                     del params["minItems"]
  132                 # No `maxItems` field.
  133                 if "maxItems" in params:
  134                     params[
  135                         "description"
  136                     ] += f" Maximum number of items: {str(params['maxItems'])}."
  137                     del params["maxItems"]
  138                 # No `additionalProperties` field.
  139                 if "additionalProperties" in params:
  140                     params[
  141                         "description"
  142                     ] += f" Additional properties: {str(params['additionalProperties'])}."
  143                     del params["additionalProperties"]
  144                 # For Gemini, only `enum` field when the type is `string`.
  145                 # For Palmyra, `enum` field is not supported.
  146                 if "enum" in params and (
  147                     model_style == ModelStyle.WRITER
  148                     or (model_style == ModelStyle.GOOGLE and params["type"] != "string")
  149                 ):
  150                     params["description"] += f" Enum values: {str(params['enum'])}."
  151                     del params["enum"]
  152                 # No `format` when type is `string`
  153                 if "format" in params and params["type"] == "string":
  154                     params["description"] += f" Format: {str(params['format'])}."
  155                     del params["format"]
  156 
  157         # Process the return field
  158         if "response" in item:
  159             if model_style in [
  160                 ModelStyle.Anthropic,
  161                 ModelStyle.GOOGLE,
  162                 ModelStyle.FIREWORK_AI,
  163                 ModelStyle.WRITER,
  164                 ModelStyle.AMAZON,
  165                 ModelStyle.NOVITA_AI,
  166             ]:
  167                 item[
  168                     "description"
  169                 ] += f" The response field has the following schema: {json.dumps(item['response'])}"
  170                 del item["response"]
  171 
  172         if model_style in [
  173             ModelStyle.Anthropic,
  174             ModelStyle.GOOGLE,
  175             ModelStyle.OSSMODEL,
  176         ]:
  177             oai_tool.append(item)
  178         elif model_style in [
  179             ModelStyle.OpenAI_Responses
  180         ]:
  181             oai_tool.append({"type": "function", 
  182                              "name": item["name"], 
  183                              "description": item["description"], 
  184                              "parameters": item["parameters"]})
  185         elif model_style in [
  186             ModelStyle.COHERE,
  187             ModelStyle.OpenAI_Completions,
  188             ModelStyle.Mistral,
  189             ModelStyle.FIREWORK_AI,
  190             ModelStyle.WRITER,
  191             ModelStyle.NOVITA_AI,
  192         ]:
  193             oai_tool.append({"type": "function", "function": item})
  194         elif model_style == ModelStyle.AMAZON:
  195             oai_tool.append({"toolSpec": item})
  196 
  197     return oai_tool
  198

  200 def convert_to_function_call(function_call_list):
  201     if type(function_call_list) == dict:
  202         function_call_list = [function_call_list]
  203     # function_call_list is of type list[dict[str, str]] or list[dict[str, dict]]
  204     execution_list = []
  205     for function_call in function_call_list:
  206         for key, value in function_call.items():
  207             if type(value) == str:
  208                 value = json.loads(value)
  209             execution_list.append(
  210                 f"{key}({','.join([f'{k}={repr(v)}' for k,v in value.items()])})"
  211             )
  212 
  213     return execution_list

  216 def convert_value(value, type_str):
  217     """Convert a string value into its appropriate Python data type based on the provided type string.
  218 
  219     Arg:
  220         value: the value to convert
  221         type_str: the type to convert the value to
  222 
  223     Returns:
  224         The value converted into the requested type or the original value
  225         if the conversion failed.
  226     """
  227 
  228     if type_str in ("list", "dict"):
  229         try:
  230             return ast.literal_eval(value)
  231         except:
  232             return value
  233 
  234     type_class = getattr(builtins, type_str)
  235     try:
  236         return type_class(value)
  237     except ValueError:
  238         return value
  239 
  240 
  241 def ast_parse(input_str: str, language: str="Python") -> list[dict]:
  242     if language == "Python":
  243         cleaned_input = input_str.strip("[]'")
  244         parsed = ast.parse(cleaned_input, mode="eval")
  245         extracted = []
  246         if isinstance(parsed.body, ast.Call):
  247             extracted.append(resolve_ast_call(parsed.body))
  248         else:
  249             for elem in parsed.body.elts:
  250                 assert isinstance(elem, ast.Call)
  251                 extracted.append(resolve_ast_call(elem))
  252         return extracted
  253     elif language == "Java":
  254         return parse_java_function_call(
  255             input_str[1:-1]
  256         )  # Remove the [ and ] from the string
  257     elif language == "JavaScript":
  258         return parse_javascript_function_call(input_str[1:-1])
  259     else:
  260         raise NotImplementedError(f"Unsupported language: {language}")
  261 
  262 
  263 def resolve_ast_call(elem):
  264     # Handle nested attributes for deeply nested module paths
  265     func_parts = []
  266     func_part = elem.func
  267     while isinstance(func_part, ast.Attribute):
  268         func_parts.append(func_part.attr)
  269         func_part = func_part.value
  270     if isinstance(func_part, ast.Name):
  271         func_parts.append(func_part.id)
  272     func_name = ".".join(reversed(func_parts))
  273     args_dict = {}
  274     for arg in elem.keywords:
  275         output = resolve_ast_by_type(arg.value)
  276         args_dict[arg.arg] = output
  277     return {func_name: args_dict}
  278 
  279 
  280 def resolve_ast_by_type(value):
  281     if isinstance(value, ast.Constant):
  282         if value.value is Ellipsis:
  283             output = "..."
  284         else:
  285             output = value.value
  286     elif isinstance(value, ast.UnaryOp):
  287         output = -value.operand.value
  288     elif isinstance(value, ast.List):
  289         output = [resolve_ast_by_type(v) for v in value.elts]
  290     elif isinstance(value, ast.Dict):
  291         output = {
  292             resolve_ast_by_type(k): resolve_ast_by_type(v)
  293             for k, v in zip(value.keys, value.values)
  294         }
  295     elif isinstance(
  296         value, ast.NameConstant
  297     ):  # Added this condition to handle boolean values
  298         output = value.value
  299     elif isinstance(
  300         value, ast.BinOp
  301     ):  # Added this condition to handle function calls as arguments
  302         output = eval(ast.unparse(value))
  303     elif isinstance(value, ast.Name):
  304         output = value.id
  305     elif isinstance(value, ast.Call):
  306         if len(value.keywords) == 0:
  307             output = ast.unparse(value)
  308         else:
  309             output = resolve_ast_call(value)
  310     elif isinstance(value, ast.Tuple):
  311         output = tuple(resolve_ast_by_type(v) for v in value.elts)
  312     elif isinstance(value, ast.Lambda):
  313         output = eval(ast.unparse(value.body[0].value))
  314     elif isinstance(value, ast.Ellipsis):
  315         output = "..."
  316     elif isinstance(value, ast.Subscript):
  317         try:
  318             output = ast.unparse(value.body[0].value)
  319         except:
  320             output = ast.unparse(value.value) + "[" + ast.unparse(value.slice) + "]"
  321     else:
  322         raise Exception(f"Unsupported AST type: {type(value)}")
  323     return output
  324 
  325 
  326 def system_prompt_pre_processing_chat_model(prompts, function_docs, test_category):
  327     """
  328     Add a system prompt to the chat model to instruct the model on the available functions and the expected response format.
  329     If the prompts list already contains a system prompt, append the additional system prompt content to the existing system prompt.
  330     """
  331     assert type(prompts) == list
  332 
  333     system_prompt_template = DEFAULT_SYSTEM_PROMPT
  334 
  335     system_prompt = system_prompt_template.format(functions=function_docs)
  336 
  337     # System prompt must be in the first position
  338     # If the question comes with a system prompt, append its content at the end of the chat template.
  339     if prompts[0]["role"] == "system":
  340         prompts[0]["content"] = system_prompt + "\n\n" + prompts[0]["content"]
  341     # Otherwise, use the system prompt template to create a new system prompt.
  342     else:
  343         prompts.insert(
  344             0,
  345             {"role": "system", "content": system_prompt},
  346         )
  347 
  348     return prompts
  349 
  350 
  351 def convert_system_prompt_into_user_prompt(prompts: list[dict]) -> list[dict]:
  352     """
  353     Some FC models doesn't support system prompt in the message field, so we turn it into user prompt
  354     """
  355     for prompt in prompts:
  356         if prompt["role"] == "system":
  357             prompt["role"] = "user"
  358     return prompts
  359 
  360 
  361 def combine_consecutive_user_prompts(prompts: list[dict]) -> list[dict]:
  362     """
  363     Some models require the prompt to be alternating between user and assistant.
  364     We combine consecutive user prompts into a single user prompt.
  365     """
  366     combined_prompts = []
  367     for prompt in prompts:
  368         if (
  369             prompt["role"] == "user"
  370             and combined_prompts
  371             and combined_prompts[-1]["role"] == "user"
  372         ):
  373             combined_prompts[-1]["content"] += "\n\n" + prompt["content"]
  374         else:
  375             combined_prompts.append(prompt)
  376 
  377     return combined_prompts
  378 
  379 
  380 def _get_language_specific_hint(test_category):
  381     if test_category == "java":
  382         return " Note that the provided function is in Java 8 SDK syntax."
  383     elif test_category == "javascript":
  384         return " Note that the provided function is in JavaScript syntax."
  385     else:
  386         return " Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax."
  387 
  388 
  389 def func_doc_language_specific_pre_processing(function, test_category):
  390     if len(function) == 0:
  391         return function
  392 
  393     assert type(function) == list
  394     for item in function:
  395         # Add language specific hints to the function description
  396         func_description = item["description"]
  397         item["description"] = item["description"] + _get_language_specific_hint(
  398             test_category
  399         )
  400         # Process the parameters
  401         properties = item["parameters"]["properties"]
  402         if test_category == "java":
  403             for key, value in properties.items():
  404                 if value["type"] == "any":
  405                     properties[key][
  406                         "description"
  407                     ] += " This parameter can be of any type of Java object in string representation."
  408                 else:
  409                     value[
  410                         "description"
  411                     ] += f" This is Java {value['type']} type parameter in string representation."
  412                 if value["type"] == "ArrayList" or value["type"] == "Array":
  413                     value[
  414                         "description"
  415                     ] += f" The list elements are of type {value['items']['type']}; they are not in string representation."
  416                     del value["items"]
  417 
  418                 value["type"] = "string"
  419 
  420         elif test_category == "javascript":
  421             for key, value in properties.items():
  422                 if value["type"] == "any":
  423                     properties[key][
  424                         "description"
  425                     ] += " This parameter can be of any type of JavaScript object in string representation."
  426                 else:
  427                     value[
  428                         "description"
  429                     ] += f" This is JavaScript {value['type']} type parameter in string representation."
  430                 if value["type"] == "array":
  431                     value[
  432                         "description"
  433                     ] += f" The list elements are of type {value['items']['type']}; they are not in string representation."
  434                     del value["items"]
  435 
  436                 if value["type"] == "dict":
  437                     if "properties" in value:  # not every dict has properties
  438                         value[
  439                             "description"
  440                         ] += f" The dictionary entries have the following schema; they are not in string representation. {json.dumps(value['properties'])}"
  441                         del value["properties"]
  442 
  443                 value["type"] = "string"
  444 
  445     return function
  446 
  447 
  448 def construct_tool_use_system_prompt(tools):
  449     tool_use_system_prompt = (
  450         "In this environment you have access to a set of tools you can use to answer the user's question.\n"
  451         "\n"
  452         "You may call them like this:\n"
  453         "<function_calls>\n"
  454         "<invoke>\n"
  455         "<tool_name>$TOOL_NAME</tool_name>\n"
  456         "<parameters>\n"
  457         "<$PARAMETER_NAME>$PARAMETER_VALUE</$PARAMETER_NAME>\n"
  458         "...\n"
  459         "</parameters>\n"
  460         "</invoke>\n"
  461         "</function_calls>\n"
  462         "\n"
  463         "Here are the tools available:\n"
  464         "<tools>\n"
  465         + "\n".join(
  466             [
  467                 construct_format_tool_for_claude_prompt(
  468                     tool["name"], tool["description"], tool["parameters"]["properties"]
  469                 )
  470                 for tool in tools
  471             ]
  472         )
  473         + "\n</tools>"
  474     )
  475 
  476     return tool_use_system_prompt
  477 
  478 
  479 def construct_format_tool_for_claude_prompt(name, description, parameters):
  480     constructed_prompt = (
  481         "<tool_description>\n"
  482         f"<tool_name>{name}</tool_name>\n"
  483         "<description>\n"
  484         f"{description}\n"
  485         "</description>\n"
  486         "<parameters>\n"
  487         f"{construct_format_parameters_prompt(parameters)}\n"
  488         "</parameters>\n"
  489         "</tool_description>"
  490     )
  491 
  492     return constructed_prompt
  493 
  494 
  495 def construct_format_parameters_prompt(parameters):
  496     constructed_prompt = ""
  497     for parameter_name, parameter in parameters.items():
  498         if parameter_name == "required":
  499             continue
  500         if "description" in parameter:
  501             description_string = parameter["description"]
  502         else:
  503             description_string = ""
  504         if "default" in parameter:
  505             description_string += f"\nDefault value: {parameter['default']}"
  506         elif "items" in parameter:
  507             description_string += f"\n List element type: {str(parameter['items'])}"
  508         elif "properties" in parameter:
  509             description_string += (
  510                 f"\n Dictionaries properties: {str(parameter['properties'])}"
  511             )
  512         if "description" in parameter:
  513             constructed_prompt += f"<parameter>\n<name>{parameter_name}</name>\n<type>{parameter['type']}</type>\n<description>{description_string}</description>\n</parameter>\n"
  514         else:
  515             constructed_prompt += f"<parameter>\n<name>{parameter_name}</name>\n<type>{parameter['type']}</type>\n</parameter>\n"
  516     constructed_prompt = constructed_prompt[:-1]
  517     return constructed_prompt
  518 
  519 
  520 def _function_calls_valid_format_and_invoke_extraction(last_completion):
  521     """Check if the function call follows a valid format and extract the attempted function calls if so. Does not check if the tools actually exist or if they are called with the requisite params."""
  522 
  523     # Check if there are any of the relevant XML tags present that would indicate an attempted function call.
  524     function_call_tags = re.findall(
  525         r"<function_calls>|</function_calls>|<invoke>|</invoke>|<tool_name>|</tool_name>|<parameters>|</parameters>",
  526         last_completion,
  527         re.DOTALL,
  528     )
  529     if not function_call_tags:
  530         return {"status": True, "invokes": []}
  531 
  532     # Extract content between <function_calls> tags. If there are multiple we will only parse the first and ignore the rest, regardless of their correctness.
  533     match = re.search(r"<function_calls>(.*)</function_calls>", last_completion, re.DOTALL)
  534     if not match:
  535         return {
  536             "status": False,
  537             "reason": "No valid <function_calls></function_calls> tags present in your query.",
  538         }
  539 
  540     func_calls = match.group(1)
  541 
  542     prefix_match = re.search(r"^(.*?)<function_calls>", last_completion, re.DOTALL)
  543     if prefix_match:
  544         func_call_prefix_content = prefix_match.group(1)
  545 
  546     # Check for invoke tags
  547     invoke_regex = r"<invoke>.*?</invoke>"
  548     if not re.search(invoke_regex, func_calls, re.DOTALL):
  549         return {
  550             "status": False,
  551             "reason": "Missing <invoke></invoke> tags inside of <function_calls></function_calls> tags.",
  552         }
  553 
  554     # Check each invoke contains tool name and parameters
  555     invoke_strings = re.findall(invoke_regex, func_calls, re.DOTALL)
  556     invokes = []
  557     for invoke_string in invoke_strings:
  558         tool_name = re.findall(r"<tool_name>.*?</tool_name>", invoke_string, re.DOTALL)
  559         if not tool_name:
  560             return {
  561                 "status": False,
  562                 "reason": "Missing <tool_name></tool_name> tags inside of <invoke></invoke> tags.",
  563             }
  564         if len(tool_name) > 1:
  565             return {
  566                 "status": False,
  567                 "reason": "More than one tool_name specified inside single set of <invoke></invoke> tags.",
  568             }
  569 
  570         parameters = re.findall(r"<parameters>.*?</parameters>", invoke_string, re.DOTALL)
  571         if not parameters:
  572             return {
  573                 "status": False,
  574                 "reason": "Missing <parameters></paraeters> tags inside of <invoke></invoke> tags.",
  575             }
  576         if len(parameters) > 1:
  577             return {
  578                 "status": False,
  579                 "reason": "More than one set of <parameters></parameters> tags specified inside single set of <invoke></invoke> tags.",
  580             }
  581 
  582         # Check for balanced tags inside parameters
  583         tags = re.findall(
  584             r"<.*?>",
  585             parameters[0].replace("<parameters>", "").replace("</parameters>", ""),
  586             re.DOTALL,
  587         )
  588         if len(tags) % 2 != 0:
  589             return {
  590                 "status": False,
  591                 "reason": "Imbalanced tags inside <parameters></parameters> tags.",
  592             }
  593 
  594         # Loop through the tags and check if each even-indexed tag matches the tag in the position after it (with the / of course). If valid store their content for later use.
  595         parameters_with_values = []
  596         for i in range(0, len(tags), 2):
  597             opening_tag = tags[i]
  598             closing_tag = tags[i + 1]
  599             closing_tag_without_second_char = closing_tag[:1] + closing_tag[2:]
  600             if closing_tag[1] != "/" or opening_tag != closing_tag_without_second_char:
  601                 return {
  602                     "status": False,
  603                     "reason": "Non-matching opening and closing tags inside <parameters></parameters> tags.",
  604                 }
  605 
  606             parameters_with_values.append(
  607                 (
  608                     opening_tag[1:-1],
  609                     re.search(
  610                         rf"{opening_tag}(.*?){closing_tag}", parameters[0], re.DOTALL
  611                     ).group(1),
  612                 )
  613             )
  614 
  615         # Parse out the full function call
  616         invokes.append(
  617             {
  618                 "tool_name": tool_name[0]
  619                 .replace("<tool_name>", "")
  620                 .replace("</tool_name>", ""),
  621                 "parameters_with_values": parameters_with_values,
  622             }
  623         )
  624 
  625     return {
  626         "status": True,
  627         "invokes": invokes,
  628         "prefix_content": func_call_prefix_content,
  629     }
  630 
  631 
  632 def _convert_value(value, type_str):
  633     """Convert a string value into its appropriate Python data type based on the provided type string.
  634 
  635     Arg:
  636         value: the value to convert
  637         type_str: the type to convert the value to
  638 
  639     Returns:
  640         The value converted into the requested type or the original value
  641         if the conversion failed.
  642     """
  643 
  644     if type_str in ("list", "dict"):
  645         try:
  646             return ast.literal_eval(value)
  647         except:
  648             return value
  649     if type_str == "string":
  650         type_str = "str"
  651     type_class = getattr(builtins, type_str)
  652     try:
  653         return type_class(value)
  654     except ValueError:
  655         return value
  656

  658 # TODO: Re-organize this file to make it more readable and maintainable
  659 def extract_system_prompt(prompts: list[dict]) -> str:
  660     for i, prompt in enumerate(prompts):
  661         if prompt["role"] == "system":
  662             system_prompt = prompt["content"]
  663             del prompts[i]
  664             return system_prompt
  665     return None
  666 
  667 
  668 def extract_last_user_message(prompts: list[dict], user_role_name: str = "user") -> dict:
  669     for i in range(len(prompts) - 1, -1, -1):
  670         if prompts[i]["role"] == user_role_name:
  671             last_user_message = prompts[i]
  672             del prompts[i]
  673             return last_user_message
  674     return "User did not specify a query."

  680 def format_execution_results_prompting(
  681     inference_data: dict, execution_results: list[str], model_response_data: dict
  682 ) -> str:
  683     # Add the execution results to one single user message
  684     tool_results = []
  685     for execution_result, decoded_model_response in zip(
  686         execution_results, model_response_data["model_responses_decoded"]
  687     ):
  688         tool_results.append(
  689             {"role": "tool", "name": decoded_model_response, "content": execution_result}
  690         )
  691 
  692     return repr(tool_results)

  695 def default_decode_ast_prompting(result: str, language: str="Python") -> list[dict]:
  696     result = result.strip("`\n ")
  697     if not result.startswith("["):
  698         result = "[" + result
  699     if not result.endswith("]"):
  700         result = result + "]"
  701     decoded_output = ast_parse(result, language)
  702     return decoded_output
  703 
  704 
  705 def default_decode_execute_prompting(result: str) -> list[str]:
  706     result = result.strip("`\n ")
  707     if not result.startswith("["):
  708         result = "[" + result
  709     if not result.endswith("]"):
  710         result = result + "]"
  711     decoded_output = ast_parse(result)
  712     return decoded_output_to_execution_list(decoded_output)

  714 
  715 def parse_nested_value(value):
  716     """
  717     Parse a potentially nested value from the AST output.
  718 
  719     Args:
  720         value: The value to parse, which could be a nested dictionary, which includes another function call, or a simple value.
  721 
  722     Returns:
  723         str: A string representation of the value, handling nested function calls and nested dictionary function arguments.
  724     """
  725     if isinstance(value, dict):
  726         # Check if the dictionary represents a function call (i.e., the value is another dictionary or complex structure)
  727         if all(isinstance(v, dict) for v in value.values()):
  728             func_name = list(value.keys())[0]
  729             args = value[func_name]
  730             args_str = ", ".join(f"{k}={parse_nested_value(v)}" for k, v in args.items())
  731             return f"{func_name}({args_str})"
  732         else:
  733             # If it's a simple dictionary, treat it as key-value pairs
  734             return (
  735                 "{"
  736                 + ", ".join(f"'{k}': {parse_nested_value(v)}" for k, v in value.items())
  737                 + "}"
  738             )
  739     return repr(value)
  740 
  741 
  742 def decoded_output_to_execution_list(decoded_output: list[dict]) -> list[str]:
  743     """
  744     Convert decoded output to a list of executable function calls.
  745 
  746     Args:
  747         decoded_output (list): A list of dictionaries representing function calls.
  748 
  749     Returns:
  750         list: A list of strings, each representing an executable function call.
  751     """
  752     execution_list = []
  753     for function_call in decoded_output:
  754         for key, value in function_call.items():
  755             args_str = ", ".join(f"{k}={parse_nested_value(v)}" for k, v in value.items())
  756             execution_list.append(f"{key}({args_str})")
  757     return execution_list
  758 
  759 
  760 def retry_with_backoff(
  761     error_type: Optional[Union[Type[Exception], List[Type[Exception]]]] = None,
  762     error_message_pattern: Optional[str] = None,
  763     min_wait: int = 6,
  764     max_wait: int = 120,
  765     **kwargs,
  766 ) -> Callable:
  767     """
  768     Decorator to retry a function with exponential backoff based on specified error types or result conditions.
  769 
  770     Note:
  771         At least one of `error_type` or `error_message_pattern` must be provided.
  772         If both `error_type` and `error_message_pattern` are provided, the retry will occur if either condition is met.
  773 
  774     Args:
  775         error_type ([Union[Type[Exception], List[Type[Exception]]]], optional): The exception type to retry on. Supports one exception, or a list of exceptions.
  776         error_message_pattern (str, optional):
  777             A regex pattern to match against the exception message to retry on.
  778             This is useful when the user wants to retry based on the exception message,
  779             especially if the exception raised is too broad.
  780         min_wait (int, optional): Minimum wait time in seconds for the backoff.
  781         max_wait (int, optional): Maximum wait time in seconds for the backoff.
  782         **kwargs: Additional keyword arguments for the `tenacity.retry` decorator, such as `stop`, `reraise`, etc.
  783 
  784     Returns:
  785         Callable: The decorated function with retry logic applied.
  786     """
  787 
  788     def decorator(func: Callable) -> Callable:
  789         # Collect retry conditions based on provided parameters
  790         conditions = []
  791         if error_type is not None:
  792             if isinstance(error_type, list):
  793                 for et in error_type:
  794                     conditions.append(retry_if_exception_type(et))
  795             else:
  796                 conditions.append(retry_if_exception_type(error_type))
  797         if error_message_pattern is not None:
  798             conditions.append(retry_if_exception_message(match=error_message_pattern))
  799 
  800         if not conditions:
  801             raise ValueError("Either error_type or retry_condition must be provided.")
  802 
  803         # Combine all conditions using logical OR
  804         retry_policy = reduce(operator.or_, conditions)
  805 
  806         @retry(
  807             wait=wait_random_exponential(min=min_wait, max=max_wait),
  808             retry=retry_policy,
  809             before_sleep=lambda retry_state: print(
  810                 f"Attempt {retry_state.attempt_number} failed. "
  811                 f"Sleeping for {retry_state.next_action.sleep:.2f} seconds before retrying... "
  812                 f"Error: {retry_state.outcome.exception()}"
  813             ),
  814             **kwargs,
  815         )
  816         def wrapped(*args, **inner_kwargs):
  817             return func(*args, **inner_kwargs)
  818 
  819         return wrapped
  820 
  821     return decorator

   10 def extract_test_category(input_string: Union[str, Path]) -> str:
   11     input_string = str(input_string)
   12     pattern = rf".*{VERSION_PREFIX}_(\w+?)(?:_unused)?(?:_score|_result)?\.json"
   13     match = re.search(pattern, input_string)
   14 
   15     # Check if there's a match and extract the captured group
   16     if match:
   17         return match.group(1)  # the first captured group (\w+)
   18     else:
   19         raise ValueError(
   20             f"Could not extract the test category from the input string: {input_string}"
   21         )

   28 def find_file_with_suffix(folder_path: Path, suffix: str) -> Path:
   29     for json_file in folder_path.glob("*.json"):
   30         if extract_test_category(json_file) == suffix:
   31             return json_file
   32     raise FileNotFoundError(f"No JSON file found with suffix: {suffix}")

   71 def load_file(file_path, sort_by_id=False):
   72     result = []
   73     with open(file_path) as f:
   74         file = f.readlines()
   75         for line in file:
   76             result.append(json.loads(line))
   77 
   78     if sort_by_id:
   79         result.sort(key=sort_key)
   80     return result

   83 def write_list_of_dicts_to_file(filename, data, subdir=None):
   84     if subdir:
   85         # Ensure the subdirectory exists
   86         os.makedirs(subdir, exist_ok=True)
   87 
   88         # Construct the full path to the file
   89         filename = os.path.join(subdir, filename)
   90 
   91     # Write the list of dictionaries to the file in JSON format
   92     with open(filename, "w") as f:
   93         for i, entry in enumerate(data):
   94             # Go through each key-value pair in the dictionary to make sure the values are JSON serializable
   95             entry = make_json_serializable(entry)
   96             json_str = json.dumps(entry)
   97             f.write(json_str)
   98             if i < len(data) - 1:
   99                 f.write("\n")
  100 
  101 
  102 def make_json_serializable(value):
  103     if isinstance(value, dict):
  104         # If the value is a dictionary, we need to go through each key-value pair recursively
  105         return {k: make_json_serializable(v) for k, v in value.items()}
  106     elif isinstance(value, list):
  107         # If the value is a list, we need to process each element recursively
  108         return [make_json_serializable(item) for item in value]
  109     else:
  110         # Try to serialize the value directly, and if it fails, convert it to a string
  111         try:
  112             json.dumps(value)
  113             return value
  114         except (TypeError, ValueError):
  115             return str(value)
  116 
  117 
  118 def sort_key(entry):
  119     """
  120     Index comes in two forms: TestCategory_Index or TestCategory_Index-FuncDocSubIndex-PromptSubIndex; both 0-indexed.
  121 
  122     TestCategory_Index: For example, `simple_20` means the 21st entry in the `simple` test category.
  123 
  124     TestCategory_Index-FuncDocSubIndex-PromptSubIndex is used when there are multiple prompts for a single function doc; this only happens in the live dataset.
  125     FuncDocSubIndex increments for each unique function doc.
  126     PromptSubIndex is per function doc. It resets to 0 for each function doc.
  127         For example, `live_simple_19-3-15` means the 20th entry in the `live_simple` test category.
  128         This entry has the 4th unique function doc and the 16th prompt for that function doc (there are at least 15 other prompts for this same function doc in this category).
  129 
  130     In either case, the universal index is enough to sort the entries.
  131     """
  132     parts = entry["id"].rsplit("_", 1)
  133     test_category, index = parts[0], parts[1]
  134     # This handles the case where the index is in the form TestCategory_Index-FuncDocSubIndex-PromptSubIndex
  135     if "-" in index:
  136         index = index.split("-")[0]
  137     return (test_category, int(index))
  138 
  139 
  140 def is_function_calling_format_output(decoded_output):
  141     """
  142     Ensure the output is a list of dictionaries of the form:
  143     `[{func1: {param1: val1, param2: val2, ...}}, {func2: {param1: val1, param2: val2, ...}}, ...]`
  144     Sometimes the model handler's `decode_ast` method will return successfully, but the output is not in the correct format, and that will mess up the downstream evaluation that expects this format.
  145     This is especially the case when the model doesn't predict any function calls, and the output is an human-readable string.
  146     Note: Empty list `[]` is considered the correct format in this check.
  147     """
  148     if type(decoded_output) != list:
  149         return False
  150     for item in decoded_output:
  151         if type(item) != dict:
  152             return False
  153         # Check for `{func1: {param1: val1, param2: val2, ...}}`, should only have one key-value pair
  154         if len(item) != 1:
  155             return False
  156         # Check for `{param1: val1, param2: val2, ...}`; the parameter-value pairs should be a dictionary
  157         if type(list(item.values())[0]) != dict:
  158             return False
  159     return True
  160 
  161 
  162 def is_executable_format_output(decoded_output):
  163     # Ensure the output is a list of strings (one or more strings)
  164     if type(decoded_output) == list:
  165         if len(decoded_output) == 0:
  166             return False
  167         for item in decoded_output:
  168             if type(item) != str:
  169                 return False
  170         return True
  171     return False
  172 
  173 
  174 def is_empty_output(decoded_output):
  175     # This function is a patch to the ast decoder for relevance detection
  176     # Sometimes the ast decoder will parse successfully, but the input doens't really have a function call
  177     # [], [{}], and anything that is not in function calling format is considered empty (and thus should be marked as correct)
  178     if not is_function_calling_format_output(decoded_output):
  179         return True
  180     if len(decoded_output) == 0:
  181         return True
  182     if len(decoded_output) == 1 and len(decoded_output[0]) == 0:
  183         return True
  184     return False
  185 
  186 
  187 def parse_test_category_argument(test_category_args):
  188     test_name_total = set()
  189     test_filename_total = set()
  190 
  191     for test_category in test_category_args:
  192         if test_category in TEST_COLLECTION_MAPPING:
  193             for test_name in TEST_COLLECTION_MAPPING[test_category]:
  194                 test_name_total.add(test_name)
  195                 test_filename_total.add(TEST_FILE_MAPPING[test_name])
  196         elif test_category in TEST_FILE_MAPPING:
  197             test_name_total.add(test_category)
  198             test_filename_total.add(TEST_FILE_MAPPING[test_category])
  199         else:
  200             # Invalid test category name
  201             raise Exception(f"Invalid test category name provided: {test_category}")
  202 
  203     return sorted(list(test_filename_total)), sorted(list(test_name_total))

FILE source/chess/searchless_chess/src/bagz.py
    1 # Copyright 2025 DeepMind Technologies Limited
    2 #
    3 # Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0 (the "License");
    4 # you may not use this file except in compliance with the License.
    5 # You may obtain a copy of the License at
    6 #
    7 #    http://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0
    8 #
    9 # Unless required by applicable law or agreed to in writing, software
   10 # distributed under the License is distributed on an "AS IS" BASIS,
   11 # WITHOUT WARRANTIES OR CONDITIONS OF ANY KIND, either express or implied.
   12 # See the License for the specific language governing permissions and
   13 # limitations under the License.
   14 # ==============================================================================
   15 
   16 """Bagz file reader/writer and PyGrain-compatible data source for POSIX systems.
   17 
   18 Bagz is a file format for storing a sequence of string records, typically
   19 serialised protocol buffers. It supports fast index based look-up.
   20 """
   21 
   22 import bisect
   23 from collections.abc import Sequence
   24 import itertools
   25 import mmap
   26 import os
   27 import re
   28 import shutil
   29 import struct
   30 from typing import Any, SupportsIndex
   31 
   32 from etils import epath
   33 from typing_extensions import Self
   34 import zstandard as zstd
   35 
   36 
   37 class BagFileReader(Sequence[bytes]):
   38   """Reader for single Bagz files."""
   39 
   40   def __init__(
   41       self,
   42       filename: str,
   43       *,
   44       separate_limits: bool = False,
   45       decompress: bool | None = None,
   46   ) -> None:
   47     """Creates a BagFileReader.
   48 
   49     Args:
   50       filename: The name of the single Bagz file to read.
   51       separate_limits: Whether the limits are stored in a separate file.
   52       decompress: Whether to decompress the records. If None, uses the file
   53         extension to determine whether to decompress.
   54     """
   55     if decompress or (decompress is None and filename.endswith('.bagz')):
   56       self._process = lambda x: zstd.decompress(x) if x else x
   57     else:
   58       self._process = lambda x: x
   59     self._filename = filename
   60     fd = os.open(filename, os.O_RDONLY)
   61     try:
   62       self._records = mmap.mmap(fd, 0, access=mmap.ACCESS_READ)
   63       file_size = self._records.size()
   64     except ValueError:
   65       self._records = b''
   66       file_size = 0
   67     finally:
   68       os.close(fd)
   69     if separate_limits:
   70       directory, name = os.path.split(filename)
   71       fd = os.open(os.path.join(directory, 'limits.' + name), os.O_RDONLY)
   72       try:
   73         self._limits = mmap.mmap(fd, 0, access=mmap.ACCESS_READ)
   74         index_size = self._limits.size()
   75       except ValueError:
   76         self._limits = b''
   77         index_size = 0
   78       finally:
   79         os.close(fd)
   80       index_start = 0
   81     else:
   82       if 0 < file_size < 8:
   83         raise ValueError('Bagz file too small')
   84       self._limits = self._records
   85       if file_size:
   86         (index_start,) = struct.unpack('<Q', self._records[-8:])
   87       else:
   88         index_start = 0
   89       assert file_size >= index_start
   90       index_size = file_size - index_start
   91     assert index_size % 8 == 0
   92     self._num_records = index_size // 8
   93     self._limits_start = index_start
   94 
   95   def __len__(self) -> int:
   96     """Returns the number of records in the Bagz file."""
   97     return self._num_records
   98 
   99   def __getitem__(self, index: SupportsIndex) -> bytes:
  100     """Returns a record from the Bagz file."""
  101     i = index.__index__()
  102     if not 0 <= i < self._num_records:
  103       raise IndexError('bagz.BragReader index out of range')
  104     end = i * 8 + self._limits_start
  105     if i:
  106       rec_range = struct.unpack('<2q', self._limits[end - 8 : end + 8])
  107     else:
  108       rec_range = (0, *struct.unpack('<q', self._limits[end : end + 8]))
  109     return self._process(self._records[slice(*rec_range)])
  110 
  111 
  112 class BagShardReader(Sequence[bytes]):
  113   """Reader for sharded Bagz files."""
  114 
  115   def __init__(
  116       self,
  117       filename: str,
  118       *,
  119       separate_limits: bool = False,
  120       decompress: bool | None = None,
  121   ) -> None:
  122     """Creates a BagShardReader.
  123 
  124     Args:
  125       filename: The name of the sharded Bagz file to read.
  126       separate_limits: Whether the limits are stored in a separate file.
  127       decompress: Whether to decompress the records. If None, uses the file
  128         extension to determine whether to decompress.
  129     """
  130     matches = re.findall(r'@(\d+)', filename)
  131     assert len(matches) == 1
  132     num_files = int(matches[0])
  133     assert num_files < 100_000
  134     self._bags = tuple(
  135         BagFileReader(
  136             filename=re.sub(
  137                 r'@(\d+)', f'-{idx:05d}-of-{num_files:05d}', filename
  138             ),
  139             separate_limits=separate_limits,
  140             decompress=decompress,
  141         )
  142         for idx in range(num_files)
  143     )
  144     self._accum = tuple(itertools.accumulate(map(len, self._bags)))
  145 
  146   def __len__(self) -> int:
  147     """Returns the number of records in the Bagz file."""
  148     return self._accum[-1]
  149 
  150   def __getitem__(self, index: int) -> bytes:
  151     if index < 0:
  152       index += self._accum[-1]
  153     if seqn := bisect.bisect_left(self._accum, index + 1):
  154       index -= self._accum[seqn - 1]
  155     return self._bags[seqn][index]
  156 
  157 
  158 class BagReader(Sequence[bytes]):
  159   """Reader for Bagz files."""
  160 
  161   def __init__(
  162       self,
  163       filename: str,
  164       *,
  165       separate_limits: bool = False,
  166       decompress: bool | None = None,
  167   ) -> None:
  168     """Creates a BagReader.
  169 
  170     Args:
  171       filename: The name of the Bagz file to read. Supports the @N shard syntax
  172         (where @0 corresponds to the single file case). If the shard syntax does
  173         not parse, then `filename` is treated as a single file.
  174       separate_limits: Whether the limits are stored in a separate file.
  175       decompress: Whether to decompress the records. If None, uses the file
  176         extension to determine whether to decompress.
  177     """
  178     if matches := re.findall(r'@(\d+)', filename):
  179       assert len(matches) == 1
  180       if int(matches[0]) != '0':
  181         reader_class = BagShardReader
  182       else:
  183         filename = filename.replace(matches[0], '')
  184         reader_class = BagFileReader
  185     else:
  186       reader_class = BagFileReader
  187 
  188     self._reader = reader_class(
  189         filename=filename,
  190         separate_limits=separate_limits,
  191         decompress=decompress,
  192     )
  193 
  194   def __len__(self) -> int:
  195     """Returns the number of records in the Bagz file."""
  196     return len(self._reader)
  197 
  198   def __getitem__(self, index: SupportsIndex) -> bytes:
  199     """Returns a record from the Bagz file."""
  200     return self._reader[index]
  201 
  202 
  203 class BagWriter:
  204   """Writer for Bagz files."""
  205 
  206   def __init__(
  207       self,
  208       filename: str,
  209       *,
  210       separate_limits: bool = False,
  211       compress: bool | None = None,
  212       compression_level: int = 0,
  213   ) -> None:
  214     """Creates a BagWriter.
  215 
  216     Args:
  217       filename: The name of the Bagz file to write.
  218       separate_limits: Whether to keep the limits in a separate file.
  219       compress: Whether to compress the records. If None, uses the file
  220         extension to determine whether to compress.
  221       compression_level: The compression level to use when compressing.
  222     """
  223     if compress or (compress is None and filename.endswith('.bagz')):
  224       self._process = zstd.ZstdCompressor(level=compression_level).compress
  225     else:
  226       self._process = lambda x: x
  227     self._separate_limits = separate_limits
  228     directory, name = os.path.split(filename)
  229     self._records = open(filename, 'wb')
  230     self._limits = open(os.path.join(directory, 'limits.' + name), 'wb+')
  231 
  232   def write(self, data: bytes) -> None:
  233     """Writes a record to the Bagz file."""
  234     if data:
  235       self._records.write(self._process(data))
  236     self._limits.write(struct.pack('<q', self._records.tell()))
  237 
  238   def flush(self) -> None:
  239     """Flushes the Bagz file."""
  240     self._records.flush()
  241     self._limits.flush()
  242 
  243   def __enter__(self) -> Self:
  244     return self
  245 
  246   def __exit__(self, exc_type, exc_value, traceback) -> None:
  247     """Ensures the Bagz file is closed when exiting a context."""
  248     self.close()
  249 
  250   def close(self) -> None:
  251     """Concatenates the limits file to the end of the data file."""
  252     if self._separate_limits:
  253       self._records.close()
  254       self._limits.close()
  255     else:
  256       self._limits.seek(0)
  257       shutil.copyfileobj(self._limits, self._records)
  258       self._records.close()
  259       os.unlink(self._limits.name)
  260       self._limits.close()
  261 
  262 
  263 class BagDataSource:
  264   """PyGrain-compatible data source for bagz files."""
  265 
  266   def __init__(self, path: epath.PathLike) -> None:
  267     """Creates a new BagDataSource object.
  268 
  269     Args:
  270       path: The path to the bag file.
  271     """
  272     self._path = os.fspath(path)
  273     self._reader = BagReader(self._path)
  274     self._num_records = len(self._reader)
  275 
  276   def __len__(self) -> int:
  277     return self._num_records
  278 
  279   def __getitem__(self, record_key: SupportsIndex) -> bytes:
  280     return self._reader[record_key]
  281 
  282   def __getstate__(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
  283     state = self.__dict__.copy()
  284     del state['_reader']
  285     return state
  286 
  287   def __setstate__(self, state) -> None:
  288     self.__dict__.update(state)
  289     self._reader = BagReader(self._path)
  290 
  291   def __repr__(self) -> str:
  292     return f'BagDataSource(path={self._path!r}'

   15 
   16 """Defines the configuration dataclasses."""
   17 
   18 import dataclasses
   19 from typing import Literal
   20 
   21 
   22 PolicyType = Literal['action_value', 'state_value', 'behavioral_cloning']
   23 POLICY_TYPES = ['action_value', 'state_value', 'behavioral_cloning']
   24 
   25 
   26 @dataclasses.dataclass(kw_only=True)
   27 class DataConfig:
   28   """Config for the data generation."""
   29 
   30   # The batch size for the sequences.
   31   batch_size: int
   32   # Whether to shuffle the dataset (shuffling is applied per epoch).
   33   shuffle: bool = False
   34   # The seed used for shuffling and transformations of the data.
   35   seed: int | None = 0
   36   # Whether to drop partial batches.
   37   drop_remainder: bool = False
   38   # The number of child processes launched to parallelize the transformations.
   39   worker_count: int | None = 0
   40   # The number of return buckets.
   41   num_return_buckets: int
   42   # The dataset split.
   43   split: Literal['train', 'test']
   44   # The policy used to create the dataset.
   45   policy: PolicyType
   46   # The number of records to read from the dataset (can be useful when, e.g.,
   47   # the dataset does not fit into memory).
   48   num_records: int | None = None
   49 
   50 
   51 @dataclasses.dataclass(kw_only=True)
   52 class TrainConfig:
   53   """Config for the training function."""
   54 
   55   # The data configuration for training.
   56   data: DataConfig
   57   # The learning rate for Adam.
   58   learning_rate: float
   59   # The gradient clipping value.
   60   max_grad_norm: float = 1.0
   61   # The number of gradient steps.
   62   num_steps: int
   63   # The frequency (in gradient steps) at which checkpoints should be saved
   64   # (`None` means there is no checkpointing).
   65   ckpt_frequency: int | None = None
   66   # If provided, the maximum number of checkpoints to keep.
   67   ckpt_max_to_keep: int | None = 1
   68   # The frequency (in gradient steps) at which checkpoints should be saved
   69   # permanently (`None` means all checkpoints are temporary).
   70   save_frequency: int | None = None
   71   # The frequency of logging in gradient steps (`None` means no logging).
   72   log_frequency: int | None = None
   73 
   74 
   75 @dataclasses.dataclass(kw_only=True)
   76 class EvalConfig:
   77   """Config for the evaluator."""
   78 
   79   # The data configuration for evaluation.
   80   data: DataConfig
   81   # How many data points to consider for evaluation.
   82   num_eval_data: int | None = None
   83   # Enables use of ema-ed params in eval.
   84   use_ema_params: bool = False
   85   # The policy used to play moves with the model.
   86   policy: PolicyType
   87   # The number of return buckets.
   88   num_return_buckets: int
   89   # The batch size for evaluation.
   90   batch_size: int | None = None

   15 
   16 """Constants, interfaces, and types."""
   17 
   18 import abc
   19 from collections.abc import Callable, Mapping
   20 import dataclasses
   21 from typing import Any, NamedTuple, Protocol
   22 
   23 from apache_beam import coders
   24 from grain import python as pygrain
   25 import haiku as hk
   26 import jaxtyping as jtp
   27 
   28 from searchless_chess.src import config as config_lib
   29 
   30 
   31 # Integer sequences of token ids.
   32 Sequences = jtp.UInt32[jtp.Array, 'B T']
   33 
   34 # The predictions are log-probabilities (natural logarithm) for the passed
   35 # sequences. It can either be marginal log-probabilities (i.e. log P(s) for all
   36 # sequences s in the batch), or full conditionals (i.e. log P(token | s_<t) for
   37 # all sequence s, time t and token in the alphabet).
   38 Marginals = jtp.Float32[jtp.Array, '*B']
   39 Conditionals = jtp.Float32[jtp.Array, '*B T F']
   40 Predictions = Marginals | Conditionals
   41 
   42 # True means the loss will be masked there, i.e. we ignore it.
   43 LossMask = jtp.Bool[jtp.Array, 'B T']
   44 
   45 
   46 @dataclasses.dataclass
   47 class Predictor:
   48   """Defines the predictor interface."""
   49 
   50   initial_params: Callable[..., hk.MutableParams]
   51   predict: Callable[..., Predictions]
   52 
   53 
   54 class DataLoaderBuilder(Protocol):
   55 
   56   def __call__(self, config: config_lib.DataConfig) -> pygrain.DataLoader:
   57     """Returns a PyGrain data loader from the `config`."""
   58 
   59 
   60 class Evaluator(abc.ABC):
   61   """Defines the interface of the evaluator that evaluates a predictor."""
   62 
   63   @abc.abstractmethod
   64   def step(self, params: hk.Params, step: int) -> Mapping[str, Any]:
   65     """Returns the results of evaluating the predictor with `params`."""
   66 
   67 
   68 class EvaluatorBuilder(Protocol):
   69 
   70   def __call__(
   71       self,
   72       predictor: Predictor,
   73       config: config_lib.EvalConfig,
   74   ) -> Evaluator:
   75     """Returns an evaluator for the `predictor` and `config`.
   76 
   77     Args:
   78       predictor: The predictor to be evaluated. The training loop continuously
   79         saves the predictor's parameters, which are then loaded in the
   80         evaluation loop and passed to the evaluator's step method.
   81       config: The configuration of the evaluator.
   82     """
   83 
   84 
   85 CODERS = {
   86     'fen': coders.StrUtf8Coder(),
   87     'move': coders.StrUtf8Coder(),
   88     'count': coders.BigIntegerCoder(),
   89     'win_prob': coders.FloatCoder(),
   90 }
   91 CODERS['state_value'] = coders.TupleCoder((
   92     CODERS['fen'],
   93     CODERS['win_prob'],
   94 ))
   95 CODERS['action_value'] = coders.TupleCoder((
   96     CODERS['fen'],
   97     CODERS['move'],
   98     CODERS['win_prob'],
   99 ))
  100 CODERS['behavioral_cloning'] = coders.TupleCoder((
  101     CODERS['fen'],
  102     CODERS['move'],
  103 ))
  104 
  105 
  106 class BehavioralCloningData(NamedTuple):
  107   fen: str
  108   move: str
  109 
  110 
  111 class StateValueData(NamedTuple):
  112   fen: str
  113   win_prob: float
  114 
  115 
  116 class ActionValueData(NamedTuple):
  117   fen: str
  118   move: str
  119   win_prob: float

FILE source/chess/searchless_chess/src/data_loader.py
    1 # Copyright 2025 DeepMind Technologies Limited
    2 #
    3 # Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0 (the "License");
    4 # you may not use this file except in compliance with the License.
    5 # You may obtain a copy of the License at
    6 #
    7 #    http://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0
    8 #
    9 # Unless required by applicable law or agreed to in writing, software
   10 # distributed under the License is distributed on an "AS IS" BASIS,
   11 # WITHOUT WARRANTIES OR CONDITIONS OF ANY KIND, either express or implied.
   12 # See the License for the specific language governing permissions and
   13 # limitations under the License.
   14 # ==============================================================================
   15 
   16 """Implements a PyGrain DataLoader for chess data."""
   17 
   18 import abc
   19 import os
   20 
   21 import grain.python as pygrain
   22 import jax
   23 import numpy as np
   24 
   25 from searchless_chess.src import bagz
   26 from searchless_chess.src import config as config_lib
   27 from searchless_chess.src import constants
   28 from searchless_chess.src import tokenizer
   29 from searchless_chess.src import utils
   30 
   31 
   32 def _process_fen(fen: str) -> np.ndarray:
   33   return tokenizer.tokenize(fen).astype(np.int32)
   34 
   35 
   36 def _process_move(move: str) -> np.ndarray:
   37   return np.asarray([utils.MOVE_TO_ACTION[move]], dtype=np.int32)
   38 
   39 
   40 def _process_win_prob(
   41     win_prob: float,
   42     return_buckets_edges: np.ndarray,
   43 ) -> np.ndarray:
   44   return utils.compute_return_buckets_from_returns(
   45       returns=np.asarray([win_prob]),
   46       bins_edges=return_buckets_edges,
   47   )
   48 
   49 
   50 class ConvertToSequence(pygrain.MapTransform, abc.ABC):
   51   """Base class for converting chess data to a sequence of integers."""
   52 
   53   def __init__(self, num_return_buckets: int) -> None:
   54     super().__init__()
   55     self._return_buckets_edges, _ = utils.get_uniform_buckets_edges_values(
   56         num_return_buckets,
   57     )
   58     # The loss mask ensures that we only train on the return bucket.
   59     self._loss_mask = np.full(
   60         shape=(self._sequence_length,),
   61         fill_value=True,
   62         dtype=bool,
   63     )
   64     self._loss_mask[-1] = False
   65 
   66   @property
   67   @abc.abstractmethod
   68   def _sequence_length(self) -> int:
   69     raise NotImplementedError()
   70 
   71 
   72 class ConvertBehavioralCloningDataToSequence(ConvertToSequence):
   73   """Converts the fen, move, and win probability into a sequence of integers."""
   74 
   75   @property
   76   def _sequence_length(self) -> int:
   77     return tokenizer.SEQUENCE_LENGTH + 1  # (s) + (a)
   78 
   79   def map(
   80       self, element: bytes
   81   ) -> tuple[constants.Sequences, constants.LossMask]:
   82     fen, move = constants.CODERS['behavioral_cloning'].decode(element)
   83     state = _process_fen(fen)
   84     action = _process_move(move)
   85     sequence = np.concatenate([state, action])
   86     return sequence, self._loss_mask
   87 
   88 
   89 class ConvertStateValueDataToSequence(ConvertToSequence):
   90   """Converts the fen, move, and win probability into a sequence of integers."""
   91 
   92   @property
   93   def _sequence_length(self) -> int:
   94     return tokenizer.SEQUENCE_LENGTH + 1  # (s) +  (r)
   95 
   96   def map(
   97       self, element: bytes
   98   ) -> tuple[constants.Sequences, constants.LossMask]:
   99     fen, win_prob = constants.CODERS['state_value'].decode(element)
  100     state = _process_fen(fen)
  101     return_bucket = _process_win_prob(win_prob, self._return_buckets_edges)
  102     sequence = np.concatenate([state, return_bucket])
  103     return sequence, self._loss_mask
  104 
  105 
  106 class ConvertActionValueDataToSequence(ConvertToSequence):
  107   """Converts the fen, move, and win probability into a sequence of integers."""
  108 
  109   @property
  110   def _sequence_length(self) -> int:
  111     return tokenizer.SEQUENCE_LENGTH + 2  # (s) + (a) + (r)
  112 
  113   def map(
  114       self, element: bytes
  115   ) -> tuple[constants.Sequences, constants.LossMask]:
  116     fen, move, win_prob = constants.CODERS['action_value'].decode(element)
  117     state = _process_fen(fen)
  118     action = _process_move(move)
  119     return_bucket = _process_win_prob(win_prob, self._return_buckets_edges)
  120     sequence = np.concatenate([state, action, return_bucket])
  121     return sequence, self._loss_mask
  122 
  123 
  124 _TRANSFORMATION_BY_POLICY = {
  125     'behavioral_cloning': ConvertBehavioralCloningDataToSequence,
  126     'action_value': ConvertActionValueDataToSequence,
  127     'state_value': ConvertStateValueDataToSequence,
  128 }
  129 
  130 
  131 # Follows the base_constants.DataLoaderBuilder protocol.
  132 def build_data_loader(config: config_lib.DataConfig) -> pygrain.DataLoader:
  133   """Returns a data loader for chess from the config."""
  134   data_source = bagz.BagDataSource(
  135       os.path.join(
  136           os.getcwd(),
  137           f'../data/{config.split}/{config.policy}_data.bag',
  138       ),
  139   )
  140 
  141   if config.num_records is not None:
  142     num_records = config.num_records
  143     if len(data_source) < num_records:
  144       raise ValueError(
  145           f'[Process {jax.process_index()}]: The number of records requested'
  146           f' ({num_records}) is larger than the dataset ({len(data_source)}).'
  147       )
  148   else:
  149     num_records = len(data_source)
  150 
  151   sampler = pygrain.IndexSampler(
  152       num_records=num_records,
  153       shard_options=pygrain.NoSharding(),
  154       shuffle=config.shuffle,
  155       num_epochs=None,
  156       seed=config.seed,
  157   )
  158   transformations = (
  159       _TRANSFORMATION_BY_POLICY[config.policy](
  160           num_return_buckets=config.num_return_buckets
  161       ),
  162       pygrain.Batch(config.batch_size, drop_remainder=True),
  163   )
  164   return pygrain.DataLoader(
  165       data_source=data_source,
  166       sampler=sampler,
  167       operations=transformations,
  168       worker_count=config.worker_count,
  169       read_options=None,
  170   )

   15 
   16 """Constants for the engines."""
   17 
   18 import functools
   19 import os
   20 
   21 import chess
   22 import chess.engine
   23 import chess.pgn
   24 from jax import random as jrandom
   25 import numpy as np
   26 
   27 from searchless_chess.src import tokenizer
   28 from searchless_chess.src import training_utils
   29 from searchless_chess.src import transformer
   30 from searchless_chess.src import utils
   31 from searchless_chess.src.engines import lc0_engine
   32 from searchless_chess.src.engines import neural_engines
   33 from searchless_chess.src.engines import stockfish_engine
   34 
   35 
   36 def _build_neural_engine(
   37     model_name: str,
   38     checkpoint_step: int = -1,
   39 ) -> neural_engines.NeuralEngine:
   40   """Returns a neural engine."""
   41 
   42   match model_name:
   43     case '9M':
   44       policy = 'action_value'
   45       num_layers = 8
   46       embedding_dim = 256
   47       num_heads = 8
   48     case '136M':
   49       policy = 'action_value'
   50       num_layers = 8
   51       embedding_dim = 1024
   52       num_heads = 8
   53     case '270M':
   54       policy = 'action_value'
   55       num_layers = 16
   56       embedding_dim = 1024
   57       num_heads = 8
   58     case 'local':
   59       policy = 'action_value'
   60       num_layers = 4
   61       embedding_dim = 64
   62       num_heads = 4
   63     case _:
   64       raise ValueError(f'Unknown model: {model_name}')
   65 
   66   num_return_buckets = 128
   67 
   68   match policy:
   69     case 'action_value':
   70       output_size = num_return_buckets
   71     case 'behavioral_cloning':
   72       output_size = utils.NUM_ACTIONS
   73     case 'state_value':
   74       output_size = num_return_buckets
   75 
   76   predictor_config = transformer.TransformerConfig(
   77       vocab_size=utils.NUM_ACTIONS,
   78       output_size=output_size,
   79       pos_encodings=transformer.PositionalEncodings.LEARNED,
   80       max_sequence_length=tokenizer.SEQUENCE_LENGTH + 2,
   81       num_heads=num_heads,
   82       num_layers=num_layers,
   83       embedding_dim=embedding_dim,
   84       apply_post_ln=True,
   85       apply_qk_layernorm=False,
   86       use_causal_mask=False,
   87   )
   88 
   89   predictor = transformer.build_transformer_predictor(config=predictor_config)
   90   checkpoint_dir = os.path.join(
   91       os.getcwd(),
   92       f'../checkpoints/{model_name}',
   93   )
   94   params = training_utils.load_parameters(
   95       checkpoint_dir=checkpoint_dir,
   96       params=predictor.initial_params(
   97           rng=jrandom.PRNGKey(1),
   98           targets=np.ones((1, 1), dtype=np.uint32),
   99       ),
  100       step=checkpoint_step,
  101   )
  102   _, return_buckets_values = utils.get_uniform_buckets_edges_values(
  103       num_return_buckets
  104   )
  105   return neural_engines.ENGINE_FROM_POLICY[policy](
  106       return_buckets_values=return_buckets_values,
  107       predict_fn=neural_engines.wrap_predict_fn(
  108           predictor=predictor,
  109           params=params,
  110           batch_size=1,
  111       ),
  112   )
  113 
  114 
  115 ENGINE_BUILDERS = {
  116     'local': functools.partial(_build_neural_engine, model_name='local'),
  117     '9M': functools.partial(
  118         _build_neural_engine, model_name='9M', checkpoint_step=6_400_000
  119     ),
  120     '136M': functools.partial(
  121         _build_neural_engine, model_name='136M', checkpoint_step=6_400_000
  122     ),
  123     '270M': functools.partial(
  124         _build_neural_engine, model_name='270M', checkpoint_step=6_400_000
  125     ),
  126     'stockfish': lambda: stockfish_engine.StockfishEngine(
  127         limit=chess.engine.Limit(time=0.05)
  128     ),
  129     'stockfish_all_moves': lambda: stockfish_engine.AllMovesStockfishEngine(
  130         limit=chess.engine.Limit(time=0.05)
  131     ),
  132     'leela_chess_zero_depth_1': lambda: lc0_engine.AllMovesLc0Engine(
  133         limit=chess.engine.Limit(nodes=1),
  134     ),
  135     'leela_chess_zero_policy_net': lambda: lc0_engine.Lc0Engine(
  136         limit=chess.engine.Limit(nodes=1),
  137     ),
  138     'leela_chess_zero_400_sims': lambda: lc0_engine.Lc0Engine(
  139         limit=chess.engine.Limit(nodes=400),
  140     ),
  141 }

   15 
   16 """Defines the Engine interface."""
   17 
   18 from collections.abc import Mapping, Sequence
   19 from typing import Any, Protocol
   20 
   21 import chess
   22 
   23 from searchless_chess.src import utils
   24 
   25 AnalysisResult = Mapping[str, Any]
   26 
   27 
   28 def get_ordered_legal_moves(board: chess.Board) -> Sequence[chess.Move]:
   29   """Returns legal moves ordered by action value."""
   30   return sorted(board.legal_moves, key=lambda x: utils.MOVE_TO_ACTION[x.uci()])
   31 
   32 
   33 class Engine(Protocol):
   34 
   35   def analyse(self, board: chess.Board) -> AnalysisResult:
   36     """Returns various analysis results (including output) from a model."""
   37 
   38   def play(self, board: chess.Board) -> chess.Move:
   39     """Returns the best legal move from a given board."""
