   15 
   16 """Implements a Leela Chess Zero engine."""
   17 
   18 import os
   19 
   20 import chess.engine
   21 
   22 from searchless_chess.src.engines import engine
   23 
   24 
   25 class Lc0Engine(engine.Engine):
   26   """Leela Chess Zero with the biggest available network.
   27 
   28   WARNING: This can only be used with CUDA (i.e. Nvidia GPUs) for now.
   29   """
   30 
   31   def __init__(
   32       self,
   33       limit: chess.engine.Limit,
   34   ) -> None:
   35     self._limit = limit
   36     bin_path = os.path.join(
   37         os.getcwd(),
   38         '../lc0/build/release/lc0',
   39     )
   40     # We use the biggest available network.
   41     weights_path = os.path.join(
   42         os.getcwd(),
   43         '../lc0/build/release/768x15x24h-t82-swa-7464000.pb',
   44     )
   45     options = [f'--weights={weights_path}']
   46     self._raw_engine = chess.engine.SimpleEngine.popen_uci(
   47         command=[bin_path] + options,
   48     )
   49     self._raw_engine.configure({'Threads': 1})
   50 
   51   def __del__(self) -> None:
   52     self._raw_engine.close()
   53 
   54   @property
   55   def limit(self) -> chess.engine.Limit:
   56     return self._limit
   57 
   58   def analyse(self, board: chess.Board) -> engine.AnalysisResult:
   59     """Returns various analysis results from the Lc0 engine."""
   60     outcome = board.outcome()
   61     if outcome is not None:
   62       # The game has now ended.
   63       if outcome.winner is None:
   64         score = chess.engine.Cp(0)
   65       elif outcome.winner == board.turn:
   66         score = -chess.engine.Mate(moves=0)
   67       else:
   68         score = chess.engine.Mate(moves=0)
   69       return {'score': chess.engine.PovScore(score, turn=board.turn)}
   70     return self._raw_engine.analyse(board, limit=self._limit)
   71 
   72   def play(self, board: chess.Board) -> chess.Move:
   73     """Returns the best move from the Lc0 engine."""
   74     best_move = self._raw_engine.play(board, limit=self._limit).move
   75     if best_move is None:
   76       raise ValueError('No best move found, something went wrong.')
   77     return best_move
   78 
   79 
   80 class AllMovesLc0Engine(Lc0Engine):
   81   """A version of Lc0 that evaluates all moves individually."""
   82 
   83   def analyse(self, board: chess.Board) -> engine.AnalysisResult:
   84     """Returns analysis results from Lc0."""
   85     scores = []
   86     sorted_legal_moves = engine.get_ordered_legal_moves(board)
   87     for move in sorted_legal_moves:
   88       board.push(move)
   89       results = super().analyse(board)
   90       board.pop()
   91       scores.append((move, -results['score'].relative))
   92     return {'scores': scores}
   93 
   94   def play(self, board: chess.Board) -> chess.Move:
   95     """Returns the best move from Lc0."""
   96     scores = self.analyse(board)['scores']
   97     sorted_scores = sorted(scores, key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)
   98     return sorted_scores[0][0]

FILE source/chess/searchless_chess/src/engines/neural_engines.py
    1 # Copyright 2025 DeepMind Technologies Limited
    2 #
    3 # Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0 (the "License");
    4 # you may not use this file except in compliance with the License.
    5 # You may obtain a copy of the License at
    6 #
    7 #    http://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0
    8 #
    9 # Unless required by applicable law or agreed to in writing, software
   10 # distributed under the License is distributed on an "AS IS" BASIS,
   11 # WITHOUT WARRANTIES OR CONDITIONS OF ANY KIND, either express or implied.
   12 # See the License for the specific language governing permissions and
   13 # limitations under the License.
   14 # ==============================================================================
   15 
   16 """Implements the neural engines, returning analysis metrics for input FENs."""
   17 
   18 from collections.abc import Callable, Sequence
   19 
   20 import chess
   21 import haiku as hk
   22 import jax
   23 import jax.nn as jnn
   24 import numpy as np
   25 import scipy.special
   26 
   27 from searchless_chess.src import constants
   28 from searchless_chess.src import tokenizer
   29 from searchless_chess.src import utils
   30 from searchless_chess.src.engines import engine
   31 
   32 # Input = tokenized FEN, Output = log-probs, depends on the agent.
   33 PredictFn = Callable[[np.ndarray], np.ndarray]
   34 
   35 
   36 class NeuralEngine(engine.Engine):
   37   """Base class for neural engines.
   38 
   39   Attributes:
   40     predict_fn: The function to get raw outputs from the model.
   41     temperature: For the softmax used to play moves.
   42   """
   43 
   44   def __init__(
   45       self,
   46       return_buckets_values: np.ndarray | None = None,
   47       predict_fn: PredictFn | None = None,
   48       temperature: float | None = None,
   49   ):
   50     self._return_buckets_values = return_buckets_values
   51     self.predict_fn = predict_fn
   52     self.temperature = temperature
   53     self._rng = np.random.default_rng()
   54 
   55 
   56 def _update_scores_with_repetitions(
   57     board: chess.Board,
   58     scores: np.ndarray,
   59 ) -> None:
   60   """Updates the win-probabilities for a board given possible repetitions."""
   61   sorted_legal_moves = engine.get_ordered_legal_moves(board)
   62   for i, move in enumerate(sorted_legal_moves):
   63     board.push(move)
   64     # If the move results in a draw, associate 50% win prob to it.
   65     if board.is_fivefold_repetition() or board.can_claim_threefold_repetition():
   66       scores[i] = 0.5
   67     board.pop()
   68 
   69 
   70 class ActionValueEngine(NeuralEngine):
   71   """Neural engine using a function P(r | s, a)."""
   72 
   73   def analyse(self, board: chess.Board) -> engine.AnalysisResult:
   74     """Returns buckets log-probs for each action, and FEN."""
   75     # Tokenize the legal actions.
   76     sorted_legal_moves = engine.get_ordered_legal_moves(board)
   77     legal_actions = [utils.MOVE_TO_ACTION[x.uci()] for x in sorted_legal_moves]
   78     legal_actions = np.array(legal_actions, dtype=np.int32)
   79     legal_actions = np.expand_dims(legal_actions, axis=-1)
   80     # Tokenize the return buckets.
   81     dummy_return_buckets = np.zeros((len(legal_actions), 1), dtype=np.int32)
   82     # Tokenize the board.
   83     tokenized_fen = tokenizer.tokenize(board.fen()).astype(np.int32)
   84     sequences = np.stack([tokenized_fen] * len(legal_actions))
   85     # Create the sequences.
   86     sequences = np.concatenate(
   87         [sequences, legal_actions, dummy_return_buckets],
   88         axis=1,
   89     )
   90     return {'log_probs': self.predict_fn(sequences)[:, -1], 'fen': board.fen()}
   91 
   92   def play(self, board: chess.Board) -> chess.Move:
   93     return_buckets_log_probs = self.analyse(board)['log_probs']
   94     return_buckets_probs = np.exp(return_buckets_log_probs)
   95     win_probs = np.inner(return_buckets_probs, self._return_buckets_values)
   96     _update_scores_with_repetitions(board, win_probs)
   97     sorted_legal_moves = engine.get_ordered_legal_moves(board)
   98     if self.temperature is not None:
   99       probs = scipy.special.softmax(win_probs / self.temperature, axis=-1)
  100       return self._rng.choice(sorted_legal_moves, p=probs)
  101     else:
  102       best_index = np.argmax(win_probs)
  103       return sorted_legal_moves[best_index]
  104 
  105 
  106 class StateValueEngine(NeuralEngine):
  107   """Neural engine using a function P(r | s)."""
  108 
  109   def _get_value_log_probs(
  110       self,
  111       predict_fn: PredictFn,
  112       fens: Sequence[str],
  113   ) -> np.ndarray:
  114     tokenized_fens = list(map(tokenizer.tokenize, fens))
  115     tokenized_fens = np.stack(tokenized_fens, axis=0).astype(np.int32)
  116     dummy_return_buckets = np.zeros((len(fens), 1), dtype=np.int32)
  117     sequences = np.concatenate([tokenized_fens, dummy_return_buckets], axis=1)
  118     return predict_fn(sequences)[:, -1]
  119 
  120   def analyse(self, board: chess.Board) -> engine.AnalysisResult:
  121     """Defines a policy that predicts action and action value."""
  122     current_value_log_probs = self._get_value_log_probs(
  123         self.predict_fn, [board.fen()]
  124     )[0]
  125 
  126     # We perform a search of depth 1 to get the Q-values.
  127     next_fens = []
  128     for move in engine.get_ordered_legal_moves(board):
  129       board.push(move)
  130       next_fens.append(board.fen())
  131       board.pop()
  132     next_values_log_probs = self._get_value_log_probs(
  133         self.predict_fn, next_fens
  134     )
  135     # Flip the probabilities of the return buckets as we want to compute -value.
  136     next_values_log_probs = np.flip(next_values_log_probs, axis=-1)
  137 
  138     return {
  139         'current_log_probs': current_value_log_probs,
  140         'next_log_probs': next_values_log_probs,
  141         'fen': board.fen(),
  142     }
  143 
  144   def play(self, board: chess.Board) -> chess.Move:
  145     next_log_probs = self.analyse(board)['next_log_probs']
  146     next_probs = np.exp(next_log_probs)
  147     win_probs = np.inner(next_probs, self._return_buckets_values)
  148     _update_scores_with_repetitions(board, win_probs)
  149     sorted_legal_moves = engine.get_ordered_legal_moves(board)
  150     if self.temperature is not None:
  151       probs = scipy.special.softmax(win_probs / self.temperature, axis=-1)
  152       return self._rng.choice(sorted_legal_moves, p=probs)
  153     else:
  154       best_index = np.argmax(win_probs)
  155       return sorted_legal_moves[best_index]
  156 
  157 
  158 class BCEngine(NeuralEngine):
  159   """Defines a policy that predicts action probs."""
  160 
  161   def analyse(self, board: chess.Board) -> engine.AnalysisResult:
  162     """Defines a policy that predicts action probs."""
  163     tokenized_fen = tokenizer.tokenize(board.fen()).astype(np.int32)
  164     tokenized_fen = np.expand_dims(tokenized_fen, axis=0)
  165     dummy_actions = np.zeros((1, 1), dtype=np.int32)
  166     sequences = np.concatenate([tokenized_fen, dummy_actions], axis=1)
  167     total_action_log_probs = self.predict_fn(sequences)[0, -1]
  168     assert len(total_action_log_probs) == utils.NUM_ACTIONS
  169 
  170     # We must renormalize the output distribution to only the legal moves.
  171     sorted_legal_moves = engine.get_ordered_legal_moves(board)
  172     legal_actions = [utils.MOVE_TO_ACTION[x.uci()] for x in sorted_legal_moves]
  173     legal_actions = np.array(legal_actions, dtype=np.int32)
  174     action_log_probs = total_action_log_probs[legal_actions]
  175     action_log_probs = jnn.log_softmax(action_log_probs)
  176     assert len(action_log_probs) == len(list(board.legal_moves))
  177     return {'log_probs': action_log_probs, 'fen': board.fen()}
  178 
  179   def play(self, board: chess.Board) -> chess.Move:
  180     action_log_probs = self.analyse(board)['log_probs']
  181     sorted_legal_moves = engine.get_ordered_legal_moves(board)
  182     if self.temperature is not None:
  183       probs = scipy.special.softmax(
  184           action_log_probs / self.temperature, axis=-1
  185       )
  186       return self._rng.choice(sorted_legal_moves, p=probs)
  187     else:
  188       best_index = np.argmax(action_log_probs)
  189       return sorted_legal_moves[best_index]
  190 
  191 
  192 def wrap_predict_fn(
  193     predictor: constants.Predictor,
  194     params: hk.Params,
  195     batch_size: int = 32,
  196 ) -> PredictFn:
  197   """Returns a simple prediction function from a predictor and parameters.
  198 
  199   Args:
  200     predictor: Used to predict outputs.
  201     params: Neural network parameters.
  202     batch_size: How many sequences to pass to the predictor at once.
  203   """
  204   jitted_predict_fn = jax.jit(predictor.predict)
  205 
  206   def fixed_predict_fn(sequences: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
  207     """Wrapper around the predictor `predict` function."""
  208     assert sequences.shape[0] == batch_size
  209     return jitted_predict_fn(
  210         params=params,
  211         targets=sequences,
  212         rng=None,
  213     )
  214 
  215   def predict_fn(sequences: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
  216     """Wrapper to collate batches of sequences of fixed size."""
  217     remainder = -len(sequences) % batch_size
  218     padded = np.pad(sequences, ((0, remainder), (0, 0)))
  219     sequences_split = np.split(padded, len(padded) // batch_size)
  220     all_outputs = []
  221     for sub_sequences in sequences_split:
  222       all_outputs.append(fixed_predict_fn(sub_sequences))
  223     outputs = np.concatenate(all_outputs, axis=0)
  224     assert len(outputs) == len(padded)
  225     return outputs[: len(sequences)]  # Crop the padded sequences.
  226 
  227   return predict_fn
  228 
  229 
  230 ENGINE_FROM_POLICY = {
  231     'action_value': ActionValueEngine,
  232     'state_value': StateValueEngine,
  233     'behavioral_cloning': BCEngine,
  234 }

   15 
   16 """Implements a stockfish engine."""
   17 
   18 import os
   19 
   20 import chess
   21 
   22 from searchless_chess.src.engines import engine
   23 
   24 
   25 class StockfishEngine(engine.Engine):
   26   """The classical version of stockfish."""
   27 
   28   def __init__(
   29       self,
   30       limit: chess.engine.Limit,
   31   ) -> None:
   32     self._limit = limit
   33     self._skill_level = None
   34     bin_path = os.path.join(
   35         os.getcwd(),
   36         '../Stockfish/src/stockfish',
   37     )
   38     self._raw_engine = chess.engine.SimpleEngine.popen_uci(bin_path)
   39 
   40   def __del__(self) -> None:
   41     self._raw_engine.close()
   42 
   43   @property
   44   def limit(self) -> chess.engine.Limit:
   45     return self._limit
   46 
   47   @property
   48   def skill_level(self) -> int | None:
   49     return self._skill_level
   50 
   51   @skill_level.setter
   52   def skill_level(self, skill_level: int) -> None:
   53     self._skill_level = skill_level
   54     self._raw_engine.configure({'Skill Level': self._skill_level})
   55 
   56   def analyse(self, board: chess.Board) -> engine.AnalysisResult:
   57     """Returns analysis results from stockfish."""
   58     return self._raw_engine.analyse(board, limit=self._limit)
   59 
   60   def play(self, board: chess.Board) -> chess.Move:
   61     """Returns the best move from stockfish."""
   62     best_move = self._raw_engine.play(board, limit=self._limit).move
   63     if best_move is None:
   64       raise ValueError('No best move found, something went wrong.')
   65     return best_move
   66 
   67 
   68 class AllMovesStockfishEngine(StockfishEngine):
   69   """A version of stockfish that evaluates all moves individually."""
   70 
   71   def analyse(self, board: chess.Board) -> engine.AnalysisResult:
   72     """Returns analysis results from stockfish."""
   73     scores = []
   74     sorted_legal_moves = engine.get_ordered_legal_moves(board)
   75     for move in sorted_legal_moves:
   76       results = self._raw_engine.analyse(
   77           board,
   78           limit=self._limit,
   79           root_moves=[move],
   80       )
   81       scores.append((move, results['score'].relative))
   82     return {'scores': scores}
   83 
   84   def play(self, board: chess.Board) -> chess.Move:
   85     """Returns the best move from stockfish."""
   86     scores = self.analyse(board)['scores']
   87     sorted_scores = sorted(scores, key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)
   88     return sorted_scores[0][0]

   16 """Evaluation for the Chess experiments, retrieving static metrics like losses."""
   17 
   18 import abc
   19 import collections
   20 from collections.abc import Mapping, Sequence
   21 import dataclasses
   22 import os
   23 from typing import Any
   24 
   25 from absl import logging
   26 import chess
   27 import haiku as hk
   28 import numpy as np
   29 import scipy.stats
   30 
   31 from searchless_chess.src import bagz
   32 from searchless_chess.src import config as config_lib
   33 from searchless_chess.src import constants
   34 from searchless_chess.src import utils
   35 from searchless_chess.src.engines import engine
   36 from searchless_chess.src.engines import neural_engines

   38 
   39 @dataclasses.dataclass
   40 class ChessStaticMetrics:
   41   """Metrics retrieved from a supervised chess data loader.
   42 
   43   In the following, s is the board, a are the legal actions, r is the
   44   (bucketized) win probability evaluated by Stockfish for the pair (s, a), and
   45   theta are the parameters of the agent. Note that we easily interexchange the
   46   term 'return' and 'win probability'.
   47   Also, win_prob(s, a) = E_bucket (P_theta(bucket | s, a))
   48 
   49   Attributes:
   50     fen: Example: "r1b1kbnr/pp3ppp/1qn1p3/1BppP3/3P4/5N2/PPP2PPP/RNBQK2R w KQkq
   51       - 4 6".
   52     action_accuracy: argmax Q(s, a) == a
   53     output_log_loss: * For action-value: - E_a (log_2 P_theta(r | s, a)) * For
   54       state-value: - log_2 P_theta(r | s) * For BC: - log_2 P_theta(a | s)
   55     kendall_tau:  Measuring the discrepancy between the order of actions (by
   56       Q-value) between the agent and the Stockfish reference. See
   57       https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kendall_rank_correlation_coefficient.
   58     entropy: - E_{r,a} (log_2 P_theta(r | s, a)). Similar to the log-loss, but
   59       we average over return buckets too.
   60     l2_win_prob_loss: For action-value and state-value only, E_a ((win_prob(s,
   61       a) - r)**2)
   62     consistency_loss: For state-value only, (win_prob(s) - max_{a}
   63       win_prob(s'))**2 where s' = next state from s taking action a.
   64   """
   65 
   66   fen: str
   67   action_accuracy: bool
   68   output_log_loss: float
   69   kendall_tau: float
   70   entropy: float
   71 
   72   # Only for the action-value and state-value models.
   73   l2_win_prob_loss: float | None
   74   # Only for the state-value model.
   75   consistency_loss: float | None
   76 
   77 
   78 class ChessStaticMetricsEvaluator(constants.Evaluator, abc.ABC):
   79   """Evaluator to compute various metrics (see ChessStaticMetrics)."""
   80 
   81   def __init__(
   82       self,
   83       predictor: constants.Predictor,
   84       num_return_buckets: int,
   85       dataset_path: str,
   86       batch_size: int,
   87       num_eval_data: int | None = None,
   88   ) -> None:
   89     """Initializes the evaluator.
   90 
   91     Args:
   92       predictor: To be evaluated.
   93       num_return_buckets: The number of return buckets to use.
   94       dataset_path: The path of the dataset to use.
   95       batch_size: How many sequences to pass to the predictor at once.
   96       num_eval_data: If specified, the number of data points to use for
   97         evaluation. If unspecified, all data points are used.
   98     """
   99     self._predictor = predictor
  100     self._return_buckets_edges, self._return_buckets_values = (
  101         utils.get_uniform_buckets_edges_values(num_return_buckets)
  102     )
  103     self._dataset_path = dataset_path
  104     self._batch_size = batch_size
  105 
  106     # Initialized to None, until step is called for the first time.
  107     self._test_data: dict[str, Any] = self._retrieve_test_data()
  108 
  109     if num_eval_data is not None:
  110       if len(self._test_data) < num_eval_data:
  111         raise ValueError(
  112             f'Not enough evaluation data points: {len(self._test_data)} <'
  113             f' {num_eval_data}'
  114         )
  115       self._test_data = dict(list(self._test_data.items())[:num_eval_data])
  116 
  117   def _metrics_to_filtered_dict(
  118       self, metrics: Sequence[ChessStaticMetrics]
  119   ) -> Mapping[str, np.ndarray]:
  120     """Returns a dictionary of averaged relevant metrics."""
  121     metrics_dict = {}
  122     fields = [x.name for x in dataclasses.fields(ChessStaticMetrics)]
  123     filtered_fields = filter(lambda x: x != 'fen', fields)
  124     filtered_fields = filter(
  125         lambda x: getattr(metrics[0], x) is not None,
  126         filtered_fields,
  127     )
  128     for key in filtered_fields:
  129       metrics_dict[key] = np.mean([getattr(x, key) for x in metrics])
  130     return metrics_dict
  131 
  132   def step(self, params: hk.Params, step: int) -> Mapping[str, Any]:
  133     """Returns the results of evaluating the predictor with `params`."""
  134     logging.info('Step of the metrics evaluator.')
  135     self._predict_fn = neural_engines.wrap_predict_fn(
  136         predictor=self._predictor,
  137         params=params,
  138         batch_size=self._batch_size,
  139     )
  140     logging.info('Computing metrics for %i FENs...', len(self._test_data))
  141     all_metrics = [self._compute_metrics(fen) for fen in self._test_data]
  142     logging.info('All metrics computed. Writing evals dict.')
  143 
  144     metrics_dict = self._metrics_to_filtered_dict(all_metrics)
  145     return {'eval_' + key: value for key, value in metrics_dict.items()}
  146 
  147   @abc.abstractmethod
  148   def _retrieve_test_data(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
  149     """Retrieves and returns the test data."""
  150 
  151   @abc.abstractmethod
  152   def _compute_metrics(self, fen: str) -> ChessStaticMetrics:
  153     """Returns metrics for the agent."""
  154 
  155 
  156 class ActionValueChessStaticMetricsEvaluator(ChessStaticMetricsEvaluator):
  157   """Evaluator for action value."""
  158 
  159   def _retrieve_test_data(
  160       self,
  161   ) -> dict[str, Sequence[np.ndarray]]:
  162     """Retrieves and returns the test data.
  163 
  164     Returns:
  165       - Boards represented as FEN strings.
  166       - A mapping from FEN strings (above) to a sequence of
  167       (legal action, stockfish score).
  168     """
  169     move_to_action = utils.MOVE_TO_ACTION
  170     bag_reader = bagz.BagReader(self._dataset_path)
  171 
  172     action_score_dict = collections.defaultdict(dict)
  173     for bytes_data in bag_reader:
  174       fen, move, win_prob = constants.CODERS['action_value'].decode(bytes_data)
  175       action = move_to_action[move]
  176       action_score_dict[fen][action] = win_prob
  177 
  178     to_remove = []
  179     for fen in action_score_dict:
  180       list_items = list(action_score_dict[fen].items())
  181       list_items.sort(key=lambda x: x[0])
  182       action_score_dict[fen] = np.array(list_items, dtype=np.float32)
  183 
  184       board = chess.Board(fen)
  185       legal_actions = action_score_dict[fen][:, 0].tolist()
  186       true_legal_moves = engine.get_ordered_legal_moves(board)
  187       true_legal_actions = [move_to_action[x.uci()] for x in true_legal_moves]
  188       # Check that the dataset contains the right legal actions.
  189       if true_legal_actions != legal_actions:
  190         to_remove.append(fen)
  191 
  192     fraction_removed = len(to_remove) / len(action_score_dict)
  193     for fen in to_remove:
  194       del action_score_dict[fen]
  195     logging.info('Removed %f of FENs, wrong legal actions.', fraction_removed)
  196 
  197     return dict(action_score_dict)
  198 
  199   def _compute_metrics(self, fen: str) -> ChessStaticMetrics:
  200     if not hasattr(self, '_predict_fn'):
  201       raise ValueError('Predictor is not initialized.')
  202     neural_engine = neural_engines.ActionValueEngine(
  203         self._return_buckets_values,
  204         self._predict_fn,
  205     )
  206     analysis_results = neural_engine.analyse(chess.Board(fen))
  207     return self._compute_metrics_from_analysis(analysis_results)
  208 
  209   def _compute_metrics_from_analysis(
  210       self,
  211       analysis_results: engine.AnalysisResult,
  212   ) -> ChessStaticMetrics:
  213     """Returns metrics for the action_value agent."""
  214     fen = analysis_results['fen']
  215     legal_actions_returns = self._test_data[fen][:, 1]
  216 
  217     return_buckets_log_probs = analysis_results['log_probs']
  218     return_buckets_probs = np.exp(return_buckets_log_probs)
  219 
  220     # Compute the entropy.
  221     mult_probs = return_buckets_probs * return_buckets_log_probs
  222     nat_batch_entropies = np.sum(-mult_probs, axis=-1)
  223     entropy = np.mean(nat_batch_entropies) / np.log(2)
  224 
  225     # Compute the L2 loss on centipawn scores.
  226     win_probs = np.inner(
  227         self._return_buckets_values,
  228         return_buckets_probs,
  229     )
  230     l2_return_loss = np.mean((win_probs - legal_actions_returns) ** 2)
  231 
  232     # Compute the return log loss.
  233     return_buckets = utils.compute_return_buckets_from_returns(
  234         returns=legal_actions_returns,
  235         bins_edges=self._return_buckets_edges,
  236     )
  237     true_return_log_probs = np.take_along_axis(
  238         return_buckets_log_probs, return_buckets[..., None], axis=-1
  239     )[..., 0]
  240     return_log_loss = np.mean(-true_return_log_probs / np.log(2), axis=0)
  241 
  242     # Compute the action accuracy.
  243     best_legal_actions = legal_actions_returns == np.max(legal_actions_returns)
  244     action_accuracy = best_legal_actions[np.argmax(win_probs)]
  245 
  246     # Compute the Kendall-Taus.
  247     if len(win_probs) == 1:
  248       # There is perfect agreement if only one action is available.
  249       kendall_tau = 1.0
  250     else:
  251       kendall_tau, _ = scipy.stats.kendalltau(
  252           x=np.argsort(win_probs),
  253           y=np.argsort(legal_actions_returns),
  254       )
  255 
  256     return ChessStaticMetrics(
  257         fen=fen,
  258         action_accuracy=action_accuracy,
  259         output_log_loss=return_log_loss,
  260         l2_win_prob_loss=l2_return_loss,
  261         consistency_loss=None,
  262         kendall_tau=kendall_tau,
  263         entropy=entropy,
  264     )
  265 
  266 
  267 class StateValueChessStaticMetricsEvaluator(
  268     ActionValueChessStaticMetricsEvaluator
  269 ):
  270   """Evaluator for state value."""
  271 
  272   def _compute_metrics(self, fen: str) -> ChessStaticMetrics:
  273     """Returns metrics for the action_value agent."""
  274     if not hasattr(self, '_predict_fn'):
  275       raise ValueError('Predictor is not initialized.')
  276     neural_engine = neural_engines.StateValueEngine(
  277         self._return_buckets_values,
  278         self._predict_fn,
  279     )
  280     analysis_results = neural_engine.analyse(chess.Board(fen))
  281     metrics = super()._compute_metrics_from_analysis({
  282         'log_probs': analysis_results['next_log_probs'],
  283         'fen': analysis_results['fen'],
  284     })
  285     current_win_prob = np.inner(
  286         self._return_buckets_values,
  287         np.exp(analysis_results['current_log_probs']),
  288     )
  289     next_win_probs = np.inner(
  290         self._return_buckets_values,
  291         np.exp(analysis_results['next_log_probs']),
  292     )
  293     next_win_prob = np.max(next_win_probs)
  294     metrics.consistency_loss = (current_win_prob - next_win_prob) ** 2
  295     return metrics
  296 
  297 
  298 class BCChessStaticMetricsEvaluator(ActionValueChessStaticMetricsEvaluator):
  299   """Evaluator for behavioral cloning."""
  300 
  301   def _compute_metrics(self, fen: str) -> ChessStaticMetrics:
  302     """Returns metrics for the action_value agent."""
  303     if not hasattr(self, '_predict_fn'):
  304       raise ValueError('Predictor is not initialized.')
  305     legal_actions_returns = self._test_data[fen][:, 1]
  306     best_action_index = np.argmax(legal_actions_returns)
  307 
  308     neural_engine = neural_engines.BCEngine(predict_fn=self._predict_fn)
  309     analysis_results = neural_engine.analyse(chess.Board(fen))
  310     action_log_probs = analysis_results['log_probs']
  311     action_probs = np.exp(action_log_probs)
  312 
  313     # Compute the entropy.
  314     entropy = -np.sum(action_probs * action_log_probs) / np.log(2)
  315 
  316     # Compute the action log loss.
  317     action_loss = -action_log_probs[best_action_index] / np.log(2)
  318 
  319     # Compute the action accuracy.
  320     best_legal_actions = legal_actions_returns == np.max(legal_actions_returns)
  321     action_accuracy = best_legal_actions[np.argmax(action_probs)]
  322 
  323     # Compute the Kendall-Taus.
  324     if len(action_probs) == 1:
  325       # There is perfect agreement if only one action is available.
  326       kendall_tau = 1.0
  327     else:
  328       kendall_tau, _ = scipy.stats.kendalltau(
  329           x=np.argsort(action_probs),
  330           y=np.argsort(legal_actions_returns),
  331       )
  332 
  333     return ChessStaticMetrics(
  334         fen=fen,
  335         action_accuracy=action_accuracy,
  336         output_log_loss=action_loss,
  337         l2_win_prob_loss=None,
  338         consistency_loss=None,
  339         kendall_tau=kendall_tau,
  340         entropy=entropy,
  341     )
  342 
  343 
  344 # Follows the base_constants.EvaluatorBuilder protocol.
  345 def build_evaluator(
  346     predictor: constants.Predictor,
  347     config: config_lib.EvalConfig,
  348 ) -> ChessStaticMetricsEvaluator:
  349   """Returns an evaluator from an eval config."""
  350   evaluator_by_policy = {
  351       'action_value': ActionValueChessStaticMetricsEvaluator,
  352       'state_value': StateValueChessStaticMetricsEvaluator,
  353       'behavioral_cloning': BCChessStaticMetricsEvaluator,
  354   }
  355   return evaluator_by_policy[config.policy](
  356       predictor=predictor,
  357       # We always use the action-value data for evaluation since it provides the
  358       # required information for all the metrics.
  359       dataset_path=os.path.join(
  360           os.getcwd(),
  361           f'../data/{config.data.split}/action_value_data.bag',
  362       ),
  363       num_return_buckets=config.num_return_buckets,
  364       num_eval_data=config.num_eval_data,
  365       batch_size=config.batch_size,
  366   )

    4 # you may not use this file except in compliance with the License.
    5 # You may obtain a copy of the License at

    8 #
    9 # Unless required by applicable law or agreed to in writing, software
   10 # distributed under the License is distributed on an "AS IS" BASIS,
   11 # WITHOUT WARRANTIES OR CONDITIONS OF ANY KIND, either express or implied.
   12 # See the License for the specific language governing permissions and
   13 # limitations under the License.
   14 # ==============================================================================
   15 
   16 """Evaluates engines on the puzzles dataset from lichess."""
   17 
   18 from collections.abc import Sequence
   19 import io
   20 import os
   21 
   22 from absl import app
   23 from absl import flags
   24 import chess
   25 import chess.engine
   26 import chess.pgn
   27 import pandas as pd
   28 
   29 from searchless_chess.src.engines import constants
   30 from searchless_chess.src.engines import engine as engine_lib
   31 
   32 
   33 _NUM_PUZZLES = flags.DEFINE_integer(
   34     name='num_puzzles',
   35     default=None,
   36     help='The number of puzzles to evaluate.',
   37     required=True,
   38 )
   39 _AGENT = flags.DEFINE_enum(
   40     name='agent',
   41     default=None,
   42     enum_values=[
   43         'local',
   44         '9M',
   45         '136M',
   46         '270M',
   47         'stockfish',
   48         'stockfish_all_moves',
   49         'leela_chess_zero_depth_1',
   50         'leela_chess_zero_policy_net',
   51         'leela_chess_zero_400_sims',
   52     ],
   53     help='The agent to evaluate.',
   54     required=True,
   55 )
   56 
   57 
   58 def evaluate_puzzle_from_pandas_row(
   59     puzzle: pd.Series,
   60     engine: engine_lib.Engine,
   61 ) -> bool:
   62   """Returns True if the `engine` solves the puzzle and False otherwise."""
   63   game = chess.pgn.read_game(io.StringIO(puzzle['PGN']))
   64   if game is None:
   65     raise ValueError(f'Failed to read game from PGN {puzzle["PGN"]}.')
   66   board = game.end().board()
   67   return evaluate_puzzle_from_board(
   68       board=board,
   69       moves=puzzle['Moves'].split(' '),
   70       engine=engine,
   71   )
   72 
   73 
   74 def evaluate_puzzle_from_board(
   75     board: chess.Board,
   76     moves: Sequence[str],
   77     engine: engine_lib.Engine,
   78 ) -> bool:
   79   """Returns True if the `engine` solves the puzzle and False otherwise."""
   80   for move_idx, move in enumerate(moves):
   81     # According to https://database.lichess.org/#puzzles, the FEN is the
   82     # position before the opponent makes their move. The position to present to
   83     # the player is after applying the first move to that FEN. The second move
   84     # is the beginning of the solution.
   85     if move_idx % 2 == 1:
   86       predicted_move = engine.play(board=board).uci()
   87       # Lichess puzzles consider all mate-in-1 moves as correct, so we need to
   88       # check if the `predicted_move` results in a checkmate if it differs from
   89       # the solution.
   90       if move != predicted_move:
   91         board.push(chess.Move.from_uci(predicted_move))
   92         return board.is_checkmate()
   93     board.push(chess.Move.from_uci(move))
   94   return True
   95 
   96 
   97 def main(argv: Sequence[str]) -> None:
   98   if len(argv) > 1:
   99     raise app.UsageError('Too many command-line arguments.')
  100 
  101   puzzles_path = os.path.join(
  102       os.getcwd(),
  103       '../data/puzzles.csv',
  104   )
  105   puzzles = pd.read_csv(puzzles_path, nrows=_NUM_PUZZLES.value)
  106   engine = constants.ENGINE_BUILDERS[_AGENT.value]()
  107 
  108   for puzzle_id, puzzle in puzzles.iterrows():
  109     correct = evaluate_puzzle_from_pandas_row(
  110         puzzle=puzzle,
  111         engine=engine,
  112     )
  113     print(
  114         {'puzzle_id': puzzle_id, 'correct': correct, 'rating': puzzle['Rating']}
  115     )
  116 
  117 
  118 if __name__ == '__main__':
  119   app.run(main)

   16 """Implements tokenization of FEN strings."""
   17 
   18 import jaxtyping as jtp
   19 import numpy as np
   20 
   21 
   22 # pyfmt: disable
   23 _CHARACTERS = [
   24     '0',
   25     '1',
   26     '2',
   27     '3',
   28     '4',
   29     '5',
   30     '6',
   31     '7',
   32     '8',

   34     'a',

   37     'd',
   38     'e',
   39     'f',
   40     'g',

   45     'k',
   46     'q',
   47     'P',
   48     'B',
   49     'N',
   50     'R',
   51     'Q',
   52     'K',
   53     'w',
   54     '.',
   55 ]
   56 # pyfmt: enable
   57 _CHARACTERS_INDEX = {letter: index for index, letter in enumerate(_CHARACTERS)}
   58 _SPACES_CHARACTERS = frozenset({'1', '2', '3', '4', '5', '6', '7', '8'})
   59 SEQUENCE_LENGTH = 77
   60 
   61 
   62 def tokenize(fen: str) -> jtp.Int32[jtp.Array, 'T']:
   63   """Returns an array of tokens from a fen string.
   64 
   65   We compute a tokenized representation of the board, from the FEN string.
   66   The final array of tokens is a mapping from this string to numbers, which
   67   are defined in the dictionary `_CHARACTERS_INDEX`.
   68   For the 'en passant' information, we convert the '-' (which means there is
   69   no en passant relevant square) to '..', to always have two characters, and
   70   a fixed length output.
   71 
   72   Args:
   73     fen: The board position in Forsyth-Edwards Notation.
   74   """
   75   # Extracting the relevant information from the FEN.
   76   board, side, castling, en_passant, halfmoves_last, fullmoves = fen.split(' ')
   77   board = board.replace('/', '')
   78   board = side + board
   79 
   80   indices = list()
   81 
   82   for char in board:
   83     if char in _SPACES_CHARACTERS:
   84       indices.extend(int(char) * [_CHARACTERS_INDEX['.']])
   85     else:
   86       indices.append(_CHARACTERS_INDEX[char])
   87 
   88   if castling == '-':
   89     indices.extend(4 * [_CHARACTERS_INDEX['.']])
   90   else:
   91     for char in castling:
   92       indices.append(_CHARACTERS_INDEX[char])
   93     # Padding castling to have exactly 4 characters.
   94     if len(castling) < 4:
   95       indices.extend((4 - len(castling)) * [_CHARACTERS_INDEX['.']])
   96 
   97   if en_passant == '-':
   98     indices.extend(2 * [_CHARACTERS_INDEX['.']])
   99   else:
  100     # En passant is a square like 'e3'.
  101     for char in en_passant:
  102       indices.append(_CHARACTERS_INDEX[char])
  103 
  104   # Three digits for halfmoves (since last capture) is enough since the game
  105   # ends at 50.
  106   halfmoves_last += '.' * (3 - len(halfmoves_last))
  107   indices.extend([_CHARACTERS_INDEX[x] for x in halfmoves_last])
  108 
  109   # Three digits for full moves is enough (no game lasts longer than 999
  110   # moves).
  111   fullmoves += '.' * (3 - len(fullmoves))
  112   indices.extend([_CHARACTERS_INDEX[x] for x in fullmoves])
  113 
  114   assert len(indices) == SEQUENCE_LENGTH
  115 
  116   return np.asarray(indices, dtype=np.uint8)

FILE source/chess/searchless_chess/src/tournament.py
    1 # Copyright 2025 DeepMind Technologies Limited
    2 #
    3 # Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0 (the "License");
    4 # you may not use this file except in compliance with the License.
    5 # You may obtain a copy of the License at
    6 #
    7 #    http://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0
    8 #
    9 # Unless required by applicable law or agreed to in writing, software
   10 # distributed under the License is distributed on an "AS IS" BASIS,
   11 # WITHOUT WARRANTIES OR CONDITIONS OF ANY KIND, either express or implied.
   12 # See the License for the specific language governing permissions and
   13 # limitations under the License.
   14 # ==============================================================================
   15 
   16 """Launches a tournament between various engines to compute their Elos."""
   17 
   18 from collections.abc import Mapping, Sequence
   19 import copy
   20 import datetime
   21 import itertools
   22 import os
   23 
   24 from absl import app
   25 from absl import flags
   26 import chess
   27 import chess.engine
   28 import chess.pgn
   29 import numpy as np
   30 
   31 from searchless_chess.src.engines import constants
   32 from searchless_chess.src.engines import engine
   33 from searchless_chess.src.engines import stockfish_engine
   34 
   35 
   36 _NUM_GAMES = flags.DEFINE_integer(
   37     name='num_games',
   38     default=None,
   39     help='The number of games to play between each pair of engines.',
   40     required=True,
   41 )
   42 
   43 # We use a stockfish engine to evaluate the current board and terminate the
   44 # game early if the score is high enough (i.e., _MIN_SCORE_TO_STOP).
   45 _EVAL_STOCKFISH_ENGINE = stockfish_engine.StockfishEngine(
   46     limit=chess.engine.Limit(time=0.01)
   47 )
   48 _MIN_SCORE_TO_STOP = 1300
   49 
   50 
   51 def _play_game(
   52     engines: tuple[engine.Engine, engine.Engine],
   53     engines_names: tuple[str, str],
   54     white_name: str,
   55     initial_board: chess.Board | None = None,
   56 ) -> chess.pgn.Game:
   57   """Plays a game of chess between two engines.
   58 
   59   Args:
   60     engines: The engines to play the game.
   61     engines_names: The names of the engines.
   62     white_name: The name of the engine playing white.
   63     initial_board: The initial board (if None, the standard starting position).
   64 
   65   Returns:
   66     The game played between the engines.
   67   """
   68   if initial_board is None:
   69     initial_board = chess.Board()
   70   white_player = engines_names.index(white_name)
   71   current_player = white_player if initial_board.turn else 1 - white_player
   72   board = initial_board
   73   result = None
   74   print(f'Starting FEN: {board.fen()}')
   75 
   76   while not (
   77       board.is_game_over()
   78       or board.can_claim_fifty_moves()
   79       or board.is_repetition()
   80   ):
   81     best_move = engines[current_player].play(board)
   82     print(f'Best move: {best_move.uci()}')
   83 
   84     # Push move to the game.
   85     board.push(best_move)
   86     current_player = 1 - current_player
   87 
   88     # We analyse the board once the last move is done and pushed.
   89     info = _EVAL_STOCKFISH_ENGINE.analyse(board)
   90     score = info['score'].relative
   91     if score.is_mate():
   92       is_winning = score.mate() > 0
   93     else:
   94       is_winning = score.score() > 0
   95     score_too_high = score.is_mate() or abs(score.score()) > _MIN_SCORE_TO_STOP
   96 
   97     if score_too_high:
   98       is_white = board.turn == chess.WHITE
   99       if is_white and is_winning or (not is_white and not is_winning):
  100         result = '1-0'
  101       else:
  102         result = '0-1'
  103       break
  104   print(f'End FEN: {board.fen()}')
  105 
  106   game = chess.pgn.Game.from_board(board)
  107   game.headers['Event'] = 'UAIChess'
  108   game.headers['Date'] = datetime.datetime.today().strftime('%Y.%m.%d')
  109   game.headers['White'] = white_name
  110   game.headers['Black'] = engines_names[1 - white_player]
  111   if result is not None:  # Due to early stopping.
  112     game.headers['Result'] = result
  113   else:
  114     game.headers['Result'] = board.result(claim_draw=True)
  115   return game
  116 
  117 
  118 def _run_tournament(
  119     engines: Mapping[str, engine.Engine],
  120     opening_boards: Sequence[chess.Board],
  121 ) -> Sequence[chess.pgn.Game]:
  122   """Runs a tournament between engines given openings.
  123 
  124   We play both sides for each opening, and the total number of games played per
  125   pair is therefore 2 * len(opening_boards).
  126 
  127   Args:
  128     engines: A mapping from engine names to engines.
  129     opening_boards: The boards to use as openings.
  130 
  131   Returns:
  132     The games played between all the engines.
  133   """
  134   games = list()
  135 
  136   for engine_name_0, engine_name_1 in itertools.combinations(engines, 2):
  137     print(f'Playing games between {engine_name_0} and {engine_name_1}')
  138     engine_0 = engines[engine_name_0]
  139     engine_1 = engines[engine_name_1]
  140 
  141     for opening_board, white_idx in itertools.product(opening_boards, (0, 1)):
  142       white_name = (engine_name_0, engine_name_1)[white_idx]
  143       game = _play_game(
  144           engines=(engine_0, engine_1),
  145           engines_names=(engine_name_0, engine_name_1),
  146           white_name=white_name,
  147           # Copy as we modify the opening board in the function.
  148           initial_board=copy.deepcopy(opening_board),
  149       )
  150       games.append(game)
  151 
  152   return games
  153 
  154 
  155 def main(argv: Sequence[str]) -> None:
  156   if len(argv) > 1:
  157     raise app.UsageError('Too many command-line arguments.')
  158 
  159   # To ensure variability in the games we play, we use the openings from the
  160   # Encyclopedia of Chess Openings.
  161   openings_path = os.path.join(
  162       os.getcwd(),
  163       '../data/eco_openings.pgn',
  164   )
  165   opening_boards = list()
  166 
  167   with open(openings_path, 'r') as file:
  168     while (game := chess.pgn.read_game(file)) is not None:
  169       opening_boards.append(game.end().board())
  170 
  171   # We subsample the openings according to the desired number of games.
  172   rng = np.random.default_rng(seed=1)
  173   opening_indices = rng.choice(
  174       np.arange(len(opening_boards)),
  175       # Divide by two as we consider both sides per opening (white and black).
  176       size=_NUM_GAMES.value // 2,
  177       replace=False,
  178   )
  179   opening_boards = list(opening_boards[idx] for idx in opening_indices)
  180 
  181   engines = {
  182       agent: constants.ENGINE_BUILDERS[agent]()
  183       for agent in [
  184           '9M',
  185           '136M',
  186           '270M',
  187           'stockfish',
  188           'stockfish_all_moves',
  189           'leela_chess_zero_depth_1',
  190           'leela_chess_zero_policy_net',
  191           'leela_chess_zero_400_sims',
  192       ]
  193   }
  194 
  195   games = _run_tournament(engines=engines, opening_boards=opening_boards)
  196 
  197   games_path = os.path.join(os.getcwd(), '../data/tournament_games.pgn')
  198 
  199   print(f'Writing games to {games_path}')
  200   with open(games_path, 'w') as file:
  201     for game in games:
  202       file.write(str(game))
  203       file.write('\n\n')
  204 
  205 
  206 if __name__ == '__main__':
  207   app.run(main)

FILE source/chess/searchless_chess/src/train.py
    1 # Copyright 2025 DeepMind Technologies Limited
    2 #
    3 # Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0 (the "License");
    4 # you may not use this file except in compliance with the License.
    5 # You may obtain a copy of the License at
    6 #
    7 #    http://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0
    8 #
    9 # Unless required by applicable law or agreed to in writing, software
   10 # distributed under the License is distributed on an "AS IS" BASIS,
   11 # WITHOUT WARRANTIES OR CONDITIONS OF ANY KIND, either express or implied.
   12 # See the License for the specific language governing permissions and
   13 # limitations under the License.
   14 # ==============================================================================
   15 
   16 """An example training script."""
   17 
   18 from collections.abc import Sequence
   19 
   20 from absl import app
   21 from absl import flags
   22 
   23 from searchless_chess.src import config as config_lib
   24 from searchless_chess.src import data_loader
   25 from searchless_chess.src import metrics_evaluator
   26 from searchless_chess.src import tokenizer
   27 from searchless_chess.src import training
   28 from searchless_chess.src import transformer
   29 from searchless_chess.src import utils
   30 
   31 
   32 _POLICY = flags.DEFINE_enum(
   33     'policy',
   34     'action_value',
   35     config_lib.POLICY_TYPES,
   36     'The policy used to play moves with the model.',
   37 )
   38 
   39 
   40 def main(argv: Sequence[str]) -> None:
   41   if len(argv) > 1:
   42     raise app.UsageError('Too many command-line arguments.')
   43 
   44   policy: config_lib.PolicyType = _POLICY.value  # pytype: disable=annotation-type-mismatch
   45   num_return_buckets = 128
   46 
   47   match policy:
   48     case 'action_value':
   49       output_size = num_return_buckets
   50     case 'behavioral_cloning':
   51       output_size = utils.NUM_ACTIONS
   52     case 'state_value':
   53       output_size = num_return_buckets
   54 
   55   predictor_config = transformer.TransformerConfig(
   56       vocab_size=utils.NUM_ACTIONS,
   57       output_size=output_size,
   58       pos_encodings=transformer.PositionalEncodings.LEARNED,
   59       max_sequence_length=tokenizer.SEQUENCE_LENGTH + 2,
   60       num_heads=4,
   61       num_layers=4,
   62       embedding_dim=64,
   63       apply_post_ln=True,
   64       apply_qk_layernorm=False,
   65       use_causal_mask=False,
   66   )
   67   train_config = config_lib.TrainConfig(
   68       learning_rate=1e-4,
   69       data=config_lib.DataConfig(
   70           batch_size=256,
   71           shuffle=True,
   72           worker_count=0,  # 0 disables multiprocessing.
   73           num_return_buckets=num_return_buckets,
   74           policy=policy,
   75           split='train',
   76       ),
   77       log_frequency=1,
   78       num_steps=20,
   79       ckpt_frequency=5,
   80       save_frequency=10,
   81   )
   82   eval_config = config_lib.EvalConfig(
   83       data=config_lib.DataConfig(
   84           batch_size=1,
   85           shuffle=False,
   86           worker_count=0,  # 0 disables multiprocessing.
   87           num_return_buckets=num_return_buckets,
   88           policy=None,  # pytype: disable=wrong-arg-types
   89           split='test',
   90       ),
   91       use_ema_params=True,
   92       policy=policy,
   93       batch_size=32,
   94       num_return_buckets=num_return_buckets,
   95       num_eval_data=64,
   96   )
   97 
   98   params = training.train(
   99       train_config=train_config,
  100       predictor_config=predictor_config,
  101       build_data_loader=data_loader.build_data_loader,
  102   )
  103 
  104   predictor = transformer.build_transformer_predictor(predictor_config)
  105   evaluator = metrics_evaluator.build_evaluator(predictor, eval_config)
  106   print(evaluator.step(params=params, step=train_config.num_steps))
  107 
  108 
  109 if __name__ == '__main__':
  110   app.run(main)

FILE source/chess/searchless_chess/src/training.py
    1 # Copyright 2025 DeepMind Technologies Limited
    2 #
    3 # Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0 (the "License");
    4 # you may not use this file except in compliance with the License.
    5 # You may obtain a copy of the License at
    6 #
    7 #    http://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0
    8 #
    9 # Unless required by applicable law or agreed to in writing, software
   10 # distributed under the License is distributed on an "AS IS" BASIS,
   11 # WITHOUT WARRANTIES OR CONDITIONS OF ANY KIND, either express or implied.
   12 # See the License for the specific language governing permissions and
   13 # limitations under the License.
   14 # ==============================================================================
   15 
   16 """Implements the training loop that performs parameter updates."""
   17 
   18 import copy
   19 import functools
   20 import os
   21 
   22 from absl import logging
   23 import haiku as hk
   24 import jax
   25 from jax.experimental import mesh_utils
   26 import jax.random as jrandom
   27 import numpy as np
   28 import optax
   29 
   30 from searchless_chess.src import config as config_lib
   31 from searchless_chess.src import constants
   32 from searchless_chess.src import training_utils
   33 from searchless_chess.src import transformer
   34 
   35 
   36 def train(
   37     train_config: config_lib.TrainConfig,
   38     predictor_config: transformer.TransformerConfig,
   39     build_data_loader: constants.DataLoaderBuilder,
   40 ) -> hk.Params:
   41   """Trains a predictor and returns the trained parameters."""
   42   logging.info(
   43       '[Process %d]: Using %d processes with %d local devices each.',
   44       jax.process_index(),
   45       jax.process_count(),
   46       jax.local_device_count(),
   47   )
   48 
   49   # Build the predictor and the data loader.
   50   predictor = transformer.build_transformer_predictor(predictor_config)
   51   # For multi-host topologies, we want every process to train on different data,
   52   # so we need to modify the seed accordingly.
   53   train_config.data.seed += jax.process_index()
   54   data_iter = build_data_loader(config=train_config.data).__iter__()
   55 
   56   # Initialize the predictor parameters.
   57   logging.info('Initializing the predictor parameters.')
   58   params = predictor.initial_params(
   59       rng=jrandom.PRNGKey(predictor_config.seed),
   60       targets=np.zeros((1, 1), dtype=np.uint32),
   61   )
   62 
   63   params_ema = copy.deepcopy(params)
   64 
   65   # Create the optimizer and initialize its state.
   66   optimizer = optax.chain(
   67       optax.clip_by_global_norm(train_config.max_grad_norm),
   68       optax.adam(train_config.learning_rate),
   69   )
   70   opt_state = optimizer.init(params)
   71 
   72   # Create the gradient and update functions.
   73   loss_fn = training_utils.make_loss_fn(predictor=predictor)
   74   grad_fn = jax.value_and_grad(loss_fn)
   75   update_fn = functools.partial(
   76       training_utils.update_parameters,
   77       grad_fn=grad_fn,
   78       optimizer=optimizer,
   79   )
   80 
   81   # Create the sharding and replicate the parameters and the optimizer state.
   82   # The sharding is flat, i.e., all devices are used in parallel (disregarding
   83   # where they are on the grid).
   84   devices = mesh_utils.create_device_mesh((jax.device_count(),))
   85   sharding = jax.sharding.PositionalSharding(devices)
   86   sharding = sharding.reshape((jax.device_count(), 1))
   87   params = training_utils.replicate(params, sharding)
   88   params_ema = training_utils.replicate(params_ema, sharding)
   89   opt_state = training_utils.replicate(opt_state, sharding)
   90 
   91   latest_step = 0
   92 
   93   # Initialize the checkpointer and restore any previous checkpoints.
   94   if train_config.ckpt_frequency is not None:
   95     logging.info('Initializing the checkpoint manager.')
   96     checkpoint_dir = os.path.join(
   97         os.getcwd(),
   98         f'../checkpoints/local/{train_config.data.policy}',
   99     )
  100     checkpoint_manager = training_utils.get_checkpoint_manager(
  101         ckpt_frequency=train_config.ckpt_frequency,
  102         max_to_keep=train_config.ckpt_max_to_keep,
  103         save_frequency=train_config.save_frequency,
  104         checkpoint_dir=checkpoint_dir,
  105     )
  106 
  107     if checkpoint_manager.latest_step() is not None:
  108       latest_step = checkpoint_manager.latest_step()
  109       logging.info('Restoring checkpoint %d.', latest_step)
  110       params, params_ema, opt_state, data_iter = (
  111           training_utils.restore_checkpoint(
  112               checkpoint_manager=checkpoint_manager,
  113               step=latest_step,
  114               params=params,
  115               params_ema=params_ema,
  116               opt_state=opt_state,
  117               data_iter=data_iter,
  118               sharding=sharding,
  119           )
  120       )
  121 
  122   # Main training loop.
  123   for step in range(latest_step, train_config.num_steps + 1):
  124     if train_config.ckpt_frequency is not None:
  125       if step % train_config.ckpt_frequency == 0:
  126         logging.info('Checkpointing step %i.', step)
  127         checkpoint_manager.save(
  128             step=step,
  129             items=dict(
  130                 params=params,
  131                 params_ema=params_ema,
  132                 opt_state=opt_state,
  133                 data_iter=data_iter,
  134             ),
  135         )
  136 
  137     sequences, loss_mask = next(data_iter)
  138     sequences = jax.lax.with_sharding_constraint(sequences, sharding)
  139     loss_mask = jax.lax.with_sharding_constraint(loss_mask, sharding)
  140 
  141     params, params_ema, opt_state, loss, grad_norm_unclipped = update_fn(
  142         params=params,
  143         params_ema=params_ema,
  144         opt_state=opt_state,
  145         sequences=sequences,
  146         loss_mask=loss_mask,
  147     )
  148 
  149     if train_config.log_frequency is not None:
  150       if step % train_config.log_frequency == 0:
  151         logging.info(
  152             'step: %d | loss: %f | grad_norm_unclipped: %f',
  153             step,
  154             jax.device_get(loss),
  155             jax.device_get(grad_norm_unclipped),
  156         )
  157 
  158   if train_config.ckpt_frequency is not None:
  159     checkpoint_manager.close()
  160 
  161   return jax.device_get(params)

FILE source/chess/searchless_chess/src/training_utils.py
    1 # Copyright 2025 DeepMind Technologies Limited
    2 #
    3 # Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0 (the "License");
    4 # you may not use this file except in compliance with the License.
    5 # You may obtain a copy of the License at
    6 #
    7 #    http://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0
    8 #
    9 # Unless required by applicable law or agreed to in writing, software
   10 # distributed under the License is distributed on an "AS IS" BASIS,
   11 # WITHOUT WARRANTIES OR CONDITIONS OF ANY KIND, either express or implied.
   12 # See the License for the specific language governing permissions and
   13 # limitations under the License.
   14 # ==============================================================================
   15 
   16 """Utilities for the main training function, in train.py."""
   17 
   18 import functools
   19 import pathlib
   20 from typing import Any
   21 
   22 import chex
   23 from grain import python as pygrain
   24 import haiku as hk
   25 import jax
   26 from jax import numpy as jnp
   27 import optax
   28 import orbax.checkpoint as ocp
   29 
   30 from searchless_chess.src import constants
   31 
   32 
   33 def replicate(
   34     array_tree: chex.ArrayTree,
   35     sharding: jax.sharding.PositionalSharding,
   36 ) -> chex.ArrayDeviceTree:
   37   """Replicates the `array_tree` across all devices specified by `sharding`.
   38 
   39   In a multi-controller setting, we cannot simply use `jax.device_put` to
   40   replicate the `array_tree` since not all devices are addressable from every
   41   process.
   42 
   43   Args:
   44     array_tree: The `array_tree` to be replicated across devices.
   45     sharding: Describes how the array should be laid out across devices. Here,
   46       we just use it to specify that the `array_tree` should be replicated (not
   47       sharded).
   48 
   49   Returns:
   50     The distributed `array_tree`, replicated across all the devices.
   51   """
   52   return jax.tree.map(
   53       lambda array: jax.make_array_from_callback(
   54           array.shape, sharding.replicate(), lambda _: array
   55       ),
   56       array_tree,
   57   )
   58 
   59 
   60 def make_loss_fn(predictor: constants.Predictor) -> Any:
   61   """Returns the loss function for `update_parameters`.
   62 
   63   Args:
   64     predictor: The predictor to evaluate.
   65   """
   66 
   67   def loss_fn(
   68       params: hk.Params,
   69       sequences: constants.Sequences,
   70       mask: constants.LossMask,
   71   ) -> jnp.float32:
   72     """Returns the loss for the model and the last state.
   73 
   74     Args:
   75       params: The parameters of the model, usually a neural network.
   76       sequences: The input of sequences to evaluate. See neural_predictors.py.
   77       mask: Mask to apply to the losses. True means the loss will not be
   78         computed there.
   79     """
   80     conditionals = predictor.predict(params=params, targets=sequences, rng=None)
   81     true_conditionals = jnp.take_along_axis(
   82         conditionals, sequences[..., None], axis=-1
   83     )[..., 0]
   84     true_conditionals = jnp.where(mask, 0.0, true_conditionals)
   85     marginals = jnp.sum(true_conditionals, axis=1)
   86     # We need to clip to avoid a division by 0 below.
   87     seq_lengths = jnp.clip(jnp.sum(1 - mask, axis=1), a_min=1)
   88     return -jnp.mean(marginals / seq_lengths)
   89 
   90   return loss_fn
   91 
   92 
   93 def _update_ema(
   94     ema_value: jnp.float32,
   95     current_param_value: jnp.float32,
   96     ema_decay: float = 0.99,
   97 ) -> jnp.float32:
   98   # The below implementation is a more numerically stable version of:
   99   # ema_value = ema_decay * ema_value + (1 - ema_decay) * current_param_value.
  100   return ema_value - (1.0 - ema_decay) * (ema_value - current_param_value)
  101 
  102 
  103 @functools.partial(jax.jit, static_argnames=('grad_fn', 'optimizer'))
  104 def update_parameters(
  105     params: hk.Params,
  106     params_ema: hk.Params,
  107     opt_state: optax.OptState,
  108     sequences: constants.Sequences,
  109     loss_mask: constants.LossMask,
  110     grad_fn: Any,
  111     optimizer: optax.GradientTransformation,
  112 ) -> tuple[hk.Params, hk.Params, optax.OptState, jnp.float32, jnp.float32]:
  113   """Computes gradients and updates the parameters using the optimizer.
  114 
  115   Backpropagation is done on the whole sequence. The whole function is jitted.
  116 
  117   Args:
  118     params: The parameters of the model.
  119     params_ema: EMA of params used in evals.
  120     opt_state: The state of the optimizer.
  121     sequences: The sequences to evaluate.
  122     loss_mask: Mask to apply to the loss.
  123     grad_fn: A gradient function, which takes some parameters, a random seed,
  124       the data to compute the gradient on, and an initial state for the
  125       predictor. It returns the gradient of the parameters for this batch of
  126       data, and extra values.
  127     optimizer: An optimizer that computes parameter updates from the gradients.
  128 
  129   Returns:
  130     The updated parameters, ema of parameters, optimizer state, the loss and
  131     the gradient norm.
  132   """
  133   loss, grad = grad_fn(params, sequences, loss_mask)
  134   updates, new_opt_state = optimizer.update(grad, opt_state)
  135   new_params = optax.apply_updates(params, updates)
  136   grad_norm_unclipped = optax.global_norm(grad)
  137 
  138   new_params_ema = jax.tree.map(_update_ema, params_ema, new_params)
  139   return new_params, new_params_ema, new_opt_state, loss, grad_norm_unclipped
  140 
  141 
  142 def get_checkpoint_manager(
  143     ckpt_frequency: int,
  144     max_to_keep: int | None = None,
  145     save_frequency: int | None = None,
  146     checkpoint_dir: str | None = None,
  147 ) -> ocp.CheckpointManager:
  148   """Returns a `CheckpointManager`, which can save and restore checkpoints.
  149 
  150   Args:
  151     ckpt_frequency: The frequency at which checkpoints should be saved.
  152     max_to_keep: If provided, the maximum number of checkpoints to keep.
  153     save_frequency: The frequency at which checkpoints should be persisted.
  154     checkpoint_dir: The directory to save checkpoints to. If `None`, the default
  155       directory is retrieved.
  156 
  157   Raises:
  158     ValueError if save_frequency is set to a non-None value, and is not a
  159     multiple of ckpt_frequency.
  160   """
  161   if checkpoint_dir is None:
  162     checkpoint_dir = '/tmp/checkpoints'
  163 
  164   if save_frequency is not None and save_frequency % ckpt_frequency != 0:
  165     raise ValueError(
  166         '`save_frequency` must be a multiple of `ckpt_frequency`. Got'
  167         f' save_frequency={save_frequency} and ckpt_frequency={ckpt_frequency}.'
  168     )
  169   options = ocp.CheckpointManagerOptions(
  170       save_interval_steps=ckpt_frequency,
  171       max_to_keep=max_to_keep,
  172       keep_period=save_frequency,
  173   )
  174   checkpointers = dict(
  175       params=ocp.AsyncCheckpointer(ocp.StandardCheckpointHandler()),
  176       params_ema=ocp.AsyncCheckpointer(ocp.StandardCheckpointHandler()),
  177       opt_state=ocp.AsyncCheckpointer(ocp.StandardCheckpointHandler()),
  178       data_iter=ocp.Checkpointer(pygrain.PyGrainCheckpointHandler()),  # pytype: disable=wrong-arg-types
  179   )
  180   return ocp.CheckpointManager(
  181       directory=checkpoint_dir,
  182       checkpointers=checkpointers,
  183       options=options,
  184   )
  185 
  186 
  187 def restore_checkpoint(
  188     checkpoint_manager: ocp.CheckpointManager,
  189     step: int,
  190     params: hk.Params,
  191     params_ema: hk.Params,
  192     opt_state: optax.OptState,
  193     data_iter: pygrain.PyGrainDatasetIterator,
  194     sharding: jax.sharding.PositionalSharding,
  195 ) -> tuple[
  196     hk.Params, hk.Params, optax.OptState, pygrain.PyGrainDatasetIterator
  197 ]:
  198   """Returns the restored params and optimizer state from a checkpoint."""
  199 
  200   def make_abstract(array_tree: chex.ArrayTree) -> jax.ShapeDtypeStruct:
  201     abstract_array_tree = jax.eval_shape(lambda x: x, array_tree)
  202     return jax.tree_util.tree_map(
  203         lambda x: jax.ShapeDtypeStruct(
  204             shape=x.shape,
  205             dtype=x.dtype,
  206             sharding=sharding.replicate(),
  207         ),
  208         abstract_array_tree,
  209     )
  210 
  211   restored = checkpoint_manager.restore(
  212       step=step,
  213       items=dict(
  214           params=make_abstract(params),
  215           params_ema=make_abstract(params_ema),
  216           opt_state=make_abstract(opt_state),
  217           data_iter=data_iter,
  218       ),
  219   )
  220   return (
  221       restored['params'],
  222       restored['params_ema'],
  223       restored['opt_state'],
  224       restored['data_iter'],
  225   )
  226 
  227 
  228 def load_parameters(
  229     params: hk.Params,
  230     step: int = -1,
  231     use_ema_params: bool = False,
  232     checkpoint_dir: str | None = None,
  233 ) -> hk.Params:
  234   """Loads and returns parameters from CNS.
  235 
  236   Args:
  237     params: The parameters of the model.
  238     step: The step at which that checkpoint was saved. If -1, loads the largest
  239       available step.
  240     use_ema_params: Enables loading of ema-ed params
  241     checkpoint_dir: The directory to load parameters from. If `None`, the
  242       default directory is retrieved.
  243 
  244   Returns:
  245     The parameters saved at `step`.
  246 
  247   Raises:
  248     FileNotFoundError: If `step` is not saved for that run.
  249   """
  250   if checkpoint_dir is None:
  251     checkpoint_dir = '/tmp/checkpoints'
  252 
  253   # Set the step to the largest available step if required.
  254   checkpoint_steps = ocp.utils.checkpoint_steps(checkpoint_dir)
  255   if step == -1:
  256     step = checkpoint_steps[-1]
  257   elif step not in checkpoint_steps:
  258     raise FileNotFoundError(f'Checkpoint {step} not found in {checkpoint_dir}.')
  259 
  260   # Construct the restore_args to inform orbax about the desired sharding.
  261   restore_args = ocp.checkpoint_utils.construct_restore_args(params)
  262 
  263   # Restore the checkpoint and return the parameters.
  264   dir_name = 'params_ema' if use_ema_params else 'params'
  265   checkpoint_path = pathlib.Path(checkpoint_dir) / str(step) / dir_name
  266 
  267   checkpointer = ocp.Checkpointer(ocp.PyTreeCheckpointHandler())
  268   return checkpointer.restore(checkpoint_path, restore_args=restore_args)

   16 """Transformer model."""
   17 
   18 import dataclasses
   19 import enum
   20 import functools
   21 
   22 import haiku as hk
   23 import jax
   24 import jax.nn as jnn
   25 import jax.numpy as jnp
   26 import numpy as np
   27 
   28 from searchless_chess.src import constants
   29 
   30 
   31 class PositionalEncodings(enum.Enum):
   32   SINUSOID = enum.auto()
   33   LEARNED = enum.auto()
   34 
   35 
   36 @dataclasses.dataclass(kw_only=True)
   37 class TransformerConfig:
   38   """Hyperparameters used in the Transformer architectures."""
   39 
   40   # The random seed for parameter initialization.
   41   seed: int = 1
   42   # The input vocabulary size.
   43   vocab_size: int
   44   # The output size (by default equal to the vocabulary size).
   45   output_size: int | None = None
   46   # The dimension of the first embedding.
   47   embedding_dim: int = 64
   48   # The number of multi-head attention layers.
   49   num_layers: int = 4
   50   # The number of heads per layer.
   51   num_heads: int = 8
   52   # Whether to use a causal mask or not.
   53   use_causal_mask: bool = True
   54   # The parameter initialization scale for the embeddings.
   55   emb_init_scale: float = 0.02
   56   # Positional encodings to use.
   57   pos_encodings: PositionalEncodings = PositionalEncodings.SINUSOID
   58   # Maximum sequence length, useful for the LEARNED positional encodings.
   59   max_sequence_length: int | None = None
   60   # How much larger the hidden layer of the feedforward network should be
   61   # compared to the `embedding_dim`.
   62   widening_factor: int = 4
   63   # Whether to apply QK normalization trick in attention layer.
   64   apply_qk_layernorm: bool = False
   65   # Whether to apply post LN after attention + MLP blocks
   66   apply_post_ln: bool = True
   67 
   68   def __post_init__(self):
   69     if self.output_size is None:
   70       self.output_size = self.vocab_size
   71 
   72 
   73 class MultiHeadDotProductAttention(hk.Module):
   74   """Multi-head dot-product attention (Vaswani et al., 2017)."""
   75 
   76   def __init__(
   77       self,
   78       num_heads: int,
   79       num_hiddens_per_head: int,
   80       name: str | None = None,
   81       apply_qk_layernorm: bool = False,
   82   ) -> None:
   83     """Initializes the attention module.
   84 
   85     Args:
   86       num_heads: Number of heads to use.
   87       num_hiddens_per_head: Number of hidden neurons per head.
   88       name: Name of the module.
   89       apply_qk_layernorm: Applies layernorm to query and key matrices, this
   90         helps training stability.
   91     """
   92     super().__init__(name=name)
   93     self._num_heads = num_heads
   94     self._num_hiddens_per_head = num_hiddens_per_head
   95     self._apply_qk_layernorm = apply_qk_layernorm
   96 
   97   def __call__(
   98       self,
   99       inputs_q: jax.Array,
  100       inputs_kv: jax.Array,
  101       mask: jax.Array | None = None,
  102   ) -> jax.Array:
  103     """Returns the output of the multi-head attention."""
  104     batch_size, sequence_length, embedding_size = inputs_q.shape
  105 
  106     num_hiddens = self._num_hiddens_per_head * self._num_heads
  107     q = hk.Linear(num_hiddens, with_bias=False)(inputs_q)
  108     k = hk.Linear(num_hiddens, with_bias=False)(inputs_kv)
  109 
  110     if self._apply_qk_layernorm:
  111       q = layer_norm(q)
  112       k = layer_norm(k)
  113 
  114     v = hk.Linear(num_hiddens, with_bias=False)(inputs_kv)
  115     # The second (sequence) dimension is undefined since it can differ between
  116     # queries and keys/values when decoding. Also checking that the inputs have
  117     # the same batch size as the reshape below does not guarantee a failure if
  118     # they are different.
  119     new_shape = (batch_size, -1, self._num_heads, self._num_hiddens_per_head)
  120     q = jnp.reshape(q, new_shape)
  121     k = jnp.reshape(k, new_shape)
  122     v = jnp.reshape(v, new_shape)
  123 
  124     # Let b=batch_size, t=seq_len, h=num_heads, and d=num_hiddens_per_head.
  125     attention = jnp.einsum('bthd,bThd->bhtT', q, k)
  126     attention *= 1.0 / jnp.sqrt(self._num_hiddens_per_head)
  127 
  128     if mask is not None:
  129       attention = jnp.where(mask, attention, jnp.finfo(jnp.float32).min)
  130 
  131     normalized_attention = jnn.softmax(attention)
  132 
  133     output = jnp.einsum('bhtT,bThd->bthd', normalized_attention, v)
  134     output = jnp.reshape(output, (batch_size, sequence_length, num_hiddens))
  135     return hk.Linear(embedding_size, with_bias=False)(output)
  136 
  137 
  138 def sinusoid_position_encoding(
  139     sequence_length: int,
  140     hidden_size: int,
  141     max_timescale: float = 1e4,
  142 ) -> np.ndarray:
  143   """Creates sinusoidal encodings from the original transformer paper.
  144 
  145   The returned values are, for all i < D/2:
  146     array[pos, i] = sin(pos / (max_timescale^(2*i / D)))
  147     array[pos, D/2 + i] = cos(pos / (max_timescale^(2*i / D)))
  148 
  149   Args:
  150     sequence_length: Sequence length.
  151     hidden_size: Dimension of the positional encoding vectors, D. Should be
  152       even.
  153     max_timescale: Maximum timescale for the frequency.
  154 
  155   Returns:
  156     An array of shape [L, D] if `add_negative` or `keep_positive_side` is
  157     `False`, else [2 * L, D].
  158   """
  159   freqs = np.arange(0, hidden_size + 1, 2)
  160   inv_freq = max_timescale ** (-freqs / hidden_size)
  161 
  162   pos_seq = np.arange(start=0, stop=sequence_length)
  163 
  164   sinusoid_inp = np.einsum('i,j->ij', pos_seq, inv_freq)
  165   embeddings = np.concatenate(
  166       [np.sin(sinusoid_inp), np.cos(sinusoid_inp)], axis=-1
  167   )
  168   return embeddings[:, :hidden_size]
  169 
  170 
  171 def embed_sequences(
  172     sequences: jax.Array,
  173     config: TransformerConfig,
  174 ) -> jax.Array:
  175   """Returns embeddings for sequences of tokens."""
  176   embs_init = hk.initializers.TruncatedNormal(stddev=config.emb_init_scale)
  177   embeddings_layer = hk.Embed(
  178       vocab_size=config.vocab_size,
  179       embed_dim=config.embedding_dim,
  180       lookup_style=hk.EmbedLookupStyle.ARRAY_INDEX,
  181       w_init=embs_init,
  182   )
  183   embeddings = embeddings_layer(sequences)
  184   embeddings *= jnp.sqrt(config.embedding_dim)
  185 
  186   _, sequence_length, embedding_size = embeddings.shape
  187   match config.pos_encodings:
  188     case PositionalEncodings.SINUSOID:
  189       pos_encodings = sinusoid_position_encoding(
  190           sequence_length=sequence_length,
  191           hidden_size=embedding_size,
  192       )
  193     case PositionalEncodings.LEARNED:
  194       assert sequence_length <= config.max_sequence_length
  195       positions = jnp.arange(sequence_length)
  196       pos_encodings = hk.Embed(
  197           vocab_size=config.max_sequence_length,
  198           embed_dim=embedding_size,
  199       )(positions)
  200   return embeddings + pos_encodings
  201 
  202 
  203 def layer_norm(x: jax.Array) -> jax.Array:
  204   """Helper function for layer norm."""
  205   return hk.LayerNorm(axis=-1, create_scale=True, create_offset=True)(x)
  206 
  207 
  208 def shift_right(sequences: jax.Array) -> jax.Array:
  209   """Right-shift the one-hot encoded input by padding on the temporal axis."""
  210   bos_array = jnp.zeros((sequences.shape[0], 1), dtype=jnp.uint8)
  211   padded_sequences = jnp.concatenate([bos_array, sequences], axis=1)
  212   return padded_sequences[:, :-1]
  213 
  214 
  215 def _mlp_block(inputs: jax.Array, config: TransformerConfig) -> jax.Array:
  216   """Gated MLP block for the Transformer."""
  217   ffn_dim = config.embedding_dim * config.widening_factor
  218   split_1 = hk.Linear(ffn_dim, with_bias=False)(inputs)
  219   split_2 = hk.Linear(ffn_dim, with_bias=False)(inputs)
  220   gate_output = jnn.silu(split_1) * split_2
  221   return hk.Linear(config.embedding_dim, with_bias=False)(gate_output)
  222 
  223 
  224 def _attention_block(inputs: jax.Array, config: TransformerConfig) -> jax.Array:
  225   """Attention block for the Transformer."""
  226   batch_size, sequence_length = inputs.shape[:2]
  227   if config.use_causal_mask:
  228     causal_mask = np.tril(
  229         np.ones((batch_size, 1, sequence_length, sequence_length))
  230     )
  231   else:
  232     causal_mask = None
  233   block = MultiHeadDotProductAttention(
  234       num_heads=config.num_heads,
  235       num_hiddens_per_head=config.embedding_dim // config.num_heads,
  236       apply_qk_layernorm=config.apply_qk_layernorm,
  237   )
  238   return block(inputs_q=inputs, inputs_kv=inputs, mask=causal_mask)
  239 
  240 
  241 def transformer_decoder(
  242     targets: jax.Array,
  243     config: TransformerConfig,
  244 ) -> jax.Array:
  245   """Returns the transformer decoder output, shape [B, T, V].
  246 
  247   Follows the LLaMa architecture:
  248   https://github.com/facebookresearch/llama/blob/main/llama/model.py
  249   Main changes to the original Transformer decoder:
  250   - Using gating in the MLP block, with SwiGLU activation function.
  251   - Using normalization before the attention and MLP blocks.
  252 
  253   Args:
  254     targets: The integer target values, shape [B, T].
  255     config: The config to use for the transformer.
  256   """
  257   # Right shift the targets to get the inputs (the first token is now a 0).
  258   inputs = shift_right(targets)
  259 
  260   # Embeds the inputs and adds positional encodings.
  261   embeddings = embed_sequences(inputs, config)
  262 
  263   h = embeddings
  264   for _ in range(config.num_layers):
  265     attention_input = layer_norm(h)
  266     attention = _attention_block(attention_input, config)
  267     h += attention
  268 
  269     mlp_input = layer_norm(h)
  270     mlp_output = _mlp_block(mlp_input, config)
  271     h += mlp_output
  272 
  273   if config.apply_post_ln:
  274     h = layer_norm(h)
  275   logits = hk.Linear(config.output_size)(h)
  276   return jnn.log_softmax(logits, axis=-1)
  277 
  278 
  279 def build_transformer_predictor(
  280     config: TransformerConfig,
  281 ) -> constants.Predictor:
  282   """Returns a transformer predictor."""
  283   model = hk.transform(functools.partial(transformer_decoder, config=config))
  284   return constants.Predictor(initial_params=model.init, predict=model.apply)
